Whenever we're up in Santa Barbara our favorite restaurant for dinner is La Arcada Bistro.  Every dish we've tried has been absolutely delicious and is very reasonably priced too.  This restaurant is a 5 minute walk across the street and on the same side as the Granada Theater.
The staff takes great care in their presentation of the food and is eager to please their customers.  They also have an amazing bar and an ambient vibe too. We'll definitely be back!

We had our women's lunch here in February, and it was a huge success. Pleasing 13 women is no easy task, but the food was great and service perfect. The crowning glory was having the excellent piano accompaniment by Ann Leatherman. We'll be back!

Tristan was a doll, however whomever was bartending the evening we went, made us two watery gin and sodas. We asked for two new cocktails. When the waiter brought our tab, he apologized and said the bartender would not take the first two drink mistakes off. This seemed like bad customer service. We will not return.
This place is flat out awful.  Our waitress was just short of being an idiot and half the items on the menu were not available.  I heard they are going out of business, not surprised.

Fantastic food, great Guinness on tap! My girlfriends monitor was fantastic, this place is family owned and operated, and they are the greatest people, so nice and friendly, one of the best places in Santa Barbara! Definitely a must come!

What a great time!  We went two nights in a row for the $3 margaritas at Happy Hour...Ricky knows how to make them just right!  We met the owner, Willie and his wife and daughters on the second night.  Wonderful people!  On Fridays and Sundays you are treated to live Irish Folk music from Willie and his daughters...great music, great voices!  Only ate and drank off the Happy Hour menu but everything looks and sounds great on the menu.  Definitely will be back to visit Santa Barbara just to hang at this great restaurant again!  Thanks for everything!

Barbara M.
Back to Life Massage & Bodywork
www.backtolifemassagesd.com

We just went in to find a coffee but found a delightful restaurant. We had already eaten which was a shame because every plate we saw looked delicious. The bartenders were copmletely amiable and even the owner passed by and said hello.

My husband ordered an expresso and it came with a brushchetta, which complemented it greatly. Since I coudln't resist I had an ice cream brownie which totally hit the spot!

Well this was the only place open for New Year's Day which is the one star. On another note, my boyfriend's coffee was burnt, my French toast was horrible and to top it off, there was a piece of hair in my food which caused me to lose my appetite. They didn't bother compensating in any way. I'll be sticking with Jeannine's and State & Fig which I am so fond of. As I'm writing this.. I just heard my boyfriend comment, "that's probably the worse breakfast I've had in Santa Barbara." (referring to La Arcada.) No we will not be returning or recommending. Btw this is my first bad review on Yelp.

We were lured in off the sidewalk while looking at the menu. It was about 1:15 or so on a Thursday and not that busy.  We ordered a half sandwich and soup and waited over 45 minutes!!  Service is bad and incredibly SLOW. Food was fair.  We'll avoid this place in the future.

Very disappointed in our lunch here.

The location is great, the food was good, service was awful.

We were seated outside right away, but it took more than 5 minutes for our server to come over. (I think it was at least 10 but since I wasn't timing it I don't want to possibly exaggerate.) It was long enough for us to decide on what we were eating and read enough Yelp reviews that we started to consider leaving. (Should have checked Yelp before, like I usually do!)

The waitress came over apologizing. We ordered a soy mocha, a grilled chicken sandwich and the crab quesadilla.

The mocha came out and it tasted like chocolate flavored water. Really gross. I wanted to trade it in for an Iced Tea. We kept looking for our server and she was nowhere to be found. There were only a few tables and it was right during the lunch hour, which should have been our clue that this was a place to avoid. There were employees everywhere but not our server. I finally asked another employee if she could send our server over.

And we waited some more. We were actually deciding to leave when our food came out. So we started eating. My grilled chicken sandwich was good, the fries were good but greasy. My husband thought his crab quesadilla tasted like tuna.

We were almost done with our food when our server finally decided to grace us with her presence. I told her to please take off the barely touched mocha and to just bring the check, which she did.

There's no reason the service should have been that bad, they were not understaffed. There is a reason they were so empty during the Friday lunch hour, and management should take note.

We will not be coming back, there are too many good restaurants in the area to put up with that!

This restaurant was a lovely stop for our holiday in Santa Barbara. The staff and owner are warm and inviting. Each of the three dishes served to our guests were attractive, tasty and prepared exquisitely. I have dined here before, for a late breakfast, and was not disappointed in my return visit. I highly recommend this restaurant for any occasion, and predict it will become a "special" occasion because of the quality experience. J Miller Henderson, NV

I wish one of my favorite breakfast spots in SB had been open today. Being that it is New Years, I had to settle on trying out La Arcada Bistro for the first time. Unfortunately, this turned out to be a mistake. My girlfriend and I are not hard to please by any means, but this place just did all they could to dissatisfy us. 

I would not recommend this spot to anyone. And, I will not return. There are just too many great places in Santa Barbara. Read on to hear how my experience went, if you are interested. 

First off, when I try a new place, I definitely go into it with an open mind, but there are a few things I expect from any restaurant as basic give-ins. My philosophy is simple. I go by the three strike rule. Service, food quality, over-all feeling. If the place gets three strikes, then that is it. I mean, I get that there are times when you have an "off" experience, but if the place strikes out, then there is something wrong at the core of the business. (In my opinion.)

La Arcada Bistro struck out. The service was poor (one example- I had to ask three different people over a 10 minute period of time for more [over-priced, barely warm, poor quality] coffee. This is a basic part of the service one pays for when going out to eat, and an easy one at that. If the server is trying hard, might be busy, the place could be understaffed, and I get that. However, this was not the case here. It came down to laziness, lack of attentiveness, and just plain disregard for a basic skill. Yes- basic. I have served in many atmospheres in the restaurant industry. I speak from experience. Refilling beverages is simple, and any service-oriented business should be proficient at the easy basic things.) Strike two was the poor quality of food, especially related to the prices. Breakfast is one of the easiest meals to prepare. If you are charging $10 for pancakes, they should be special in some way. I got two small pancakes that had less flavor than the cardboard that the box of mix they undoubtedly used came in. Strike three, overall feeling, came when my girlfriend found some hair in her lack-luster french toast breakfast. I asked the server if this was typical of their food, and when she assured me it wasn't I told her that my girlfriend had lost her appetite. The server offered no apologies and did not attempt to rectify the situation. This as I am sure you all know, is a major service blunder. Not only did the server reflect poorly on her own skills, but more importantly, the business itself. Needless to say, I will not recommend this place to anyone, and will on the contrary steer anyone who asks away from this business. I am a very reasonable consumer, but three strikes and I am done. I won't be surprised if La Arcada Bistro is out of business before the Spring. 

I am a solution oriented person, so if you are looking for a good place to have breakfast and find yourself near this one, there are several right there that are far better: The Andersen, Jeannine's, and State & Fig are three places in La Arcada that blow the "Bistro" out of the water. Do yourself a favor and try one of them instead.

Outstanding. 

Food is good, price is fair, and the craic is the best. 

I highly recommend!

If there is ever one day that everybody needs to BE ON, it's this day...

It was New Year's Eve before our symphony and we had to find a place to eat. We waited longer then we should have and ended up here because we just kept walking toward The Granada Theater. 

They had outside seating available and a NYE prefix menu that looked promising. 

They had lobster tail or prime rib so we were going to get both and share... We were seated and found out that they ran out of lobster tail... No big deal, we just both ordered the prime rib prefix dinner. We told them we had to leave by 8 and let them know that we only had 45 minutes to dine.

They brought our wines first, and they poured me the wrong one. We informed him and about 15 minutes later he brought out the right one. They weren't even busy inside. It was a laid back older crowd that looked like they wanted to be there all night, at least until 9pm then probably go home and sleep.

Then when they brought the correct drink there still was no soup or salad that we had ordered. We waited patiently. There was another couple that was frustrated and had to go inside to get WAITED on so we had to do the same thing. Once we explained the situation AGAIN they promptly brought out the Prime Rib first. Which was Well Done and when we ordered it they asked how we wanted it. We, of course, said medium rare. 

When I asked the wine server why these were well done and told him that we told the waiter we ordered them medium rare he told me,  "Oh, He's Sick."

Then came the salad and the soup. The lady that dropped it off even told us, "See, if you come inside and get us then we get you what you need."

The point is we shouldn't have to come inside and get you? How hard would it have been to bring a small dinner salad then 5-10 minutes later the soup. It was all backwards and all at once. They even brought me the wrong soup.

Then we had dessert and downed the Champagne and we were on our way. 

The food was forgettable and the service was not... In the worst kind of way.

This was a fantastic NYE that we had thought out the day, and unfortunately instead of me remembering our dinner as awesome. It will forever be remembered as less then stellar. Shame on the management for being so lax on the servers and shame on the serves for leaving us out in the cold on such an important day. 

This place owns us big time but I doubt we will ever be reciprocated.

1-1-13
Walking down State St. on New years Eve with out of town guests and this was one of the few restaurants open. Decided to take a chance on their special: $36 for wine, soup, salad, lobster or prime rib, triffle, and champagne. 

Pro:  Lobster was plentiful and good, soup was tasty
Con: - House wine not so great. Couldn't tell the merlot from the cab and neither was 
           good.
         - Soup portion too small 
         - Prime rib was overdone/tough. Both owner and waiter explained that "it's 
           difficult to get varying degrees of doneness within a roast"
         - triffle dessert was nothing more than fruit cocktail and jello with a smattering of
           vanilla pudding

The owner and his daughter did sing some lovely Irish ballads and he makes a point of visiting each table....he's very personable.

This place feels like family took me in and wants only the best for me. Trini, the owner is obviously a movie star and her main assistant/ waiter/ procurer Joe is AMAAAZING. Joe is the epitome of a service oriented employee. He takes care of my bratty mother like the royalty she is. 
We love this place, the service, the delicious food, and the love! 
Thank you! Thank you! Thank you!
Cary and Caryna

The worst place I had ever had eaten!!! The service is a lousy, the food mediocre at best.
The restaurant is presented in a very nice setting, outdoor sitting, clean and beautiful menus. We were seated and later we were asked if we were ready to order, placed our order, waiter never wrote anything down, ten minutes later another waiter came to ask for the order again because the first waiter forgot what we had ordered. After that everything went downhill. After that it took 25 minutes to get our order, when the order arrived I told the waiter that we never got our salad and she apologized and asked if we still wanted the salad. Of course my respond was, Yes!  She leaves and we expect a salad within five minutes. I finish my food and the salad never arrived. At one point I saw a guy rushing out the restaurant and at the same time that we were leaving the restaurant I see the guy coming back with a couple lettuce from the supermarket. Will I ever come back to this place, Nope!. Will I recommend this place, Nope.

I'm giving 5 star for the excellent service! The food was good, hubby thought his seafood linguine was Excellent! My dish was average, but Willie Quinn the owner was absolutely adorable, hospitable and made you feel like family! We will always pop in to say hello when in town!

This place is one of Santa Barbara's treasures. The people complaining about slow service don't get it. The restaurant was open on New Year's Day, when most other places weren't, so it may have taken a little longer to get your food. Big deal! Enjoy the atmosphere and the European ambiance. The owners are wonderful, very interesting people, the food is excellent, the Irish entertainment is wonderful and unique, and the ambiance is relaxing and non-hurried. That's what Santa Barbara is about. If you're in a hurry, try McDonalds. If you want a fun and interesting experience, and good food, this is a great spot.

We went to la arcada bistro for lunch & sadly, we will probably never go back.

The services started out ok, but quickly went downhill when the server was writing our order down & quickly forgot what my husband ordered. She said she spaced & asked again, I thought she recovered well, admitting she spaced & apologized, I was impressed that during her spacing out, she remembered he did not want tomatoes. Sadly when he got his order, she brought him his "tri tip" sandwich which had tomatoes, remember, he specified twice that he really did not want tomatoes. He put them to the side & she never said a word. Can't blame her.

We waited far too long for our credit card to be taken & the waitress returned it without a pen. Apparently today was not her day.

If you're still reading & do decide to go here, do not order the $6 Irish soda bread. It's a few sad pieces of dry bread. La arcada salad is pretty & not too bad, not sure it's worth $16.
I had the crab cake Benedict it was lovely. So was the waffle. The place is beautiful. Great find

We have often passed this restaurant on visits to a nearby art gallery and decided to stop for dinner.  It was a great decision.  The food was fabulous, service was exceptional and they had happy hour drink and hors d'oeuvre specials that were great.  We will definitely go back.  The shepherd's pie was amazing, and the spinach lentil soup was equally tasty and piping hot, just the way I like it.  I highly recommend the guacamole too.

This place was great. The outdoor seating was wonderful and the sangria was some of the best we've ever tasted. Unfortunately, the sangria wasn't included in happy hour, which was disappointing. But it was so delicious!!! We didn't try the food so we can't vouch for that, but I'd highly recommend this spot to sit outside and enjoy a cocktail (and try the food, too!)

We started out intending to go to Andersen's Danish Bakery & Restaurant next door on Sunday morning, but it was busy, and the noise and bustle from the happy white people sort of turned me off. We ducked into La Arcada Bistro, and boy are we glad we did. 
They have live music, including Irish music, though none was playing when we were there. They have a great bar selection, from what I could tell. But we came for the Sunday brunch, and it was exactly the right tone to preface our afternoon at the Art Museum a few doors up. The wait staff was attentive but not intrusive. The French Dip was excellent. Having been a restaurant manager 36 years ago of an establishment which had it's French Dip Roast Beef Sandwich as it's drawing card, I feel I am qualified to say, that this was a very good version.

Wow!!!

This place rocks the world!!!

My wife, father-in-law, mother-in-law and I took a little day trip to Santa Barbara and just stumbled upon this place after sitting in 3 Hours of traffic!!!!  We walked into the first place we came across and what a great discovery...  

This place has everything anyone would want in a restaurant.  Everything we ordered was amazing!!!

My inlaws ordered the French Dip, I had an amazing quesadilla and my wife had shrimp pasta.  We eat out a lot and this meal was so good we came back that same night and had amazing lobster dinner.  Another great decision!!!

I love most things but my inlaws can be a little harder to please but we all would come back, this place was just a great experience food, atmosphere and people.  I felt like I was eating at a family members home..

If you come to Santa Barbara and don't stop by this place for a meal you're really missing out!

Make sure you say hi to Joe the chief and Aoife the waitress!!!  They rule the world as far as I am concerned!!!!
The smell of sandwiches drew me and my friends in but the taste of their strawberries with cream and French toast was the best I've ever had. My go to breakfast place now!

Had lunch here last weekend with a friend who was visiting from out of town. She and I started off by ordering tangerine mimosas, only to be told that they were out of tangerine. Not that big of a deal, but still...I ordered the crab quesadilla and after a very long wait, it came out stone cold. The shredded cheese was not melted at all and the crab was cold as if it came straight from the fridge. Tortilla was barely toasted.  I sent it back.  My friend had the crab melt sandwich and the crab in that was fishy but the fries were good.  Hubby had the chicken fettuccine alfredo and he liked it a lot.  We all waited way too long for our food. And then trying to flag someone down to get the check took forever, and it took too long for them to process the credit card as well. The ambiance is really nice, great people watching along the State Street promenade, but the food and service don't make it worth it. Right down to the wobbly table at which we were seated. Servers watched us struggling to stabilize the table and did nothing to help.  Prices do not match the experience. Skip it.

I won't return here. Starting with the bad service as the waiter was not attentive. Next was the fail of the drink menu. Mojito said FRESH raspberries, lime, mint and soda WATER!  What I got twice as they tried a second time was RASPBERRY SYRUP that by no means was fresh but from a container. The soda water was sprite! TOTAL FAIL! Even on the second attempt of my asking for it without the raspberry syrup and with soda WATER they still put a sugary soda in. 

Food was nothing special either.

The food was average, and that's not a bad thing. It didn't completely blow my dress up though. It was solid and filled the need for a decent lunch meal.

I had the tuna melt and a side salad. The portion was good size and I left satisfied. The tuna itself wasn't too fishy, which can be a problem with this type of sandwich. The flavored iced tea was the bomb though.

Service was very friendly and welcoming. I would give them another try, but maybe for breakfast next time around.

I went there for a Sunday brunch.  The place was not overly crowded, but they were understaffed and the service was extremely slow. I ordered a mimosa and a classic Eggs Benedict. The Mimosa was slow to arrive and even though I was nursing it, it was gone long before the Eggs Benedict arrived. The key to a good Eggs Benedict is the hollandaise sauce and there was so little sauce on it that I can't even form an opinion. Basically it was poached eggs on a slice of ham and an English muffin. The eggs, ham, and english toast were fine...  To top it off, the drink menu did not list prices, but they were making a big deal out of the fact it was "Happy Hour," so while I should have asked ahead of time the $8.50 price on a tiny mimosa was a shock.

What made it frustrating was that I always had to work to get someone's attention after long waits. Even after I paid with my credit card, there was a long wait to get my card and bill back and then they didn't even bring a pen. I feel bad because obviously they are under staffed, but as a patron is was not a good experience.

Great family owned business, My Film group had a Film Festival Party there in February 2017, and wow what a great party we had. The drinks were flowing, the food was never ending and the music, Live DJ, disco lighting, red Carpet entrance and overall atmosphere was excellent. Will definitely be back for drinks, food and hopefully another party there soon....

Stopped by this place to relax with a glass of wine after touring State Street and its many shops. Trina the owner sat us and made us feel very welcome. Joe the chef came out and asked if we wanted anything and proceeded to convince us to try one of his special salads. It was delightful and complemented our wine beautifully. He stayed and chatted for a minute and described a shrimp soup he makes and said if we came tomorrow he would make it for us. We did. He did and it too was wonderful. We are from Portland Oregon so we are spoiled with good restaurants and La Arcada deserves your business!

Worst lunch I've ever had in my life... I got the crab sandwich and it came out on Wonder Bread basically and was flattened out and the taste was WEIRD.  The chicken soup was okay, but it's the only reason why this review gets one star.  My husband got a French Dip and couldn't bite through the meat so took it out of the sandwich and used a knife and treated it like a chewy steak.  Ton of other restaurants in Santa Barbara, don't waste your time, tasted buds, or money.

well located gem of Santa Barbara . Great margaritas !! Irish breakfast, good lunch options, small bites, delicious diner. Changing menus and specials. You will always find something tasty. Friendly service. and do not miss the happy hour also on weekends!

First time here, I would say it is pretty good. I order the Santa Barbara Scramble and it is decent. The waitresses are nice. I was hoping the entree would be a little cheaper from the taste of of the food but it could be the location. Overall, I am satisfied.

Been here a fews  times  for breakfast, and  lunch and dinner. Best place to eat very friendly staff. The food is beauuuuutiful ...!!! very good. The best drinks of had like Sangria, Mojitos n all the drinks. I truly recommend this place to eat at at any time.

I came here with family for breakfasts the really enjoyed the food and the atmosphere. The cafe hostess sat us outside at a table where you can see the downtown street and under the shade. I had ordered the eggs Benedict which was so amazingly delicious! The service was great and the waitress very attentive. Very nice place to eat!

After shopping around, we found this cute bistro with outdoor seating. The presentation was great and the music appropriate for the kind of food offered on the menu. 

But my god the food is mediocre. I ordered the crab melt with a side of the cheddar soup. The bread was toasted with what appeared to be Kraft cheese and in between the two slices were pieces of crab that tasted like too much mayo. On the corner of my plate were, I kid you not, RUFFLE POTATO CHIPS. Everything about my lunch screamed "store bought." I could have easily made this at home.
The cheddar soup was actually veggies and clams. I was confused and asked the waitress what it was and she said, "cheddar soup you ordered." Um. Okay. 

And yes this place is understaffed. There were 6 tables and one server. No wonder she messed up my soup order she's running around trying to please 6 tables.
Excellent service, prompt but no hovering.  The chowder was superb, the steak bites were delicious.  Very favorable first impression.

IF YOU USE YOUR CREDIT CARD, REVIEW YOUR FINAL STATEMENT, THEY FORGED AN ADDITIONAL AMOUNT FOR A TIP. 

My husband and I had lunch here a few days ago. The food was fine. Nothing to write home about nor complain about.  My issue is with the illegal charge that was added to my tip amount.  

I am one that monitors my account daily with my receipts.  I know this may seem trivial but the bottom line is it was an illegal act. I had to ask for my my copy of the receipt once I signed it.  

In checking my account this morning I noticed that a $3.00 amount was added to my tip amount through my online banking final amount.  I phoned my bank, we made a conference call to the restaurant and spoke with the owner Trini.  

I asked to stay on the line while she located her copy of the transaction.  She confirmed that "I" left a $9.00 tip. I stated that I have my original copy that "I " signed which was for a  "$6.00 tip" 

At the top of our conversation I asked if I could fax a copy of my receipt to her and she stated they did not have a fax, I asked if I could email it.  She said yes.  After she came back to the phone, she stated that she did not have an email address and wanted to mail me the money in a check. 

I stated that this was a credit card issue and I wanted her to issue a refund through her terminal.  She stated she was unable to do that. I said that I was also a merchant and know that it is possible and can be done instantly.  She then said I am not sure if I can do this today.  The time was 2:40pm.  All banking institutions are still open at this time! 

I told her at that point that I did not feel comfortable and i would exercise my right to file a dispute for the charges with my bank.  My banking institution witnessed the call and made notes and will file a formal complaint. 

Keep in mind in Santa Barbara, the majority of people do not look at price tags let alone follow up with the accurate charges. 

This was wrong!  There is no way that one can make the numeral 6 into a numeral 9 without forging it. 

So people pay cash or monitor your account when you dine here.

I have to be honest and say that I never really noticed this place before, even though its right on the State St. entrance to La Arcada. Its been so many iterations in the past that I just didn't notice when another popped up. Fortunately a friend of mine did notice and she booked our annual Holiday dinner there for a group of 9. Nothing about the look of the place will tell you this but the menu has a bit of an Irish bent to it featuring Irish Oatmeal and something called a "Traditional Irish Breakfast" (eggs, Irish Bacon, Sausages, Black and White Pudding, Tomatoes, Mushrooms & sweet Irish Soda Bread) on the breakfast front while offering Shepherds Pie on the dinner side. There is also a wide range of classic dishes form other cuisines ranging from shrimp scampi and chicken piccata to New York steak and a decent looking burger. Throw in a quesadilla and some nachos just to round of the international flair and flavor of the menu :-) We got an outdoor table which was quasi-indoor thanks to an awning,  clear plastic sheeting, and nice space heaters that kept us sheltered from the cold and a rare rainy night in town :-) There were a couple other large groups in that evening but we had a dedicated server and the manager/boss/owner also helped out with our group so service was fine, though one order got misplaced and arrived quite late but we were comped for it and everyone was fine with that. Food wise, I opted for the Shepherds Pie which I really enjoyed. It was nice to find something so totally different on a menu for a change. Others in the group went with the classics like the Piccata, Seafood Fettucine and Salmon.               Though I didn't get to taste anyone else's meals, plates were emptied and no complaints were lodged :-) The general consensus was these were solid takes on classic dishes. Good place to go to serve many palates and tastes and with most dishes under $20 the value is reasonable as well. Small but varied selection of local beers on tap. Didn't get to see the wine list as we brought our own, corkage was $15. Live music many nights, usually acoustic guitar with light vocals.

If you have ever strolled down State Street in Santa Barbara, then you are aware that it is the home of a plethora of both local and chain restaurants and cafes. It can be overwhelming to choose the "right" one for your eating/drinking/socializing needs. La Arcada is one of the many options to choose from. How does it stack up?

La Arcada is a cute bistro located on a corner real estate offering indoor and outdoor seating in an Irish meets Spanish- ambiance (which makes sense as the owner is Irish while his wife is Mexican). During the early afternoon, it is calm and inviting but apparently can get rowdy on weekends when there is live Irish music reverberating the air. Think: Irish bar meets cafe with rustic wood trim but stuccoed walls. 

Although La Arcada didn't have too many customers at the time of our patronage (between 2 and 3pm); I didn't feel quite that welcome. It isn't that the server and staff were rude per se; they just weren't that inviting. Not to mention: slow. Very, very slow. Despite this, we browsed the menu having not yet eaten lunch seeking some light fare. My boyfriend and I decided to share plates and went with the House Salad (Grilled chicken, fire-roasted red peppers, red onion, blue cheese, toasted pine nuts,red delicious apples and mixed greens tossed with balsamic vinaigrette-- $16.00) and the Irish Soda Bread (with Kerry Gold butter and Dubliner Cheese -- $6.00). Due to it being Happy Hour, we also shared a Bellini ($5.00). 

The key to La Arcada is presentation. The salad and bread arrived at the same time and had an elegant but approachable feel. The salad was absolutely delicious with just the right amount of vinaigrette, tender chicken, and veggies. Although it was enough for my boyfriend and I to share; I still think it was much overpriced though for the quantity. Not necessarily satisfying if you are very hungry. The Irish Soda bread was a good deal with plenty of bread and large slices of cheese. I found the bread to be a little dry (and I love Irish Soda bread so I've had it plenty of times). It wasn't awful but I wasn't blown away. The Bellini was a highlight though. It was tasty and strong which is great being that it was a happy hour price and sometimes restaurants water down drinks during those times. 

A minor note but still worth mentioning is that the bathroom is a single-stall meaning that you have to wait quite a long time if someone is inside. Plus, it is an awkward back of the house area next to run down soda machines. Not good if you really have to use the bathroom!

There honestly isn't much more to be said about La Arcada. The experience wasn't bad but also not memorable on the positive side; making it simply an okay medium-choice on State Street but not life-changing. If nothing else though, the outdoor seating is quaint with great views of State Street. I would say this is a hit or miss option in lovely Santa Barbara.
Super dog friendly,  also incredible home made soups. Delicious and pleasantly perfect food.  Healthy and delicious. Love this place.

I would give 2.5 stars, but in honor of my mom being so disappointed by her sandwich, I rounded down to 2 instead of up to 3...

We were here for lunch, and loved the fact that we could get outdoor seating right in the prime realty area of state street in SB, so that was a great start. Then they forgot my mom's iced tea about 4 times, and we just felt awkward having to reorder it each time. Their lunch menu isn't the cheapest in the world, but for a bistro on state street what do you expect? I got their crab melt sandwich which was overly greasy to me. I could feel the oil and cheese on my fingers way more than I wanted to, and this is coming from someone who absolutely loves cheese. It was just an okay sandwich. 

Then my mom got here french dip sandwich and when she opened it up, noticed that all of the meat had so much fat on it, she had to burn a ton of extra calories cutting away at all of the fat in her sandwich! Who wants to eat pure fat? No one pretty much. And for a sandwich of that price, that work should already be done for the consumer. Better yet, buy better quality meat without that extra fat in it! My uncle thought his salad was so so and their homemade soup was also nothing to scream home about either. Really we all just felt blah, and left wishing we had eaten somewhere else.
Must try their cowboy cookies, so yummy! The lady behind the counter was so friendly and goes above and beyond.

Wild Mushroom pizza is delicious. Somehow, Honor Market has created a decadent pizza that is also light and refreshing. The perfect satiating pizza for a hot summer night. Add a salad and ya gotta meal. 

ps the Americano is excellent also!
Oh my God I love this place! I can't wait to go back! Delicious food and pretty good coffee.

I heard about this pizza a while back and have been meaning to try it for sometime now. My friend and I came here on a sunny Saturday afternoon. We ordered the Blistered Tomato pizza and took it with us to the beach just down the road.

As we ate the pizza, all of the ingredients - the cheese, brocoli, tomatoes - melted together in every bite, creating a kind of harmony on your palate. But the real kicker was the sesame seed toppings drizzled on top of the cheese: what an unexpected delight. 

If I had to recommend a friend to a pizza place, it'd be this one.

The food delicious, the store quaint, the staff... a little stand offish. We are obsessed with this place and stop in every time we are in Summerland. The scones are a MUST. Get there in the morning so they are still fresh. Their everything cookies are a delicious enigma. I'm not sure what's in them but I freak out every time. Moist on the inside, crisp on the outside. 

Pizza is a must as well. Made fresh, best ingredients. I was so pleased. Which is what makes the staff attitude so disappointing! When I asked some questions (simple ones, like how many shots were in the coffee) they were very short with me (there are 2, by the way). I brushed it off as a bad day. But when I came in the next day, I encountered the same attitude! 

So go for the food, but don't expect the warmth or the "honor" you might expect!

Love this place!  Grab and go sandwiches are delicious!  All the cookies are delectable...not to mention great service from the staff, especially Katie!!  Will be back to try the pizza...check it out.  You won't be disappointed!
Not typically a fan of scones, but the raisin pecan scone here is next level.  The perfect companion to an almond milk latte. Nicely curated merch to browse through adds a nice touch.

Great place to pick up dinner or a snack. Have tried salads, sandwiches, pizza, cookies. All are wonderful. Would have given five stars but the prices are on the high side, especially if picking up for a group. Great food though.
Fabulous takeout pizza. Wine, beer, dessert and coffee. Honor Bar menu also available for take out. Hannah provided 1st class service. Cool stuff for sale too.

Get the scone, just get one! I almost got the chocolate chip cookie the other day, they are really good. It was morning aka breakfast time and I shamed myself into thinking I needed to fit in with the other breakfast eaters out there. I'm so glad my co-dependence kicked in at the best time. These scones are light and buttery with a generous amount of nuts and dusted with powdered sugar. If you don't like the scone then don't read any of my other reviews etc. I think the Honor Market won my scone business! Scone on peeps! ‍

An impressive compact, but jammed packed, market filled quality products. This sisters the Honor Bar right next door and offers a small to go menu. Pizza and desserts are amazing. Tried their house made granola  and loved it, will be taking a couple bags of those back home for sure. They have a small collection of beverages, wine, champagne, sparkling wine, and a small selection of home accent-giftware ranging from gorgeous picnic blankets, cutting boards to big coffee table books. I'll take one of each please!

Great place that has super high quality pizza at surprisingly reasonable prices. Honor Market delivers a unique twist on typical pizza flavors with a crunchy medium thin crust that's somewhere between Neapolitan cracker and San Francisco sourdough (ala Cheese Board and Arizmendi). I imagine every combination is good; we had the Wild Mushroom, Sweet Pepper and Spicy Kale. On our visit margherita pizza was the special (to make this a local family takeout it will have to be a regular item). The secret dipping sauce is herbaceous and slightly spicy from garlic and peppers -- a great twist on the ubiquitous side of ranch dressing so many take out places offer. At $15 for a 16" pie ($18 if you add sausage) there isn't a better deal in town by price. The quality ingredients are equal or better to anything in the 805 and while selection is limited the taste/flavor/preparation rivals the best pizzas anywhere.

Best pizza ever! I tried the mushroom and broccoli rabe and they were both incredible. I love how you can taste wine while waiting your food. They had a great selection too. Oh and the chocolate chip cookies are amazing.
This is the best scone I have had in CA( so far). If u are in the area, must drop by to give a try, trust me is worth of the drive.
Just had the summer corn pizza, nearly flawless. It also comes with a green dipping sauce that packs a little heat to balance the sweetness of the corn.
This place is amazing and brand new. We are so excited. Melanie was so sweet and helpful. The pizzas are worth it. Will be back many times. Thank you Honor Bar.

If you're familiar with the Houston's /Hillstone restaurant group, then you know they always pay attention to quality and detail. The Honor bar is no different. Very quality ingredients, service staff is  friendly, and amazing cocktails. The menu is slightly scaled down, but still has some great choices.  Very warm and friendly feel, I would highly recommend it if you're in the area.

The pizza at Honor Market is amazing! I always get the social pizza of the day-I have never been disappointed and the ingredients and combinations are super unique and flavorful.

I dream of this pizza and always stop when I'm coming home from SB airport and don't feel like cooking.

Amazing place and good food and cute home decor items!

The most amazing pizza I think I've ever had! Super fresh and unique and so so delicious! They even have wine while you wait!! The staff is so friendly and inviting! They also have the coolest stuff to browse through and buy!! The pizza is a must- have to try it!!
Delicious reasonably priced coffee! Friendly staff. An easy stop on the way through town. No seating.

Delicious scones and treats but the real find is ..... the pizza. I don't like pizza, I've never liked pizza until now. The freshly baked crust, the delicious herbs and fresh ingredients make this an entirely different pizza experience.  I devoured three sizable slices last night. There no grease, light cheese and immense flavor. I am craving it just from writing this review.   Enjoy.

Honor Market is an amazing little shop with food and home goods. It is highly curated and cool. The taste level is insane. So sophisticated. I got a great latte and some of the coolest smokey wine glasses I've ever seen. The food looked amazing. I must go back for the carrot cake I saw on display. Wow! Go here, eat, get a gift. It's the best!

Got a free pizza coupon in the mail and decided to give it a try....YUM! We got the three pepper with feta and pickled onions and it was absolutely delicious. Unique topping combos - Will definitely be returning to try the other pizzas. Thanks!

We were out for a walk on Coast Villiage Rd. and to our pleasant surprise The HM was open and loaded with goodies. Best pizza ever! The crust is Perfect.  The crispy kale topping started with a light crunch and than melted in our mouths.  The green dipping sauce will blow your minds! 

Competition over, best Pizza the 93108 has to offer. 

Charge up your Tesla's and Go Now!

This is the BEST pizza I have ever had, period.  In fact, it's better than pizza.  The combination of flavors and the unique variety makes this a favorite place to visit while in the Santa Barbara and Montecito area. Seriously, you need to try their pizza.

Fantastic, flavorful, fresh, savory, gourmet pizza  with pizazz ! 
Really sublime pizza here. 
Delectable treats and coffee available here  too. And fun little gifts, cool chocolate bars, local wine, etc...   But their pizza really gets me. Not too expensive, with inventive unique flavors that are crazy delicious, sesame crust,  and divine dipping sauces.  
I get so entranced with their  pizza, I often forget to hop over to the Honor bar!

Care to the customer gets no better than this.  Juliette was warm, friendly, and extremely helpful.  French dip (from Honor Bar menu $22) had plentiful, tender, and flavorful beef with a very good roll. Cowboy cookie, each bite exquisite.

Milk Bar Has "Crack Pie". Honor Bar Has "Crack Pizza"

I've been coming here for awhile and have always had a great experience with both the food and the staff.

Tonight since I was flying solo I finally got to order the corn, wild mushroom white pizza I've been wanting to try for ages.

To say it did not disappoint would be an understatement. I am obsessed with this pizza. Super easy ordering and pick up process, too.

Best pizza in the SB area hands down - nothing that compares to the Honor Market pizza.  Worth a drive if you live anywhere nearby and haven't tried it.  The crust is really crispy and they run the cheese over the edge of the crust, which is a really nice touch!  My wife and I have been a number of times for different pizzas and you can't go wrong.  That said, our favorites are the three pepper, the autumn (it had bacon, squash and chard and the combination was amazing), the corn/poblano, the greek and the chicken meatball.  And the store has a bunch of cool retail items as well so you can look around if you have a wait.  Get a cookie to take home too -- you won't be sorry.

Get the scone, just get one! I almost got the chocolate chip cookie the other day, they are really good. It was morning aka breakfast time and I shamed myself into thinking I needed to fit in with the other breakfast eaters out there. I'm so glad my co-dependence kicked in at the best time. These scones are light and buttery with a generous amount of nuts and dusted with powdered sugar. If you don't like the scone then don't read any of my other reviews etc. I think the Honor Market won my scone business! Scone on peeps ‍

Never was a fan of the crust but it was convenient with decent pizza. Now prices have shot way up and the pizza topping options aren't very inspiring. I asked for jalapenos on my chicken meatball pizza and the reply was "we don't do that here". "We don't allow add ons even if you pay for it." Montecito has a lot of options I'm going elsewhere. That being said I've had nothing but great food and accommodating service next door at the Honor Bar Restaurant.

The Honor Market is THE place to go for interesting pizzas in Montecito/ Santa Barbara. Several reviews complain about price and portions but it's all kind of a moot point as far as i am concerned because the stuff here is so good, so well prepared, the service friendly and courteous.
Scones are available here.  A real Scone should melt in your mouth and not crack your teeth when you bite into it. There is a real difference between an American Scone and a British one. The British version has less butter and less sugar because the Brits butter and add preserves to theirs.
So where does the HM Scone come in? Definitely an American Scone. Delicious, buttery and as American as Meat Loaf. I love them.
The HM also makes dynamite Espresso drinks guaranteed to keep you going towards your work rather than away from it. i don't see it all the time but if they have a carrot cake: buy a slice, buy a whole one and a huge cup of coffee, sit on the curb and dig into it with a big fork.
They also have all sorts of doodads, books, kitchen implements: all of good quality. i know because i bought a Mandolin here and it works much better than my previous model.
Drop in, take home a Kale or Corn Pizza, buy a good bottle of red and watch  a good movie like "Goodfellas" or "Howards's End."

Some of the best pizza in town but they've raised the prices on their entire menu twice since opening well under a year ago, resulting in pizzas that are now over 7 dollars more than their initial price. Disappointing from a company with traditionally strong customer service.

This is a great addition to Montecito for a pre-made sandwich of the day, carrot cake or latte (the raisin pecan scones in particular are pure nirvana). The pizzas are quite good but I wish they had a more standard option (like ham & mushrooms) since my husband is a traditionalist so broccolini or corn as a topping is not going to cut it (and they don't allow substitutions).

Decent. Pizza was more fancy then good. I expected chicken meatballs with broccolini and actually it has been changed to kale. Was not the type of pizza most kids would eat as far as it's close relation to conventional pie

One of the things that gave me the heebie geebies about the HONOR BAR was that they did not have Pizza nor desserts. Well now, all you have to do is walk 10 feet and you can have both from the same people that brought you the Honor Bar, Houston's, etc.
The most important thing about a PIzza is the crust and the crust at the HB is absolutely delectable. This may sound easy to attain but believe me, someone who has made 1000's of pizzas for a local grocery store ...it is definitely not.
The desserts are limited but the Compartés chocolate (organic luxury chocolate)is first rate though there is a Scone on the menu as well as Cookies. Espresso drinks are also good but WHERE ARE THE CAKES???

Very friendly service. However, the pizza is terrible.  Tastes like frozen crust.  I love the Honor Bar restaurant menu for its flavor and freshness so I was excited to try the new Honor Market take-away counter.  Very disappointed in the pizza quality and the coffee was mediocre at best. I won't be ordering the food again but I might stop in to buy a gift item from their retail shop.

Always fantastic service. I usually stop in for an iced latte to go, and have picked up some other pastry items in the past. Most recently, I needed to escape LA and driving over to Montecito is usually my go to spot. It's nice that things are open and feel halfway normal around here.

I stopped off at Honor Market to grab a latte before hitting the beach. I'd picked up sandwiches already so didn't need food items but the menu always looks really yummy.

I'll definitely order to-go or dine in soon. Great selection of little gifts in the store as well.

Second best kale salad locally (after Scarlett Begonia). Would give four stars but I sort of didn't understand the packing charge.  But very close to five stars.  The menu isn't large but everything is consistently great.

Summary: next door to Honor Bar but they have a different menu and very decent coffee/desserts! 

Food: good baked goods! I had a really good cookie to go with my coffee... they also have pizza! I didn't try the pizza but it looked legit! 

Service: the worker behind the counter was really nice and professional. We ordered the wrong item and she quickly made everything perfect! 

Ambiance: the best. Can't be beat. Location is key and this place sits on a beautiful street in one of my favorite beach towns! Perfect weather to go along with the perfect scene! 

Peking: Santa Barbara has lots of parking places everywhere! No issues with parking... I recommend parking a bit farther to enjoy a really nice walk to this place. 

Conclusion: I only ordered cookies and coffee and that was really good... the place is affiliated with Honor Bar and the food at Honor Bar is always better than average! I can't imagine anyone eating here walking away unhappy. I will definitely be trying our their pizzas and other items next time I'm in the area!!

Stopped by on our way to Solvang from Glendora, needed a pick me up after 3 hours on the road with our 7 and 3 year old. We got 2 warm freshly baked chocolate chip cookies which were eaten immediately by the kids, and two Cowboy cookies which were very satisfying!

Worst! Coffee! EVER!!!!

YOU GUYS NEED TO CALL KLATCH COFFEE and ask them how to make coffee. My husband, who is NOT AT ALL picky about coffee even said it was one of the worst hes ever had. He prefers the mochas, which tasted like nestle syrup. I had a regular latte and it didnt taste anything like espresso. Im so bummed.

it's one of our favorite places in Montecito and we always stop by for a coffee, scone and a bit of shopping when coming to SB.  today's coffee and service were great as always, however, while I was waiting for my coffee, six other people came in to the tiny store.  that is totally unacceptable during a pandemic. they need to review their Covid policies asap.

Some of the best pizza in town but they've raised the prices on their entire menu twice since opening well under a year ago, resulting in pizzas that are now over 7 dollars more than their initial price. Disappointing from a company with traditionally strong customer service.

Update: in addition to raising the prices, they have also made the pizzas smaller - they used to fill up the entire box and now fill up barely halfway

Fantastic staff and great coffee. I always make a note to hear in on my way down the 101.

Great people!

Cheesy cheesy pizza 

So good that even being lactose intolerant did not stop me from eating it (my toilet did not like this decision though)

Little light on sausage but cheesy cheese was exceptional

" Nothing brings people together like good food" 
Just moved in and found this charming energized restaurant surrounded with wonderful items for entertaining in your home. Everyone are personable, friendly and attentive. From a coffee scone to a phenomenal fried chicken sandwich which  was flavorful and cooked perfectly. The name becomes this place and the energy and regulars enjoy every bite, and continue to create moments within the community of peace and laughter at this gem.

Ok possibly the best sandwiches I have ever had. The bread is amazing. Love the pickled pinions. All the food is amazing. Cute little shop with awesome Hugh quality items. I bought a Frama shampoo and conditioner and love them.  Great stop on a drive up the 101 as well. Seating outside as well. Highly recommend.
Loved the pizza - crust was buttery and had a crispy cornmeal bottom.  Easy take out, it was ready quickly.

Possibly the best Pizza I have ever had.  I cannot remember when I have come across a better  balance of flavors and textures.  Tonights special was the Greek.  Simple but amazing.  The crust is to die for.  Frankly, I am shocked to find such a killer pie so close to home.  I need to try their Bar/Eatery next door.
Best pizza I have ever had!!! I wish we had one in Monterey! We will for sure come back!

Stopped in on a Monday night to order two pizzas. One cheese for my 9 yr. old son and the Mediterranean for my wife and I. The cheese on both was terrible and inedible. Don't take a chance on  pizza at Honor Pizza,  go and get your pizza somewhere else.

Staff are lovely, products are lovely.  Beautiful store.  I would say enjoy the view and spend your money elsewhere.  Overpriced and coffee is horrible.  I don't know what kind of beans they're using for espresso but it's not dark roast.  Flat and bitter
Our go-to coffee spot in Montecito.  Staff are uber professional and friendly and the coffee is quality.  We haven't tried them yet, but their pizzas and cookies look yummy!

Can't eat at Honor Bar without stopping here for some goodies to take home (Raisin pecan scone? Chocolate chip cookie? Slice of pizza? Something hot to drink? Yes, please!). If you're looking for lunch but you don't have time to sit down at Honor Bar, you can order anything off the Honor Bar menu to go at Honor Market.

The Honor Market has the most amazing pizza's!  The crust is thin and flavorful and my favorite is the Three Pepper....the subtle flavors of the peppers and the pickled onions are such a tasty combination, there's no other pizza out there like it.  The crust is always crunchy and be sure to dip it in the magical green sauce that they give with the pizza's.  They also have an amazing breakfast burrito....it's small but just the right size so you're satisfied but not overly stuffed.  While you wait for your food, look around, they have the most eclectic and cool stuff to buy for yourself or gifts for your friends.  Espresso, wine, scones, cookies...they've got it all.  I love it there!!!!

I just love the food here! The pizza is absolutely amazing, the selection rotates daily. I love that they use seasonal ingredients, the store is very clean and inviting. Service is wonderful, they are very knowledgeable about the product and eager to help. Prices are a bit high, but the quality is well worth the splurge. Great option while in Montecito!

I don't know if my review should have as much weight as the other reviews I see here... I was only inside for five minutes and only ordered a scone and a cappuccino.

But the girl that helped me (my receipt says it was Emma) was either trained very well or just a nice person or both... super friendly.  That can make or break your first impression of a place.

The coffee was solid.  The scone was just so perfect... maybe the best I've ever had.  I'm not gonna embarrass myself here and start going on and on about this scone.  But it was so delicate and buttery... tons of pecans and super flaky.

I wanted to give it a five. I will go back soon and update the review. Until then let me start with what they do right
1. Beautifully curated shop. You can always find a hostess gift or something much more 
2. Delicious cookies at a fair price of two dollars per cookie.
3. Pick up to go salads or order a pizza.   Coffees are pretty good 
4. The reason they get a lower rating then I would like to is  because of the gentleman in the kitchen who kept walking around without his mask even popping food in his mouth and not washing his hands and eating right where he's making the pizzas.    I asked and pointed that out to the cashier. The man in the kitchen glared at me. I finally ended up speaking to Shauna the manager who is lovely. I am hopeful that they will solve this.   I observed it happening multiple times while I was there even after I said something.  
We want and do support local business.   They need us. Please Honor Bar. Support those who support you by having staff adhere to Safety &  health protocols. 
We will come back to try again

Beautiful bike ride from Santa Barbara on the coast trail. Venture into Montecito and treat yourself to honor market pizza. The Greek pizza is to die for with light fluffy crust with or without the chicken sausage. Take your pizza back down to butterfly beach and enjoy!   
We will be back. Memorable flavors and must be tried!
A good second choice if you don't have time for Honor Bar. The pizza is incredible and desserts are incredible.

The food was good but it doesn't come with hash browns and toast !? The cashier pre checked "15%" tip before she turned it around to me lol not too slick young lady. $35+ dollars for two egg Benedict's is pretty outrageous but to be honest the food prices in Santa Barbara all around is pretty nuts and they rated this a "$$" out of "$$$$" which is utter nonsense it's definitely "$$$$". Two egg Benedict's in Cerritos (a high rated neighborhood too) is only $15+ which COMES WITH HASH BROWNS AND TOAST

Best Corn Dog on the planet!  And I've been craving one since I was pregnant with my daughter.  Now I'm pregnant with my second and finally my craving for non-fast food and delicious gourmet corn dog has been satiated!

All these bad reviewers should just shove it... It was a wonderful experience from the ordering at the counter to the great customer service to sitting down at the picnic tables to receiving our food. Plus workers kept coming out clearing and cleaning plates so there was always an open table. My sandwich was great and my husbands tri tip as well. I can see why the typical Santa Barbara yuppies don't like it... We loved it and could tell that people love working there and caring about good food.

We're local, walking from home customers and want The Shop to succeed. Today was a disappointment. Hopefully, it was an off day or adjustment to being so popular.
 
I ordered quickly as the group of 6 ahead of me was lagging and offered me to go before them. My husband likes eggs and bacon so I got him the Rollex on the order taker's recommendation.  Half the egg was very cooked(dark brown) basically burnt. He tossed it halfway through. My Ahhnold was bland.

And, the funny part...the table of 6 who ordered after me were served before us, as was another table who ordered after me.

So, not a bad experience, just underwhelming. My take-away, still quality ingredients and maybe needing a bit more attention to detail.

Think this is one of the or the best cafe in SB. Wonderful staff and customer service every time. Came in starving once and asked if I could have any small leftover crumbs from the kitchen while waiting for my order. The guy came out with a carrot bran muffin on the house. Places like that always steal my heart and I always look forward to go back. The food is usually excellent I've had a few things that lacked some and others that were amazing, esp their baked goods! Good outside tables with a view towards the hills. Lots of free parking.

We stopped driving back from LA at 12.30pm. The school crowd had just gotten there. I was like 'oh my god no! It will be ages before we eat.' Hungry three year old being no fun. I could believe how fast the line moved and how fast the food arrived. It was great! We had the 'just the tip trip sandwich and some French toast for the wee guy. Not one bit left on the plate and the ice coffee was really nice too. Add to that super friendly staff and this is our new lunch stop between slow and LA. An easy 5 stars
Excellent brunch place! We had a delicious wrap and chicken sandwich, both were very filling. Nice outdoor seating with umbrellas, and the service was prompt. Would definitely return here.

3.5/5 

The Shop is located in the more residential parts of Santa Barbara and parking is pretty easy to find. I ordered the tugboat, which is an eggs Benedict on top of fried chicken and biscuits drizzled with some sauce. The tugboat was pretty good and the chicken was just right. Not dry and crisp to perfection. My friend ordered one of their kale salads and she said it was a bit disappointing. It lacked flavor and overall wasn't enjoyable. The Shop offers indoor and outdoor seating although there is more room in their outdoor patio.

The Shop is also a pay first, then sit down restaurant. This place is great for groups since no added gratuity or etc is added to your meal. I would  say a major reason I wouldn't necessarily come here often is because the pricing for their dishes isn't the most reasonable. The tugboat was $14 and it didn't have any sides or anything. 

Food was good, but the portions of food for their price could be better.

Integrity issue..mismatched pricing..accidental,too busy or ...?

Has anyone noticed their actual receipt machine (not the credit card receipt with total and no details) with the details of your order never prints?  Have been coming here on and off for about a year.  Same story. 

Today, the price listed for the weekend Benedict special with ham on their newer printed menus was lower than the one listed on the board.  They don't tell you this.  I noticed and asked if it was a different ham ...explaining second time around that I was also trying to understand price difference.  No is same ham.  I ordered the one from the printed menu in my hand pointing to it,  and when I did math i got charged the higher price. I asked which version he rang up.  He said he didn't know.  (He is the owner or main manager) he then checked and said higher.  
Without receipt was hard to tell where else this happened on the order and if axxess discount was truly given. 

He offered to give me the dollar, but what I wanted was transparency.  I had written in a tip and said just add it to the tip.  Plus, with the line behind me getting longer, it was not worth my bucks or the energy (plus don't want to disregard the people in line). 

Integrity at an establishment is critical.  Even if they have a mistake they should own it, clarify it.  Given the long duration of them not being able to print receipts makes me wonder are there other subtle small price discrepancies.  It is bigger than the dollar here or there with customers...but everyday...how many customers adds up for the shop.  If just a mistake fix it, fix the menu and fix your receipt machine.  Also your online menu still does not work, is  this so it is easier to play with pricing? I never thought about why it doesn't work until now,  hopefully is just a coincidence but it may affect credibility in eyes of some of your customers 

Hope it earns a four soon from me. Been here 3x this month with family, visitors and friends. 
Why 3: Integrity concern. Main reason!!
First time visit last year, hamburger was way undercooked. 
Today Brought out food and didn't bring the drink until end of meal.  

Why I hope it earns a four (I will return and update)
Pretty good food! Ham and bacon not too fatty, quality seems good. 
Nice sunshine. And shade outdoor seating 
Like the local vibe and want to support the local entrepreneurs especially those professing to source more local (and I would hope organic) product

Thanks Shop. Hope u get the pricing sorted and the receipt machine working 
I will update the review after next visit.

Highly recommended. Went for breakfast the other day and had a cappuccino, fried chicken with biscuit and gravy. Super scrumptious. So scrumptious we went back the same day for lunch. We had the friend chicken sandwich (yum!) and the burger and fries (double yum!). Atmosphere was great, nice outside seating area and the staff were friendly. No complaints.
Our bachelorette weekend started with lunch here. Absolute perfect lunch spot. The Mac and Cheese dish is amazing! Casual, relaxed outdoor seating. Staff were sweetest!

This place was going to be our first stop in town on our vacation, my bestest found it on yelp. Drove by and I thought it was a little coffee cart and I was really in the mood for a breakfast spot. I didn't see any seating, and I have a toddler so a high chair is required if I plan on getting any eating done. I am SO GLAD we decided to try to go a second time. What I found was indoor seating, great coffee and food. My husband and I always order a little of everything. We had pasteries, oatmeal, yogurt and coffee. The mocha was amazing and I would kill for that blueberry muffin recipe, seriously i think i licked the plate...The oatmeal and yogurt were both hearty, light, simple and full of flavor. SO GOOD!

 Aside from the really great food, did I mention I have a toddler? Well halfway through breakfast my son starts dancing to the little mermaid and lion king music they were playing. My bestest even commented that "they had a really eclectic music mix on that morning." The guys actually changed the radio to a toddler station. Seriously?! Probably the most considerate gesture of any restaurant we've been to since we've become a family of three. 

The guys were super friendly, if the food wasn't already good enough to bring me back (which it was) the service for sure sealed the deal. They seemed to genuinely love what they do, making great food and treating their customers like friends. Well done!!!!
Really good small brunch spot that has both outdoor and indoor seating. The food is really delicious and it's definitely a must-try in Santa Barbara!

So good, glad to see them so close to my house, its great to have other options besides tacos , pizza and subs. Breakfast is great, (tug boat) and served till close i think. The General Sanders is my favorite and my favorite local beer from Pure Order.

I love eating at the shop, amazing food . I gave it 4 stars because of the food and the location is perfect. I choose not to give them the full 5 stars because ,I recently  went there for breakfast as a take out. I had a groupon and only had a remaining balance of $1.71 I used my bank card and when I was asked to sign I notice it said $9 total. I took a double look because he said my total $1.71 when first handed over my card and saw that the guy who was helping me had applied a 15% tip on my TAKE OUT ORDER. I feel like you should let the customer decided on the tip and not help yourself. Not ok , I will not be going there for a while. So please check your totals before signing when you purchase anything there with your card.

I ordered the Eggs in yo face and a side of potatoes. The eggs were delicious! Two Poached eggs on a bed of avocado sitting on a single toasted bread slice. The potatoes were simple, potato chip sliced grilled with onions and seasoning. Great combo! And I washed it down with orange juice, sweet and tasty. Can't wait to come back and try the rest of the menu!

The Santa Maria is my fav! I'm a sauce person. The bbq sauce is really good and makes the chicken sandwich. Fries are pretty good as well. Seems a bit pricey....so it's only an occasional lunch spot for my husband and I.

amazing! Went on a Saturday morning around 10 AM and was not packed! we ordered and had our food and drinks in five minutes.  The food alone gets five stars, the drinks were good, and the view is something to see if you are from out of town. if i'm ever in Santa barbara again, it will be a must!
Best of the best! You can't go wrong with anything on the menu! We live 3 hours away and we come to Santa Barbara Just to eat at The Shop. Our family's all time fave by far! Freshest, tastiest food!

We love this place. Great food, great coffee, and great service. 

My wife took me here on my birthday and they even lit a candle for me and sang happy birthday from the kitchen. 

Then recently my wife and I came on our anniversary and she has the Breaky Sando and I had the YOLO. 

BEST breakfast sandwich and Fried chicken in SB by far.

Thanks for the great time and food!!!

Visiting beautiful Santa-B regularly as a little get away from crazy busy LA...Our first stop in town- The Shop Cafe on N. Milpas. If you are looking for an awesome breakfast/ lunch place- here it is! The food in The Shop Cafe worth every penny! Always fresh, delicious, tasteful assortments, great coffee too! One of my favorites- Justin- Yo- Face! ( Best poached eggs, salmon slices on a tasty crunchy toast).

Thank you The Shop Cafe for great friendly customer service and excellent food!

Will be back soon! :)

Breakfast for lunch! 
Ok, I will have to say, this is by far one of the best things I have ever eaten...in my life!  And for all that know me, know I am a huge foodie and have dined at many places.

I had the Carnitas Eggs Benedict.  The man at the window (maybe be the manager or owner) suggested substitution options because of my restrictions with raw egg.  He suggested poached hard eggs and a gravy instead of hollandaise.  The substitutions were spot on delicious and did not take away from the original dish.

The son had what's called, "YOLO..." biscuits, gravy and chicken. And said it was his new favorite.  The biscuit was tender and moist, chicken had a crispy coating yet balanced well with the dish and not being too overwhelming.

For my husband's sweet tooth...French toast with micro basil.  My gosh, had a bite and it was amazing too!!!
Surprisingly the micro basil took the French toast to another level...pure genius and an experience in every bite.

They have a bulletproof coffee that everyone talks about and their vanilla latte is the best I've had.

When in the area, it definitely is a must stop...goooooo!

We came to this place for breakfast this morning. I normally really enjoy coming here for lunch so I decided that breakfast would be equally good. 

I ordered the Sando and it was delicious, my fiancée ordered the Yolo and the chicken was very salty. No biggie.

However, I went up to the window to get napkins and the young kid who was bringing our order of fries out picked at our plate of fries and ate a couple before he walked our plate out to us ! 
Who does that ? This was unprofessional and disgusting. 

Such a great place that I won't be coming back to because of this unprofessional behavior.

There are so many yummy breakfast options in Santa Barbara but we decided to give this one a shot. I was a little surprised to find that it looks to be a to-go only place from the outside. However, you order at the front and can either eat your food indoors with fork and knife and plate and all or grab a seat outside.

Prices are a bit steep compared to other breakfast joints (you're looking at a $12-15 sandwich only, no sides). However, everything tastes wonderful.

I ordered the salmon-in-your-face with a poached egg ($10.50). It's a slice of toast with salmon, capers, and red onions. It's surprisingly filling, at least for a petite girl like me. I saw some photos where the toast came with two poached eggs but I think they changed the menu since.

My boyfriend ordered the tugboat which is basically eggs Benedict and only offered on the weekend. He got it with the tomatoes and bacon ($13). It was filling--ingredients are stacked high and a bit hard to eat without getting the different ingredients all over your face!

It's not a typical waiter-service restaurant. Also, come before 9:30! Anytime after that and the lines get very long. There isn't a lot of indoor seating so don't forget to bring a jacket!

nom nom nom!
perfect hearty brunch plates :)
We were in SB for a day and we know this was a popular place and it was! We got there at 10:30 and there was a line. So how it works is, you order and pay and then wait for your number to be called. They have both indoor and outdoor seating (can be really hot if you are right under the sun- they do have big umbrellas for each table but they don't cover the entire bench)
We ordered the YOLO and the Tugboat to share among the 4 of us and we were all super full.
The gravy on the YOLO was mindblowing! The fried chicken was done in a special way, more like how people deep fry fish fillet which makes it so much more interest. It was delicious! Went so well with the egg!
Our friends ordered the Tugboat which was great too. I think the way they deep fried the chicken made it extra interesting and less greasy.
We ordered the cold brew too, it was nice, not sour :)
Awesome service, decent prices, and all the food is amazing. One of the best tri tips in town... Can't beat the box lunch either!

I'm not sure what I got --  I know, that sounds weird, but you'll understand in a second. 

I just recently moved to Santa Barbara and was referred here by a co-worker. So seeing as I had nothing to do today, I decided to give it a try. 

The restaurant is easily missed, as it sits conspicuously next door to an auto repair shop. You order your meal at a window and are given a number. There are quite a few tables outside and a handful inside. Your food is brought to your table and bussed as well when you're finished. Service seemed fine for the minute interaction I had with anybody. Sandwiches come a la carte, so if you want fries or another side, don't forget to add it on. 

Everything on the menu sounded delicious and I was having a hard time making a decision. I asked the guy at the register what the most popular items were and he said: (1) The Tugboat and (2) the Chingon. Unfortunately, he also informed me that they were out of Hollandaise sauce and hence, I couldn't order either the (1) Tugboat or (2) the Chingon. 

New plan...

I decided to go with the General Sanders sandwich. The menu describes the sandwich as a "Buttermilk-fried chicken, beats, carrot puree and spring greens." However, as you can see in my picture, the sandwich is nothing like that. In fact, it was basically a thinly breaded dark meat chicken piece, placed on a bed of cole slaw and served on a roll. 

The strange thing is, none of the other photos of this sandwich look this way on Yelp -- which is why I'm curious. Did they run out of the other items on the sandwich and just slap some slaw on there?

My sandwich was okay, albeit the roll was a little dry. The chicken is dark meat (as opposed to the classical chicken breast), but I think this lends it to be more tender and juicy. The entire sandwich lacked seasoning, specifically salt. 

Prices are fairly reasonable, though the sandwich and a small iced tea ran me about $12.00. 

I'd come back here to try some of the other options for sure and I may even get this sandwich again to make sure it wasn't a fluke. Though, if you're able to see pureed carrots, beets and spring greens in my picture below, feel free to send me a message! 

3-Stars: "A-OK."

This place is so good my husband had the French melt it was amazing! I've never had anything like that before absolutely delicious. I got the Rolex it was really good but the French melt was even better we will be coming back here very soon. The service was really fast and very polite cool spot.
Everything we ordered was delicious( yogurt parfait, salmon tugboat, blueberry muffin, and drinks).

Hands down the best breakfast in Santa Barbara. We've been coming to Santa Barbara for over ten years, so trust me when I say we've tried every restaurant in town...TWICE.

I had the Rolex with avocado, and my wife had the best damn oatmeal. The Rolex was in a league of it's own when it comes to breakfast wraps. And I think it was the flatbread that really sealed the deal. Simple, fresh, creative, and delicious. Loved the smoked tomato spread. And her oatmeal was just as amazing. When I heard it had marscapone in it I thought it was going to be overly sweet and almost desert-like. Not at all the case. This oatmeal is a delicate balance of tasty ingredients that melts in your mouth.

The food is amazing and not expensive. it's a perfect location away from the crowds on State Street with plenty of parking and a nice outside area for sunny days. The service was awesome and we met the owner Chris who was super nice. Go there.
Yelped best breakfast in Santa Barbara and it did not disappoint!! It's a walk-up but don't let that fool you! Food and service is 5 star! Highly recommend!
best breakfast deal in SB. I get the eggs in yo face with salmon at least once a week.

Perhaps occasionally I've been a little loose with my 5-stars but this place earned every bit of it. I got the quinoa salad and it was just delicious, the pistachios were a nice touch. The locality was nice, and the staff was extremely pleasant. What do you think the numbers on the bottles of water mean?

My friend and I were walking the dog down Milpas today when we made this wonderful discovery....The Shop!  Delicious food with a comfortable patio. Dog friendly too!  This is my favorite breakfast spot! Will try the lunch next time... Two thumbs up!

Fate is great thing! Rather than fight with the morning crowds at the pastry shops in Solvang my family and I decided to take our chances and find a local place in Santa Barbara before we made it to the Fess Parker DoubleTree.  Usually I select the place based on all those great Yelp reviews but today my wife took her shot while I drove and boy did she find a great place.
We almost missed the place so look closely as you get near the end of the 700 block. There is parking in the front and you can park in the 20 minute zone. The staff will watch for the meter maid while you eat.
The place was buzzing.  I could tell the staff was having a great time, whether taking orders, pulling espressos or crafting the meals.  You order through a window all the while watching the chef plate the meal of those lucky patrons that made it there before you.
A cherry & vanilla coffee cake had just been brought to the window just under our noses as we ordered as well as pecan cinnamon rolls with orange icing. The sweet smell was just too much. One of each were a perfect choice for the latte' and a sample of treats to arrive later.
The YOLO was my choice from the menu board. This gave me the chance to savor three things that must be crafted perfectly and from scratch to meet my standards, biscuits, sausage gravy and fried chicken.  I wasn't disappointed.  Mind you, this is not for calorie counters unless you like counting higher and higher. The chicken was moist on the inside and just the right amount of flavor and crispiness on the outside.  The chicken sat on fried biscuits surrounded by a moat of sausage gravy.  It is a must have for B&G lovers.
My wife got the The Tijuana, chicken and avocado wrap and my daughter ordered the lunch box of chicken nuggets & mac n' cheese.  Both were great choices as I am sure all the selections are.  The surprise was that the nuggets were handmade and hand breaded with a mac n' cheese that had at least three cheeses and very creamy.
As I read this and look at the other great choices from the other reviews I think its time to pack up the family and head back to The Shop before we head south.
Enjoy SB!

Stopped here a coupla weeks ago for a burger and fries. Great fresh bun. Great real beef patty. Nice self serve water situation. BUT. One of those burgers that made me wonder whether the chef had ever tried to eat it as served. Huge, which is nice sometimes, but that much burger, if eaten at a sane rate, is a mess and a half by the end. Bottom bun totally soaked with grease, the last handful unrecognizable, all sauce and squished out whatever it is. And the whatever it is is perhaps another bad idea. Not sure if you're someone who wants balance, when thinkin burger, but if so this ain't for you. They use bread and butter pickles ("sweet and sour") and a jalapeno(?) aioli, that pair as something more on a dessert wavelength than anything else. This is a burger with no bite, served (tho not sold this way on the menu) with thick potato chips (probably house made) that don't seem particularly flavorful.
