The water tastes less like tap water than most Santa Barbara restaurants, but is served in steel cups with horrible rims - sharp and thin and not particularly successful. Bonus: if you sit on the (spacious, charming) patio the cups reflect just right, and you ask yourself whether somehow you're drinking a severely dehydrated child's urine sample (or apple juice, if you're feeling less juvenile). 

The sweetheart who took our order wasn't in to eye contact, or verbal responses, which was kind of a bummer, though understandable, considering that 90% of their lunch crowd is sb high students.

Who knows. I'm feeling harsh, but more because I don't think the price reflects the quality of service, or menu creation. It's a sweet location. I wish it was more in line with the actual neighborhood they could serve, instead of a hip spot on paper and a lackluster experience in person.

Found this spot through yelp decided to give it a try. We got the arugala salad and the top long eggs Benedict over fried chicken they were delicious the salad was a bit sweet due to the oranges and pomegranates but the feta cheese offset the sweetness. you order all your food at the counter and you get your own utensils and water and they bring out your food. we finished everything! perfect spot for a breakfast or lunch

Wow, that was such a good breakfast! Thanks yelpers for such a good find. I ordered the tug boat weekend special with buttered fried chicken and some fresh fruit. The food came out very quickly and was nice and hot. The fried chicken was crisp and full of flavor and so were the biscuits and gravy covering it. Haven't had eggs Benedict that tasted that good for a while.
Just had a fabulous lunch.  We had the fried chicken sandwich, the tri tip sandwich, a burger & Mac & cheese.  Great food, good service.  The Mac & cheese was to die for.

I had the Just the Tip (lol) sandwich and it was great. It was served on high quality bread with some creme fraiche which really put it over the top. Awesome.
The french press coffee I had was equally good and they gave me some whole milk to put in it, a great way to start a lazy Saturday.

On a road trip. Got hungry. Looked for a spot on yelp. Found this beauty. And took s chance. 
Wow! Simple. Real. Fresh. Delicious. 
Outdoor seating is perfect on this gorgeous day. 
Chris, the proprietor was super helpful, charming and down to earth. 
This will be a first choice stop every time we're in SB. 
THANKS FOR EVERYTHING!

Breakfast has always been my favorite meal of the day. To find this place a truly one of the highlights of our trip.  The restaurant is at a street corner, kind of easy to miss if you drive too fast 

Weekend seems to be packed with people so it may be wise to get there early.  We ordered southwest chicken French toast and the in yo face salmon.  The salmon combo was absolutely delicious. The wheat toast was out of this world!  So soft and tasty. The smoked salmon was definitely a home run.  Mixed with a poached egg and capers, the flavor was top notch.  

The fried chicken with French toast was nothing I've ever had.  So good and fresh.  It's not drenched in overly sweet maple syrup, but the balance of flavor was just right.  

Highly recommend this place for breakfast and brunch.  If you are ever in the area this is a must visit.  Oh, and did I mention the coffee latte was better than Starbucks?  There you go.

I've been coming to The Shop since you guys have opened, when things were actually affordable and the food was fantastic.

I came and ordered the YOLO, which I paid for and was shortly called back to be told that the YOLO was no longer available for the day, no problem. I switched it to the TugBoat with Fried Chicken, which Is always my second choice. When it came out, it was highly underwhelming, the fried chicken looked burnt and the pieces were so small, which I was willing to overlook, but then I tried the biscuit which was so dry and falling apart that It was hard enough to swallow down with the lack of sauce.

I thought about telling the staff about this right away, but I wasn't trying to put anyone on the spot, because I didn't have the time to wait for another plate, which would also be a waste of food, if it was thrown out.

I love the shop, but that was a very disappointing experience, and just wanted to let you know that, and I hope that does not becomes a standard thing, as at $15 with a tip, it is not cheap and expect more.

Also, it was about 90 degrees in the back area with no fan and no water in the water jug. 

Lastly, there was a guy who was wearing at least $75 dollar shoes and did not look homeless who was annoying us in line about having not ate in 3 days and if we could buy him a meal. He kept coming to the back area and sat down and make comments on the things my group was talking about, it was rather uncomfortable, and after 10 minutes he would get up and go back in line to bug others to buy him a $12 - $15 item.
Love this spot.  Everything I've had is amazballs.  Seriously. Delicious.  I go on the reg. and you should too.
Wow! Can't say enough good things. Rollex was wonderful!! Great small outside cafe with great service. Definitely heading back next time we are in Santa Barbara.

Our go to breakfast stop whenever we visit Santa Barbara...friendly staff and awesome, wholesome breakfast to start your day right! They also have bulletproof coffee which tops it all off. Thank you to the staff for making the experience positive every time!
This place was my pre work breakfast spot. No longer :( it's like this place just stop caring about the quality of the food. I miss the old shop!!

Went yesterday for lunch, pretty damn good chicken sandwich called the sweet marie. Great mix of flavors that compliment each other. I've never been here but have always driven by this area, it's about what you would pay for a good burger or sandwich meaning it's not cheap but it's worth the trip
Ignore the sourpuss reviews. Food is scratch made and better than most snooty breakfast places in town. Owners work in house and always check on customers to ensure breakfast is up to par.

This has become my new fav breakfast spot! Not only does the food taste fresh but it's so yummy too! My fave is the french toast, the bread is so fluffy and the syrup is amazing. Second favorite was the Rolex but now i love the Chilaquiles yumm!!! The truth is there isn't anything i've ordered that i haven't loved. The outdoor seating is great and the service is great. The food is so tasty i always forget to take a picture before i dive in

This place is amazing. First of all everything that came out of the kitchen looked so good. I had the salmon eggs in yo face with avocado added and my boyfriend had the sweet Maria. Both were absolutely amazing. It's the next day and I'm craving it again. It is a little bit pricey but well worth it. Parking is on the street and they have limited seating.

Excellent food! The food & drink is easily 3.5 stars, I round up because of Yelp. The fried chicken here is perfecto. I think they use only white meat. I got the General Sanders, amazing. Wasn't sure how I felt reading the description, but it is beyond the written words. Great combination not over powered by the slaw or apples. The chips were crispy too. The chicken and gravy with their biscuit and eggs wonderful too. We also ordered the Rolex. It was good, different. Creative take on a wrap. Their wrap tastes like injura bread functions efficiently like a tortilla. Pretty unique. All the fillings inside were fresh and perfect. The Rolex could've been a little bigger or perhaps served with a side of something, but I liked that it donates $2 from the order. Get a side of biscuit, it's the best!

They serve mimosas in mason jars which was a nice touch, you get a lot for $8. Lots of different drinks including fruit smoothies and coffees. Overall a great breakfast place. The seating on the patio is great it has a view of the mountains and the homes. Inside is lovely too wish there was more lighting inside. Dog friendly patio, but no water bowl. 

The lines can look long but they move pretty fast. Order your food at the window take your number and have a seat they'll bring it to you. Casual but the food has grandeur in presentation, flavor and quality. 

Staff working in the kitchen was fabulous They were pushing out food with passion and precision. They have a fully exposed kitchen so you can watch everything being made. However we really didn't appreciate the server who brought us our food. She had a major attitude towards everyone and kept bringing us the wrong food. We would say thank you and she'd walk away almost pouting. Very immature behavior for someone who looks like a full grown woman. On top of that she wouldn't say the items name, when we'd ask she'd look at us like with disbelief. Other servers bringing out the food were sincerity and attentiveness. She was just exceptionally rude. Funny thing is we actually tipped 22% ahead of time after we placed our order and paid at the window. Her attitude disgusted me so much I wanted to go back and lower the tip amount. My guess is people either don't tip at all or tip a small amount here since it's not full service, and most people only tip max of 20%... considering it was Father's Day and she's on the clock representing a business you'd think the given would be to be nice and presentable. As a general rule of thumb tips are one of those things you have to earn she definitely didn't deserve it. Also the gentlemen taking our order only gave us a receipt for the credit card and not an itemized receipt. Usually at restaurants you receive both the credit card receipt and itemized receipt as proof of purchase and so you can check to see everything you ordered was delivered. He was young, but young isn't an excuse. Since the line was long we let it go. 

Parking was surprisingly plentiful on the street. It's a lovely shaded area all around. Cute shops and lovely things to look at. 

Tips: wear a hat and shades, it can get very sunny. Also you can leave your tip at the window when you order via credit card receipt, or in cash at your table, if you have cash then I recommend cash tip because the servers here are a hit or miss.

This is such a hidden gem. It's a very quaint and quiet cafe, so it can be easy to miss, but this place is an absolute must if you are in the area. The customer service was fantastic, the atmosphere was cute and quaint, and the food was literally some of the best that I have ever had. I ordered the Rolex (scrambled eggs, bacon, avocado and roasted tomato sauce in a house made wrap) with a house made parfait, my girlfriend got poached eggs on toast with avocado and a side of fresh fruit. Everything was absolutely delicious, fresh, and well made. We will be back without a doubt. I wish there were more places like this!
Amazing food! I had a difficult time choosing because it all looked so good. Ended up taking the pancakes and they were amazing! Definitely go here when you're in santa barbara!
The food was cold and tasteless. Coffee was blah. Will not be returning. Parking not convenient. So not worth the hassle of finding parking and waiting on cold food.

I got the Justin Yo Face and it was delicious. I loved the salmon and the fried capers, the egg was perfectly poached. Also tried the Sambo and it was great too. Love the fresh breads there, next time I'm in the area I will come back again.

The Shop Kitchen is an unsuspecting walk up window off of Milpas with great food! After you order your food at the window, seating can be found in a small, open-air, indoor area, or outside at picnic tables under bright yellow umbrellas. Fun music fills the air as you enjoy brunch. My fiancé had the toast with homemade almond butter, bananas, granola, and honey, and it was AMAZING! I had the chicken eggs Benedict, however the chicken on top was not the best...the only reason I am giving this 4 stars instead of 5. The eggs Benedict was served on a delicious homemade buttermilk biscuit. A great find for a casual brunch!

My favorite Santa Barbara brunch space. The food here is absolutely delicious and they have something for everybody. The menu is of decent size and is super fun. I've eaten everything here and it is all amazing. I love the atmosphere. You order at the windows, get your number, and choose a table inside or out depending on your preference. Before long you're food is delivered and ready to eat, or instagram, and it's defiantly instagram worthy. I come here every time I've had a night out. It's the perfect hangover remedy. It's also the perfect place to bring visitors. The food is great, the crowd is great, the parking is easy, you can't go wrong. And as a cherry on top there's a super cool car dealerships across the street that you can check out where they have a ton of classic and exotic vehicles for sale. It's pretty dope.
Great service and even better food. Went to the shop today and had one of the best breakfast salads I have had in a long time. I would highly recommend checking this place out!
What a fun breakfast spot! Delicious veggie omelette and breakfast wrap! Great service and atmosphere. Wonderful breakfast experience during our road trip!
I love everything I've tried. Fresh ingredients mostly prepared in house. The yogi is a must have, to die for. Highly recommended.
Favorite breakfast spot in SB. Husband always gets the east side with carnitas. I try to switch it up but always come back to the Tugboat.

The Shop Cafe ROCKS! I was on a road trip with a couple of my girlfriends and we Yelped best breakfast in Santa Barbara and The Shop Cafe came up with a great rating, so we had to try it! I have to say the menu item names are HILARIOUS, so when you order make sure to say what u want with gusto! Eggs IN YO FACE....YO! LOL!  Best service anywhere,  ask for Dudley! He's awesome! He went above and beyond to make us feel welcome, he even wrote out a small itinerary of stops for us to do on our road trip! The food was FABULOUS! I ordered the YOLO, fried chicken breast, sausage gravy and the flakiest biscuit you will ever eat, IT WAS DELICIOUS! A must stop if you're in the area!
The food was bald and over salty. There were flue ever where. The Service was bad and they were a little rude

Every once in a while a nondescript, understated place knocks your socks off. That was my experience at The Shop Cafe in Santa Barbara.  If you are not familiar with this place, I could easily imagine walking/driving right past its trailer like appearance; I'm so glad we stopped.  I had the Good Day Sunshine breakfast - an absolutely delicious bowl of fresh sourced ingredients including kale, pom seeds, parsnip, feta and crispy potato with poached egg - one of the tastiest and imaginative meal salads I've ever eaten.  You can easily modify the ingredients (add/subtract) to suit your own dietary preferences as well - the staff is very friendly and accommodating. I can't speak to the pancakes or waffley side of things but I will say that the breakfast I did enjoy exceeded my hopes in every way.  This will now be a destination stop for us the next time we are in Santa Barbara!
Had the Sweet Maria sandwich today and it was delicious. Customer service is amazing.

I enjoy how this place has a very beach-y diner feel.  You walk up to order outside and most of the seating is outdoors.  

The food is really good.  On the weekends they serve a eggs Benedict with different choices of toppings from tomatoes to bacon and fried chicken.  By the way, B ordered the tomatoes to be healthy, but after trying the fried chicken, I regretted my decision!  

There is a healthy scramble plate that is also really good with kale and eggs.  It definitely tastes healthy.  

The prices were a little pricy since you were not really being served, but overall it was a good place to grab brunch.

Had breakfast here with my bf one morning. It's like a old Pup N Taco or Taco Bell type location, so you walk to the window to order. The outside looks like nothing special, and the name is quite generic, but the breakfasts were delicious, well put together, bistro-type food! Sit outside and enjoy! Truly a hidden gem/treasure not to be missed! Yum!

Generally, I love this place. The Pigs in a Blanket (BLT) is so delicious, hitting flavor, texture, appearance, and taste over the top. I highly recommend it.

I have not been as pleased with the 2 salads I have had there. They must have taken one salad I had 6 months ago off the menu. Last night I had the Cecelia for $10. I was truly underwhelmed, both in the size of the order and the flavor. When I opened the Take-out box, I was shocked that the amount was small, especially since the cost was not. There are other places in SB where I can get a salad for $8.50 and get two meals out of it. Not so with the Cecelia. Plus, no matter what the price, I would not order it again.
We passed by the shop café during our trip and the breakfast were amazing and delicious with outside deck.

Great find!!!!     Amazing breakfast.    I love to search out great breakfast spots......    well I took the shot, and score!!!!     Started with a cappuccino for me and a latte with Almond milk for Anna; just perfect!!     They had a special eggs Benedict with Carnitas that was to die for!  From their standard menu we had the house cured salmon on top a slice of perfect wheat toast,  a poached egg and blended with delicious flavors of fried capers, onion and dill crème fraîche.   If you love finding a great hole in the wall restaurant like I do,  you won't go wrong coming here.
Love this place tasty food lovely atmosphere and great service. I definitely recommend the salmon on toast

A little over priced for the amount of food u get. Ordered the salmon in yo face. It's good but u only get one slice of bread and salmon. Then we ordered Mac on crack. Blue cheese was too strong for my taste. Probably won't come back

I got the Best Damn Oatmeal and it was the best damn Oatmeal!!! Initially ordered the Tug Boat but was not a fan of the hollandaise sauce. However, everyone in the restaurant  seemed to love it because it was a popular menu item. Service was excellent. Reasonably priced food.

We came here based on the rave Yelp reviews.  If you are not from here, the restaurant sign is not visible from the street.  If you see the "J's Tire" sign and yellow umbrellas then you are at the right place.  This is a very casual eatery, you order your food with the cashier and then find a table (outdoor seating with some indoor tables).  The food came out pretty quick, presentation was nice.  We ordered the eggs Benedict with carnitas and French toast with fried chicken. Our food came out cold.  French toast was under cooked and soggy in the middle.  The fried chicken (dark meat) that came with French toast has a nice crispy coating and good flavor.

We were about to head home to Venice, CA but needed some coffee before we hit the road--

Didn't want to StarBUCK it, so we decided to drive around looking for a local cafè.

We stopped when we saw a "coffee" sign outside and couldn't help but order a bite to eat as well. 

Completely taken by the whole atmosphere and most importantly the FOOD--it's like having a meal in your home prepared by a personal chef.  The food really has the feel of what optimum home cooking is like.  One of the owners brought our food to the table.  You've got to love these guys, it's a beautiful thing. 

We had the salmon and poached eggs on toast (GENIUS idea: they fry the capers--absolutely GENIUS flavor and texture!) and the ham, egg, and cheese on a ciabatta. 

I don't write Yelp reviews often but felt compelled to do so for the Shop Cafè.  This is the place to go if you like REAL food.  Great ownership and atmosphere, but above all, phenomenal food.

I've had Just the Tip, Jean Claude Van Ham, General Sanders, and Pig in the Garden. All delicious, but Just the Tip is definitely my favorite. Their in house made chips are great (crunchy with just a little bit of give) and the fries are decent, but not as good as everything else. At about $10 per entree this place is worth going. Rather hipstery, but if you're okay with that, this is the place to go.

I don't write reviews very often but this place is great! Just had the Rolex- basically a breakfast burrito in a wrap, with delicious a smoky tomato based sauce inside. Came out hot and fast and much bigger than I expected for the price. I'll be back for another one soon.
Shrimp grits and almond butter banana bread were good but the portions are small and the orange juice didn't taste fresh squeezed.

This was easily our favorite food stop on our SB vacation. SO good in fact, we ended up dining here 2 days in a row for breakfast! 
The eggs benedict was incredible. We had the version with bacon one day and then the fried chicken on the other. I was a little wary of the fried chicken, thinking it would be heavy and icky - but it's actually lightly breaded, very similar to chicken katsu. And it was amazing. My husband is now all about comparing every eggs benedict he has with the one from The Shop Kitchen.

Healthy options with a twist. Take the ti me to find this place. Weekends they offer an expanded breakfast menu   Recommend their eggs Benedict which features their home made biscuits and avocado and southwest hollandaise sauce. French press coffee too!  Funky atmosphere. Cali at its best
While passing through Santa Barbara we stopped in here for a weekday breakfast.  It's fast and excellent - far better than any of the cookie cutter places we passed on the way here.  Recommended.
I love The Shop! Everything is really creative and tasty. I found a great deal on www.Seeker.co and got a free coffee with my breakfast! The Yogi has the fluffiest yogurt you'll ever encounter.

We keep coming back! My wife and I have tried numerous items from their breakfast menu and have loved them all. My favorite is their weekend breakfast menu item called tugboat (eggs Benedict) with their signature buttermilk fried chicken for an extra $4. My wife's favorite is a breakfast wrap called Rollex. It's not the cheapest place to get breakfast, but if you want some killer home-made style food, this is the place. Even though it's next door to an automotive shop (hence the name), the Rivera views are great!

Think of this restaurant as a Hipster food truck without wheels.

I think the reviewers are being a little too kind to this establishment and maybe it's because it's a college town with few breakfast options?  Anyhow, we chose it because of it being on the way to UCSB where we had a tour scheduled on Wednesday for my son.

The location is super hard to find without your GPS tapping you on the head and telling you exactly where it is. Why is that you ask?  Because they don't have any exterior signage, at least none that I could see as we were driving by. The only thing that tipped us off that it was a place to eat was the fact that there are umbrellas outside and we could see the tops of peoples heads above the hedge. What makes it more difficult is that the business directly next door is some kind of automotive shop (I guess that's where they derived the name of this restaurant), which made me think initially that this outdoor seating area was simply for the customers of the automotive place to wait while their car was being worked on.

Alas, thankful to have found the restaurant I now faced the challenge of finding parking. Street parking in the nearby neighborhood is your only option. 

To order food you place your order at the window, get a number and then you go and find a seat. After craving pancakes I was sad to be told that they only make pancakes on the weekends (who does that?  evil, people, evil!). So I settled for the Banana in Yo Face, which is a thick slice of Brioche toast, slathered with almond butter and topped with sliced banana and finished off with a ribbon of honey. Super good but still not pancakes.

My son had the YOLO which is a buttermilk biscuit topped with fried chicken and sausage gravy. 

Food is decent but overpriced for what you actually get. I'm sure some would argue and tell me that they are making the bread from scratch and therefore it's worth more, but so are other restaurants and the same price includes table service.

Um. YUM. If you are driving through SB like we were, I would highly recommend this place. The food was incredibly fresh and delicious (and that is coming from a food snob Aussie!) and the customer service is great. The place is also very cute. Definitely get the yogurt parfait side - yummo!
Great breakfast! The eastside toast is spicy but perfect aid! Salmon eggs Benedict and the Tug boat with bacon is so yummy!

Incredible breakfasts! One of the better lox combos I've had on the west coast.

Fresh juice and picnic tables out front -- great compliments to the breakfast and get your day started right.
I tried the Crack Mac...OMG!  Soooo tasty and very cheesy, loads of bacon and pecans.  A must try if you like mac n cheese, incredible!!!
Fresh, healthy, delicious. A great find if you're a foodie. Menu is diverse and has something for everyone. Beautiful on the plate too. Will definitely come back

Great spot with great food and really nice staff.

I had the salmon in ya face and it was delicious! The Kamboucha on tap is also highly recommended.

Just tried this spot for the first time...really good lunch. Kept it simple and went with the Shop Burger and it didn't disappoint. A lot of my SB friends recommended this place and I'm glad they did. Well priced burger, real tasty while being a little different than everyone else. Real good fries as well. Def recommend. Will be back next time I'm in SB.

Driving through, stopped by for a quick and healthy breakfast. The Shop Cafe was a great Yelp! find. I had the good day sunshine salad which is a fresh kale and field greens salad, sliced fennel, roasted apples, feta cheese, with a poached egg on top. What a wonderful combo for breakfast salad. The girls had the saldo sandwich which is scramble eggs, ham, cheese, and mayo on a shop bun. The hubby had their amazing oatmeal which was creamy and hearty, and delicious. Their coffee was also good, great bold, but not bitter flavor. I would have loved to sample their baked goods since they bake all their breads. Would definitely return to The Shop Cafe, staff was also friendly.

shop kitchen is amazing. went with 'general sanders' and a beermosa, neither disappointed. with so much mediocre fried chicken being offered, shop kitchen be a blessing. the bun was toasted perfectly and the apple slaw was top notch. only bummer is I live in LA and don't have this closer. then again, if I had it closer, I'd probably get fat. thanks for hosting my favorite cheat day meals, Shop Kitchen. ya'll the real MVPs.
A must go. Try the shrimp with grits or the poached eggs. Quality food at a fair price this place rocks.
We went to The Shop Cafe for brunch and were blown away by the delicious food. Check out our full review here: http://chroniclefoodie.com/home/2014/2/6/foodie-diaries-brunch-at-the-shop-cafe
Love this place! Great food, great outstanding seating. And fun for a little group, especially on a pretty day. Creative meals!

This place is hit or miss in my humble opinion and is missing that "loving feeling".  The eggs Benedict are nice and the waffle batter buns will leave you with a blissful carb high as your insulin level shoots through the roof.  The food is fresh and everything is house made.  Everything tasted good - 4/5 stars. 

But....I've been here a couple times and each time seems to miss some thing(s) and leave me feeling like I may not come back.  

They are often out of things on their already very small menu.  I think this happened both times...disappointing. 

The food isn't served as warm/hot as it should be and timing seemed off the couple times I came by.  

The ambiance is a bit off....unless maybe it is super busy (not that way the times I came by).  You order at the window and find a seat next to busy Milpas.  

The prices seemed high for breakfast "to go" style.  $12 for 2 poached eggs over biscuit, ham, avo, sauce.  Nothing else on the plate.  Or maybe, it was the presentation?  Seemed like something should garnish it?  Maybe it was that everything wasn't perfect.  

Either way, I would say it is worth a try, but I'm not a regular.  A few dollars more and I'm sitting by the ocean with full service, hot coffee, and a great full plate breakfast.
Sooooo Goooood. Go early and order the tugboat and coffee. Best brunch!

Absolutely fabulous little café with outside and inside seating. Feels very homemade .....food is absolutely excellent. Definitely try the toast with housemade almond butter and bananas on top. The Mac on crack is incredible. Can't say enough about this place it would be my first six star review if I could.

Came on a Saturday morning, waited in line for a bit, sat outside, and was so happy! We split the fried chicken tugboat and YOLO. While the fried chicken was great in both dishes, I should have gone with a different meat like carnitas for the tugboat to make better use of the avocado. Star of the meal? Definitely the sausage gravy in the YOLO. It was so flavorful, savory, and I truly could have licked the bowl (I did, in reality). Come eat here!

Awesome, low key place for brunch. Order the YOLO to lower your life expectancy a few years, but it's totally worth it. They have the best damn oatmeal...actually that's the name given to their oatmeal, but it's pretty darn good. Also, they have really good iced coffee. Extra bonus, they accept the Axxess card.

Don't get what all the hype is.  Food came out cold, Mac and cheese had no flavor, bits of bacon for a "side of bacon". My husband and I felt sick all day after eating here. Seating is terrible. Obviously won't be going back here.

Disappointing. Tables were not clean. I sat at a dirty table the entire time I waited for my order and even after it came out. Some patrons had resorted to clearing their own tables. Since the party before me had left a considerable mess I did not have the means to bus it myself. When I had asked for help earlier the waitress brushed off my request. No apologies given when it finally was cleaned up. 

I had the Salmon Tugboat. Salmon was tough in areas and I was not impressed.

This is a little over due....but ! Never to late. I had my wedding rehearsal brunch with The Shop cafe on October 10th. Everything was amazing ! Food was so good ! Service was great ! Drinks were always full - literally couldn't have asked for a better experience. Mind you we were a group of 23 ranging from ages 2 years old - 80 years old, everyone left satisfied. 

The owner I wish I knew his name was so helpful. We contacted him literally a week before the event and he made sure he would accommodate us on such last minute. We had so much going on with our wedding that this was last one our list out of our 1000000 things to do. But to be honest this might have been our favorite event. Being at a ONE huge table with 23 of your closet friends and family with amazing food and drinks in beautiful Santa Barbara , what more could we have asked for ? 

Me writing this review says a lot , my husband and I are in the hospitality industry so we critique ever last thing and really I have nothing bad to say about this establishment except I wish you guys were in Los Angeles ;) 

HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!! We will be back :)

I wanted to follow up on my wife's comments about the Shop Cafe.  We had the perfect morning-after wedding brunch for 22 friends and family.  What a spectacular way to celebrate our wedding!  Chris was great both during planning and throughout the meal.  In the time leading up to the event, he was extremely responsive (which was important because we were planning from 300 miles away) and had helpful suggestions. The service was great, and most importantly the food was awesome.  I've been to the Shop Café four times, and never had a less than stellar meal (the just the tip sandwich can't be beat!).  The location is great - our outdoor seating allowed us to enjoy the perfect Santa Barbara day.  From all the positive Yelp reviews, it is clear that SB already knows that the Shop Cafe makes good food, but they are great for hosting large events too!

When visiting SB with friends recently, I was tasked with finding a place for breakfast. The Yelp reviews for The Shop Cafe led us here and we were glad they did! This place was delightful! The menu was creative, with a healthy-alternative focus and great eye-appeal.  When the food arrived, the portions were generous and tasty. All four of us enjoyed our meals, from the Yogi yogurt to the pancakes, to the Eggs Benedict and the Rolex. And I got "kudos" for a great pick! Note: orders are placed at a walk-up window and seating is outside, mostly picnic benches under patio umbrellas, separated from busy Milpas by a low fence and some vegetation. We enjoyed the setting on a quiet Saturday morning.

Delicious! I was looking for a breakfast place and saw  some pictures of some of the plates and decided to try it without looking at the menu.  I was surprised to see how creative the menu was and really enjoyed the food!

I expected that it would be a sit-down type of restaurant, but you order the food at the window which is later brought to the table.  The food is prepared in the kitchen which could be seen entirely through a large window. My friend and I ordered the Tug Boat breakfast, which was similar to an eggs Benedict w a California twist. My friend had it with the maple bacon and I had it with fried chicken and they were delicious! 

There is inside and outside seating and under the perfect Santa Barbara weather, how couldn't we sit outside?  This was a great find! Great food and great people working behind the window!

This is a very hip funky place I believe it used to be a tire store now they serve Gourmet foods that are very original and affordable. If you want to have some fun try their Mac on crack. It's outstanding.
went again yesterday omg loved the poached eggs on salmon their toast was soooo good seasoned just right every bite was heavenly. thanks again guys but try to open at 630 am for us early workers
Favorite place for breakfast when visiting Santa Barbara. YOLO is the best thing on the menu I've tried so far.

We had our post-wedding brunch at The Shop Cafe and it was awesome! For a group of 20, seating, service, and food were all fantastic. Chris was very easy to work with during the planning period; we were able to set the menu we wanted, reserve two great tables outdoors, and hang out for as long as we wanted. For anyone looking for a fun, relaxed spot for a group brunch or lunch, I'd highly recommend The Shop Cafe. Everyone had a lot of fun and no one left hungry!

Ah, Yelp made the Shop Cafe look so amazing. And I'm sure most dishes are pretty good, but what I ordered I couldn't finish. That made me sad. 

I had the Tugboat with tomato. All the tugboat options look so good! And if I was a normal human being, I wouldn't complain. But, I'm weird and I didn't like the biscuit the Tugboat comes with. For some reason it was just too doughy, as if it wasn't cooked all the way. But, the two organic eggs were great! 

Also, the lemonade was delicious. 

I would still come back to try something else.
Living in Santa Barbara there are many restaurants to choose from. I came through Groupon and what an amazing spot to have found. I will return, the food is delicious!
Love this little gem. Yummy & pretty healthy! The location is nothing fancy, but don't let that deter you. Its a fav for sure!
the breakfast sandwiches are amazing and the coffee is delicious too. great value for the quality.  my breakfast sandwich can usually double as much too as is so filling and rich.

Don't let the ordering from a window fool you ! This was the best breakfast I've had in a long time. My hubby had the veggie eggs Benedict I had the YOLO (chicken biscuit & Gravy). The food came out fast and the outside sitting experience made it very enjoyable for our son. Highly recommended for couples and families.
The food here is killer. Fresh salads, amazing sandwiches, outstanding attitudes. This place rocks!

Looking for a service-light, outdoors-friendly, small-ish place for breakfast? The girls and I wanted something "healthy" so we came to The Shop.

The Shop is what out of towners usually think of when you say "California." They have delicious and plenty of hot drinks (I thoroughly enjoyed my chai latte). They don't have nonfat milk, so the sweet cashier offered to mix the skim and 2% for me. There was a long line for breakfast around 10-11AM Sunday morning, but the line moves fast. 

The poor cashier girl was swamped that morning we went. They were understaffed for the cashier spots, but the kitchen seemed to be functioning fine! I love their glass windows so you can see your food (drinks AND brunch) items being made in real time. Ingredients are absolutely the fresh-est and delicious. Service was on point that morning we went. They have food runners that bring your food out to your table, and even after we all finished our breakfast, one sweet boy went to our table to ask us how we were doing!! That's awesome considering that The Shop isn't really a full service spot--and people were just lounging in their exercise gear on a lazy Sunday morning! Props.

I loved my delicious "Good morning Sunshine" kale salad. I was afraid that the feta would be too strong, but it was superb. The runny egg really made my salad POP in a good way. We sat at an outdoor picnic table (limited, so first come first reserve!) and enjoyed being in that intimate space with a bunch of other diners. The one thing I hated were the annoying buzzing flies around us. There's nothing much to be done, but maybe place some fans around the patio so the flies leave us diners alone! Otherwise, they are dog-friendly, kid-friendly, and even accommodate for larger parties with their seats. They also have indoor seating, but most people want to sit outside during brunch time. Pricing is on the lower side for brunch spots in Socal...or even in SB in general. I'd totally come back here again.

This place is the bomb. We leave Happy every tym. Best french toast in the fn world. The burgers tuck u in and GENTLY kiss u on the forehead. If you dont like french toast there then you hecking get OUT! Drinks were yum and environment sweet and pleasant

I have been here 3 times this week.... I got the yolo twice and the tri-tip sandwich once..

In the yolo, I have never had a better piece of fried chicken. It is just perfect, juicy and tender. I had a bite of my friends chicken sandwich with the strawberry bbq sauce and I have to say, it may be the best thing I have tried there. It is definitely what I am getting next time I go for lunch.

The food is great, with fantastic service and friendly people. HIghly recommended.

Split the refreshing General Sanders (burger) and the not-so-hot Tugboat (eggs benedict) with shop-cured salmon. The burger loaded with juicy fried chicken and apple cole slaw was phenomenal but the chips were stale. The eggs benedict was also a little too much on the raw side with the egg yolk and salmon. I think it would be better if you get it with a different kind of meat like fried chicken or carnitas.

All-in-all, it was great but be sure to be quick about snagging outdoor seating; it's much nicer than sitting inside.

Wow. What a great surprise. After hearing about this little hole in the wall I visited one Sunday morning with a group of friends. Everyone at the table was happy with the food, and my shrimp with grits was truly outstanding. The portion was reasonable, not too much, the quality of the sauce was very good, and the grits were quite creamy and delicious, better than usual. The grits were more like a polenta. I ordered lemonade which was perfect. I will be back for sure.
The eastside with carnitas was delicious... the meat was very tender, poached eggs was cooked perfectly. I had the macchiato and it was delicious and strong!

My husband and I would frequent this cafe for breakfast and I would order Salmon-in-Yo-Face and he would order YOLO. The salmon dish was served with a decent slices of cured salmon, paired nicely with  with red onion and capers, and topped with perfectly poached egg. 

The YOLO dish was this delicious combo of sausage gravy, tender fried chicken, and warm buttermilk biscuit - this was my husband's favorite biscuit & gravy dish in town. Unfortunately, they've since changed the menu and this YOLO is no longer the same - the gravy is not as flavorful and the fried chicken was little dry. 

We went there recently and tried their new menu. I tried their Mac on Crack - it was OKAY, nothing crazy about this dish. The mac & cheese was bland tasting and it was strange with tartness from the slices of apple. If anything and you want to just sample, order a side bowl of it. 

My husband tried the General Sanders and that was good. The fried chicken was cooked nicely and went nicely with the apple sale and spicy mayo. I would order that next time over the mac & cheese. 

I think their drinks are a little on the expensive side - orange juice and smoothie that was not all that special - just your basic fruits blended together. They have outdoor seating which is dog-friendly and self-serving with utensils and all.

Very delicious food with cute outdoor seating. It's probably a 4.5 star. If the OJ was only from fresh oranges and didn't taste like it had a little bit of the bottle OJ juice mixed in it, I'd probably give a 5. 
I ordered the bacon tugboat and just the tip. Both were good.

Well. Two poached eggs, a slice of toast, a deep dish  bowl of thankfully not-so-greasy homefries or quartered potatoes of some sort: cost $1.00 maybe = price  $11.00. They've done a nice job with the al fresco seating. I  would not want to eat indoors there. Alll in all, reasonably pleasant on a warm morning, but nothing that really brings me back. Also, I'm  obliged to share that I was joined for breakfast by a rather pesky fly.
Great little place for breakfast! Nice staff! Small menu which makes it even better! Michalda that my husband had was tasty!!!

We came here after seeing them on Yelp and it was a great decision! I had the Tugboat with salmon. The salmon was cured and lovely. My friends had the Tugboat with apple bacon and the other had the Eastside toast. Every be loved their breakfast!

After scouring the reviews on Yelp for a place in SB with solid food and a decent price, I thought I'd check out The Shop Cafe and it didn't disappoint. The menu is a new twist on comfort foods and the location is walk-up diner with the benefit of a huge patio and super friendly staff. 

I ordered the Sweet Maria and it was really tasty. It was definitely more than your average barbecue chicken sandwich. The strawberry bbq sauce was the perfect compliment to the smokey flavor of grilled chicken and onions topped with smoked mozzarella. The sauce wasn't too sweet or too tangy and had just a slight hint of strawberry. And anyone who appreciates a good sandwich knows it's all about the bread, which is made in-house at the Shop and sealed the deal for me. 

My friend ordered the YOLO and was jonesing for another by the time we got home. The chicken was crispy, the biscuit was fluffy and griddled, and the whole thing was smothered in gravy. What's not to like? 

My only regret is the place is so far away from where I live. I'll definitely be stopping by The Shop again as soon as I can find another reason to get down to Santa Barbara.
Interesting variety but so far not that great for me and my friend. I'll check today and see if the eggs are hot on my breakfast sandwich.

Absolutely love frequenting The Shop! What a great place to go for breakfast. The fried chicken tugboat is one of my favorites. I love their bulletproof coffee (only downside is I wish they would blend it just a litttttle bit more because it separates!). Second best would be the kale salad with bacon.
I definitely recommend going to the Shop if you're into really yummy food and a local SB spot.

went here for the first time yesterday after hearing about it from a friend.  Had  the shrimp po-boy ( a special, not on the menu but it should be) with crispy shrimp, a smoky sauce and fabulous fresh bread. We also ordered fries, and after they were all gone my husband was still scooping out the homemade ketchup and eating it on its own.  My friend had the tri tip sandwich and liked that too. We will come back and try breakfast next.
I had the Yolo. Delicious! My husband got the Salmon in Yo Face and it was yummy too. It's a place we would definitely come back to if we are ever traveling this way.
I had the carnitas tugboat and it was honestly one of the best eggs bennys I've had. Definitely recommend.

The main reason for trying this place was the whole wheat chapati used in the "rollex". The chapati is an Indian flatbread that is thin like a crepe. The dark wheat-flavored chapati was used to create a breakfast omelet wrap that was highlighted by a bright smoked tomato sauce. The bacon and egg were also good, but the avocado was awkwardly big.

The "yolo" had buttermilk fried chicken that was thin like a chicken fried steak, slightly curdled flavorful gravy, an overcooked poached egg, and a biscuit that reminded of campsite quick bread cooked in a skillet. The "rollex" was better than the "yolo".

We started by sitting outside, but moved indoors when the odor of a nearby dumpster fouled the air.
Cute little spot with amazing food .  Everything on the menu looks good and the service was quick . The chilaquiles were so delicious!

Ridiculously good. Was in town for just one night/day so yelped for a good breakfast spot and found this place. Great menu, but went a la carte with a fried chicken, two soft poached eggs and guacamole. Threw in some honey and Cholula and it was pretty much perfect. If I'm ever in Santa Barbara again, I'd definitely come here.

Great little brunch spot! Order at counter and they bring the food out to you, drinks come out on the side window and you self grab. 
Had the tug boat egg Benedict with fried chicken, the eggs were perfectly poached and came on top of home made biscuits and avocado, amazing and highly recommended! Get the side of potatoes too for $5! They have great mimosas (mostly champagne and splash of orange juice), others got spicy bloody and loved it! Will definitely be back when I visit SB

Honestly i didnt know what to expect however all tje reviews indocated this is the place to eat so here we are.  Now onto the food, the tugboat and sweetcakes rocked. I would highly suggest getting these.
I WILL BE BACK!

We at breakfast at the Shop Kitchen this morning.  We had the salmon tugboat.  Their version of Eggs Benedict.  They serve it on a biscuit with avocado and hollandaise sauce.  The salmon was super fresh and the portions were generous.  We enjoyed it.  The biscuits as a little heavy on the stomach, post meal.
Had the Frenchie and it was really good. The whip cream had an interesting flavor but good nonetheless. I definitely want to try other things in their menu when I visit Santa Barbara soon

This is a delicious and casual food stop. You park on the street, order at the window, and you pick either an indoor our outdoor table where they bring the food to you.

I had the In Yo Face Egg, with avocado added, and it was simple but hit the spot.   I wish I had space to try their Eggs Benedict too...but I'll just have to pay them another visit on my next trip to Santa Barabara!  My husband had their Fried Chicken with an added egg.  The chicken was very tasty - my guess is maybe it's a free range chicken that they tenderized? It was a tad tougher, however a very tasty meat.  It was well marinated and fried, and it was drenched in gravy and came with a biscuit. I was pretty sure my husband could not finish it - but finish it he did.  I kept on grabbing more bites of it myself before it was gone.  Our 5 year old son was happy with eating from both our plates as well.

Long line for Sunday brunch hours. This is usually a good sign! 

Tugboat w/ salmon- 4 stars; not my order but from what I tasted, it was a pretty good benedict. The only thing was they forgot the sauce at the beginning and it had to be asked for. Benedicts are not usually my thing but it was good. 

Just the tip- 5 stars; tip sandwich with cheese and carmelized onions. I tend to avoid onions overall but the caramelized onions gave a sweet taste to the sandwich and it was good. Just oozing goodness. It came with a side of chips. 

Had a patio and indoor seating area. Self serve for coffee complements, water and utensils.

800 mile road trip and this is our best meal yet! Found them here on Yelp and our experience was even better than the pics and reviews. A fun cafeteria style diner I highly recommend adding to your itinerary.
The Shop Cafe is a great place to eat, I have only been there for breakfast and it is spectacular. I got" the best damn oatmeal" and it was superb, I will definitely come again.
Found this place in Groupon and was glad I came. Food portions were big and the taste was great. I am a very satisfied customer.

Good food but pricey, $15+ for a chicken sandwich and a non-refillable drink is even overpriced for a place with no parking.

Expecting tip (which the default is set on 20 or 15 percent) and the person charging the card also reminds you, for just handing you a pricey sandwich shouldn't be a good idea.

I'm working nearby and could be a regular customer but going there whenever I'm bored of other fast foods around.
Had an amazing breakfast! I had the Tugboat with the maple bacon and my husband had The Frenchie! Would definitely drive back up for breakfast!

Gorgeous patio outside for the perfect Sunday Brunch! You order at the cashier window and then you can sit down anywhere with your number stand so they can deliver the food to you. Food came out abnormally fast! 

Get the Rollex. The wrap is slightly fluffy with a light crisp. Seriously, it tastes homemade. Ingredients were evenly distributed and not falling right out of the wrap. 

Another yummy one was the Just the Tip Tri-tip sandwich. Tender meat, not too dry. The  ciabatta bread with the onion spread was perfect! The right amount of sauce just to complement the meat.

Out of these two options, I would choose the Rollex.

I love The Shop Café! Anything you get will be yummy and there are choices that will satisfy vegetarian/vegan appetite.  I have been waiting for a place like this to pop up on Milpas, there are not many places you can go to for good coffee, I wish they were open later in the day even if it was just for Coffee:)
Weeks later, I'm still dreaming about this place. I had banana, honey, and almond butter on a biscuit and I'm telling you, as weird as it sounds, I'm dieing to go back!

Holy fucking shit! I'm so glad I stumbled across this spot because I had the best freaking breakfast ever. I'm usually not even a fan of breakfast but once I saw the fried chicken Benedict I was like... I need this in my life. It was everything I imagined... the chicken was fried to perfection and i believe it was Panko battered. The biscuit that it was on was so bomb especially with the avocado! I had an English breakfast tea with it (yum!!) and my bf had the fried chicken in gravy with biscuit .. which I may add was also very very good.

So glad my friends told me about this place! It is soooo tasty.  I had the "just the tip" which is their tritip sandwich. I was a little unsure about the wasabi creme fraiche it came with but they put it on the side.  I ended up slathering my sandwich with it all.

The vibe of the place is great.  Walk up window to order with a super friendly staff.  The menu board and overall branding is great.  Felt like I was in another city, like Portland, and not on Milpas Street.  

My friends got the Shop Burger and the Big Salad. Both looked fabulous.  The lemonade was great. Sat out on the patio on a warm day and really took in the atmosphere.  

Can't wait to go back and try more. The combinations of ingredients were not things I would think of, but after having this one sandwich, I trust their judgement. They had items such as "strawberry bbq sauce" that we sampled for fries and it was very tasty.  

They also had amazing sounding breakfast.  They add mascarpone to their oatmeal, which is genius - I might have to do that myself.  Their biscuits were gigantic and were calling out to me, but I needed to save them for another time.  

All around great place, the staff is so nice, the food is excellent and fresh.  Only open for breakfast and lunch.

Me and my husband used a Groupon for our breakfast. It was a great deal and would definitely go here again. I had the Yolo with a mimosa. That was delicious but far too much food for one person. It was extremely heavy but none the less amazing. My husband had to finish it for me. And my husband had the pulled pork eggs Benedict. They were sooo good. The pork was the best part. It tasted like it was slow cooking for a long time. Will definitely be back.

Why have I never heard of this place? 

Came here on a Saturday afternoon, with beautiful weather.  We just couldn't decide what to order. Actually, I forgot what I ordered but I remember we accidentally ordered a salad. We thought it was breakfast-y item, but it was just a salad with a poached egg. Nonetheless, the salad was so amazing! Had squash, dinosaur kale, poached egg. I could eat it forever.


We also got the mac n cheese. It was really good but in my opinion, it could've done without the bacon.

I def am going to come back. Probably try the rolex. 


BUT SERIOUSLY, why wasn't this under my food radar?!
We had the Ahnold for breakfast. It's great with mixed greens as a side. Only seating is outdoors which is great because weather is perfect!

one of my favorite breakfast places in SB! love the causal style and food. I wish they didn't remove the veggies in yo face though :( but when the owner was there he still made it for me! Love this place!

SO GOOD!
I have been here at least 10 times and every time I get something different that I absolutely love. It has amazing service with a very welcoming vibe and the food is out of control. 
There are a wide variety of items and they are constantly coming up with new items which are never a disappointment. I bring friends whenever they are in town and they are always so pleased. The "Tugboat"- their version of eggs benedict- is my favorite and amazing along with everything else I've tried. Along with the classic biscuit with honey and butter.

I was in need of some decent breakfast on Milpas, and found this place on Yelp.

I ordered the salmon and a coffee. I think I paid $13 total. I picked up an Independant paper and there was some good music in the background. I waited a reasonable amount of time. The ingredients are pretty good. 

The guy who served me was nice, Chris. He's very on top of things. He had a black beard with a few white hairs. Looked like a true local.

The food was really delicious. The only thing is that the portion was a bit small. I was still kinda hungry afterwards. It was delicious though.

Came by the other day both wife and I ordered the salmon Benedict. The helping of home made cured salmon was great, covered with Hollandaise on home made biscuits was almost too much to eat. But we both managed somehow.  You order at the window and they will bring you the food served on the picnic benches outside. Prices are moderate, and a good value. Only down side is the parking in front is limited to 15 minutes unless you can find parking in back on the street.
Definite return.

My husband and 18 month old stopped in here this morning. Food was good and it was fun atmosphere. My only complaints were that thru ran out of kid friendly food and it was 11:30a. No pancakes, no muffins. The bacon was underdone and seating is tight enough that we had to ask to sit at a table with other patrons. (Super crowded on weekends, obv.) In the end I'd probably come back because it was unique.

Mac on Crack:  pasta with gorgonzola and chopped apples.  It sounded odd but I had to try it because I love the ingredients separately and I was charmed by the name.  Very worthy of its name.  I combine these ingredients myself at home now, but it's not as good as The Shop. A Milpas corridor business to support.

For a laid back outside breakfast spot, this place can't be beat when it comes to the hearty and classic style food. I had the Eggs Benedict with ham and tomato on a biscuit and couldn't finish it, which never happens because I love my eggs Benny. I took it home because I couldn't imagine not finishing it. You will love it, and it's a good start to your SB sunny day. It's dog friendly too so it's nice to pup watch. I'd go again for sure.

Terrible service and overpriced burnt coffee.  People behind window were not friendly- never going back.

Went when they were just starting up- maybe they have their act together now?

In my opinion, the Chilaquiles were just an illusion. They looked so great and I was so excited when I got it, but I didn't like them. Maybe you will like them more than me! I would have given them 1 star. But this place seems really nice environmentally and menu wise, and if I happen to go there again I will update my review. Awesome that they had Bulletproof coffee.

My first time eating at The shop was an average experience.  The good; friendly service, food came out quick, and really nice outdoor eating area. The bad; chicken in benedict was not cooked fully. 

I did get to try the French toast and chicken, that was fully cooked and tasted great.  

I may have just got unlucky....
Excellent place for brunch! A SB local told us about this place and it did not disappoint. Everything is fresh and delicious with a cool little outdoor seating area to enjoy the perfect weather.

"Mac on crack" and "just the tip" as names of great food is what sums up what makes this place great. Not cheap but quality that is on par with expensive restaurants that would charge you far more. You won't be disappointed and scott, who was at the window, was friendly and quick to figure out based on our tastes what we should go with. 
Try it, you'll sing there praises too.

We were heading back to SF from SB and yelped this place. It was, in a word, PERFECT for breakfast. Great vibe, good music playing on the outdoor sound system, and, most important, great food. I had French toast with bananas and strawberries with basil whipped cream and real maple syrup.  Husband had In-Yo-Face salmon with a poached egg and fried capers, red onion, and dill creme fraiche. Oh, and we ordered a side of bacon which was cooked to perfection and delicious; it came with honey drizzled over it which I didn't particularly want but could deal with. The outdoor tables are separated from the street by a hedge, which I liked because it made the space seem a little more private and blocked the exhaust fumes. Also, great coffee. Added attraction: across the street is a used car dealer that sells mostly vintage high-end and/or obscure cars (Bentley, Rolls Royce, Porsche 911, Morris Minor woody, etc.) and the owner was super friendly and knowledgeable.  If I'm ever in SB again I will definitely return here for breakfast.
We had the tugboat, and it was scrumptious. The hollandaise was smokey, and biscuit was tender. Perfectly boiled eggs. Super friendly.

It's just after 8 am while I wrote this review - Well...the food looks great on the menu but the ambiance was not what I expected. For a $27.00 breakfast with no drinks and only water, I expect a little different of an experience. 

We decided to come here because of the reviews and menu but no one mentioned that at 8 am in Santa Barbara, on a Sunday morning, we'd be sitting outside with Michael Jackson blasting "Gotta be Starting Something"...in the background ... not what I was hoping for in the back grown with these views!!

Next song... "Superstition" ... still not the selections that go with the scene here- In my opinion. 

So the outside is a nice, quaint set up with umbrellas and and nice breeze.

The inside sitting area is not exactly appetizing. Maybe if the sun was shining in? I'll take a picture...

They serve water in cute little stainless steel glasses...I like that touch.

Next song "Jesses Girl".... 

Maybe it's just that the music is too loud. It's like Entertainment and foreground rather than background music. Hey but maybe that's what they are going for???



Also- something I found odd was the bathroom situation. When we were getting water, someone came out of hr bathroom and walked to the place where utensils and napkins were to grab a napkin to dry his hands?! Nothing in bathroom to dry hands with? Went in later and there were paper towels. The door was also quite beat up. 

My favorite song is playing now but I still don't want to hear it right now at this time !! Maybe at dinner time? " Summer of 69"... love it in the car and out at night but not at breakfast during relax and conversation time.

This yelp is distracting me just enough to tolerate waiting for the food . If a nice soft and easy music selection was playing, I might be holding hands, talking and enjoying a nice coffee but we may have to get the food to go at this point. I'm not one to ask a restaurant to change their music when it is possibly what others like and are accustomed to here on Sunday morning...

Whew what song is next??? 

Wait for it!!! Oh this is a GOOD one....

"Shock to heart" - nothing like a little Bon Jovi to get the conversation going in the morning. Maybe I should just go for a jog around the restaurant because that's what I should be doing to this music. 

Ok food is here! I'm gonna eat and review the food next. 

I'm gonna go grab the silverware now at the counter.  

That I don't mind but you'd think the food runner might offer if we forgot to do it...

Ha - stand by for the food.

Finally a song that makes sense! Perfect timing!! Did they see me writing this??? 

"My girl..." by I think the Coasters?!! Ahhh food looks great!!!

Ok the food was good. I loved my Benedict. The Chilaquiles was underwhelming but edible. 

We could still smell the sealant on the tables outside and the didn't wipe them down which I thought was strange for a restaurant. At the least someone would wipe down the tables right? 

Very popular spot. I know now how to describe it /what to expect... and now you do too!!

I have only tried lunch, not breakfast and after reading reviews looks like I need to at least give it one more shot for breakfast. I REALLY wanted to like this place because it is super cute and I've heard great things. Perhaps it is a good place, but just not a good fit for me.

It looks like a lot of thought was put into the menu but the menu is limited. None of the sandwiches really called out to me, I usually like savory for lunch so adding strawberry bbq sauce or apple slaw to my sandwich doesn't appeal.

General Sanders: Fried chicken was good, I wasn't a huge fan of the bun (it's sheer size overpowered the chicken, i wasn't sure there was any chicken in there), I ate the slaw separately.

The Tijuana: Probably the healthiest option, it was lacking and the chicken was a little dry.

Sweet Maria: Gouda was a little overpowering, and again I'm not a huge fan of sweet in my sandwiches.

Fries and Onion Strings: YUM, extra crispy made to order and onion string deliciousness.

This excellent New American eatery serves fantastic breakfast and lunch. Our party had the Eggs-in-yo-Face (perfectly poached egg atop thick toast; they added crumbled bacon to mine), YOLO (biscuit in a rich, savory gravy topped with phenomenal fried chicken), Bananas-in-yo-face (thick toast with house-made almond butter, honey and bananas), and the Rollex (Scrambled eggs, bacon, smoked tomato spread & avocado wrapped in chapati). The food was perfect, staff great and outdoor seating was just what we needed.

Eat here... eat here now. Early morning breakfast so we were here when it opened and got the Banana toast, the Frenchie with chicken, and the sunshine bowl.Every single thing was delicious. The banana toast stayed crispy even after layers of almond butter, bananas, and honey smothered it while we ate the other things and the fresh almond butter gave it an added crunch. The chicken and french toast- SAME! Crispy chicken and french toast drizzled in sweet syrup. Yum. Hard to rate (and eat) a salad after that but they got it right with the ingredients which complimented each other wonderfully. With only outdoor seating it's a beautiful place to have breakfast (and it's cool and overcast today). Go!

This is one of my favorite places in Santa Barbara. I come here for breakfast every couple of weeks and have had almost all the items in the menu. Everything is fantastic, but my favorite dish in the Bananas In Yo Face.

Decent brunch spot in Santa Barbara.

The flow is a little odd, and we had to ask people if they were in line or waiting for a table. We ordered our Mac on Crack and Tugboat Carnitas and drinks from a walk-up window, first. It was a gorgeous Sunday in SB, so there were no available tables outside. We ended up going inside, which was cold with concrete everywhere. I had to walk back outside and around the line of people waiting to order, to get our drinks that were sitting outside of another window. The carnitas tasted great on top of their biscuits, though. The Mac on Crack was a little soupy thanks to the bechamel sauce, but it still tasted fine. The iced tea was okay, but had an aftertaste like it was run through the same machine as the coffee.

Awesome joint! Great food with a order them sit style, with an outdoor patio off milpas. Did not get here on time for breakfast but ordered lunch instead and everything was amazing. The general sanders is also bomb, they are very proud of their fried chicken. I highly recommend this place for breakfast or lunch.

Came here for lunch and I don't really have much to comment on in terms of the food. It was decent. I had the fried chicken burger and also the salmon dish. 

But I'm really leaving a review because of the shady practise the girl at the cashier uses when you order your food. It's one of those payment system where they turn the tablet around and you sign your name. When I ordered, she swiped my card and turned the tablet around and just said "sign here". Of course all I saw was the line and signed my name.

It was not until I received my food when I took a look at the receipt and noticed that I paid 25% tips for the meal!!!! I was shocked and felt completely duped. It is so shady that they choose the tip % for you before they turn the tablet around. I didn't feel like confronting them but seriously, if management sees this, you need to stop this shady practise. We are paying for the food and we should choose the amount. Never choose it for the customer please. 

TLDR: Cashier chooses the tip % (25%) on the screen before you pay, make sure you watch the monitor closely. Shady stuff.

This place is a food gold mine! 

Hot, delicious, and fun.

The location is hard to find if you're using GPS. You'll see a mechanic's shop, but the restaurant is a little hidden. The patio umbrellas and people eating are what tipped it off for me (I thought it was a waiting area for the garage).

Anyway, I had the YOLO, which was fried chicken with biscuits and gravy. A lot of gravy. A LOT OF GRAVY. I think they could've used a little less but hey, you only live once!

Next time, I look forward to trying their other breakfast dishes. I loved the friendly service and the obvious pride they take in their food. The premises were clean and no-nonsense.

I can't wait to go back!
Such creative meals with so much awesome flavor! A local spot that no one should miss out on! The Rollex is a weekly treat as well as the Just the Tip sandwich. You can't go wrong worth is place.

My Daughter is a regular here and loves it, so much so she suggested we go here on Mother's Day while I visited Santa Barbara. 
They were so ill prepared for the volume obviously, we waited forever for our food and it was frozen when it arrived.  I was more disappointed for my Daughter who wanted everything to be special for me. Very sad as she tells me it's usually excellent.

My wife and I found this place thru Yelp as we always do whenever we travel and again we found the best place. OMG  the food is absolutely incredible and pretty much all made on premises. My wife had the Yoghurt "home made" it was so light and so good I could had one myself as well. I had the "in your face salmon"   Unbelievable!!!  from the well toasted bread to the house cured salmon, the perfect poached eggs this whole combo was the best I have ever had. The French press coffee is the perfect extra touch.
We liked it so much it did not take us long to figure out where to go for breakfast the next morning. Our second experience was just as memorable as the first one.
My compliment to the Owners Dudley and his partner. We wish you all the success you deserve.

I tried this place for lunch on a lunch break and was hoping for better things. I get a fairly long lunch, but most of that time was spent waiting so if you are on a time crunch, might be a issue. Food looked and sounded promising as we ordered the sweet maria and just the tip sandwich with a side of mac and cheese which we split.  The first couple bites of the sweet maria, all I tasted was grilled onions, but was hoping to get some of their strawberry bbq or chicken with no luck.  The "just the tip" sandwich seemed promising after the first couple bites, but after so long, it was just too greasy to enjoy. The tr-tip was not dried out at all, but the grease seeped to the bread, lettuce and just made it soggy and unenjoyable to the point where we went hungry for lunch.

Came here after needing a place to eat on the road and found this on yelp. The employees were so knowledgable on the food and its background and seemed genuinely excited about it, which was a great change of pace. The food was spectacular and the ambience was lovely as well. A very care free, relaxing place to go. I was especially impressed by not only the person working the register but the people who brought us our food were just as friendly, helpful and pleasant. I will come back every time I am in the area!

Breakfast/Brunch date with my girlfriend. We enjoyed it!!! Line was fast, don't be intimidated by the line. Food was unique, delicious and a a perfect portion. The cashier was cordial, friendly and patient. Coffee was good as well, just wished they had soy milk as an option though they did have almond milk.  Seating is very limited, you can share tables with other people but looks like they need a lot more space. It's dog friendly and location is small. Worth the visit if you're in town.

Yum!! It was so hard to choose what to get here, everything sounded/looked amazing! My boyfriend got the Salmon In Yo Face (with eggs on top), & I got The Sando (ham & egg sandwich with avocado). We also got a side of bacon, which was probably the BEST. BACON. IVE. EVER. HAD. 

Go here!



The end.

Literally had one of the best omelettes in my life at this place. I created my own egg white omelette with mushrooms and it was heavenly. The best part was the mushrooms, so fresh and delicious. My friend got the avocado toast and the good day sunshine salad - both so good! The environment was super cozy and the staff very friendly, I would definitely go back.

Delicious, fresh, delightful, all are words I'd use to describe our brunch! Highly recommend this spot if you're looking for an off the beaten path eatery in SB! We ordered the Salmon with two poached eggs and the vegetable scramble along with two organic lattes with almond milk. It was the prefect combo!

The Shop Kitchen was not all its cracked up to be!  I had the shrimp and grits. The grits were good, but the shrimp was uncooked and not seasoned.  I sent it back, but it came back pretty much the same way.  Other things on the menu may be great, but I don't recommend the shrimp and grits!!
great little spot on milpas... nice people, great food and really affordable. love the creativity. delicious and awesome outside seating area. highly recommended.

They reduce bacon infused chicken broth for hours for the super savory gravy that is the star of the YOLO... A delicious biscuit topped with fried chicken that floats atop a generous bowlful of gravy.  Oh, and don't forget to add a poached egg or two!

Other honorable mentions: 
Just the Tip - tri tip steak sandwich with caramelized onions and a horseradish sauce
Jean Claude Van Hamme - ham, Brie and honey goodness!
Oatmeal - not comparable to the amazing chef creations above, but very well made for just being oatmeal.

On top of all that, this place takes Axxess (buy one get one free)!
Awesome, thoughtfully crafted food. Had the granola & coffee for breakfast. Yummy!Friendly service. Dog friendly on the patio!

I've looked for an excuse to make my way over to Milpas and eat at The Shop for a while now, and my first experience was a delight! This place has the makes of a Santa Barbara staple and certainly adds to the quirky, Milpas Street experience. It's a pleasant break from all the great Mexican food of Santa Barbara. The Shop provides a friendly atmosphere with outdoor seating and tasteful, affordable food. The website advertises that it serves "slow food, fast," and I certainly found this to be true. My food was light, never over seasoned or over cooked. I left with leftovers feeling full and refreshed. With an affordable place like this, don't hesitate to spring for the fresh-squeezed lemonade and dessert. I got a brown sugar shortbread cookie that was to die for! Besides having a great product, though, The Shop has great service. By my second visit, the owner introduced himself - and I even got to meet his adorable dog, a big plus for a pet lover like me! My only complaint about The Shop is that they're not open for dinner. The Shop certainly deserves your business not only for the owner and the owner's family hardworking in getting this place off the ground (opening a restaurant is never an easy task) and the excellent food they deliver.

very good brunch place in downtown sb. the workers are very nice and the owner is very passionate about his place. the food here is really good; you can't go wrong with anything on the menu. i love how its really customizable, especially the benedicts. the way that the restaurant works is very efficient, you order at a counter and they bring the food to your table. if you want a good brunch and you need to be in and out of a place by an hour, this would be a great place to go. also they serve green star coffee, which i love

The only reason I didn't give this place 1 star is because it seems like this place is recognized for their breakfast menu.

I came here to have lunch 45 minutes before the place closed because I was nearby. I ordered the Mac on Crack and my girlfriend ordered the Souper Cheesy. Both of these menu options were terrible. The soup had no flavor and tasted like water. My Mac on Crack tasted horrific. I'm not exaggerating when I say I almost vomited. To top this all off, they have water and water cups outside that is self serve. This water tasted like metal and I'd rather remain dehydrated then continue to drink more.

It's been a little over 48 hours and I STILL can't get this deliciousness out of my head. If you're looking for a tasty breakfast spot with a chill vibe, this is the place. We ordered the Chilaquiles and the Tugboat and shared the two. You can't go wrong with either. We added salmon on our Tugboat and I'm drooling over the memory of this dish. I may want to try the Tugboat with the fried chicken next time but the salmon was delightful. I need to stop with this review and grab some lunch before I completely drool all over myself. Check this place out!

This small place is known for breakfast/brunch. Order at the counter and enjoy their outdoor patio. The Eggs Benedict comes on a biscuit and does not disappoint. They could go lighter on the hollandaise sauce so if you don't like a lot of sauce ask for it on the side. The baked goods are phenomenal and made in-house.

Love the outdoor concept & fun twist on classic brunch items! I had the fried chicken Benedict & was amazed at how much food I got!

The hollandaise was really yummy, but I could have used a touch more as the chicken was a bit too crunchy on the outside for me & needed more of that moisture. But the huge amount of avocado on my plate left nothing to complain about.

Order at the window and take your table style. They have outdoor and indoor(no air conditioning) seating. I ordered the tugboat with fried chicken, and my boyfriend ordered the tritip sandwich. The tugboat was ok. Just ok. The poached eggs were a little over done, and the fried chicken tried to have flavor, but just didn't succeed. I would give it a participation ribbon. No complaints about the hollandaise sauce. The biscuit was a tiny bit soggy in some parts and really dry in others, but no perfect balance was met. 
The bread that was used for the tri tip was delicious. The tri tip itself was somewhat dry. The onions has a tinge of bitter flavor. It was served with a wasabi sauce that was a little too viscous to be a good dip. 
The chips that came with the tri tip were fantastic. 
Would not come back, but it was a good meal if you're not looking for something that will wow your taste buds.

Meh.  Had great potential.  We had the Yolo and salmon in yo face.   The lox had no flavor and was gelatinous and only came with one egg.  The Yolo was missing something too...maybe an egg?  It was pricey for a walk up joint that is next to a tire shop that smells like a dumpster with Flys everywhere.

Great local place for breakfast or brunch!  I had the Sando and it was made with off the bone ham, fresh avocado, and the roll tasted homemade.  The wait was minor for 10am on Mother's Day!  Several of my companions had the Tugboat and thought it was great, with the heirloom tomatoes and the pork.

Why on earth would you ever want to eat here for breakfast? My girlfriend and I went there for breakfast and the woman who took our order couldn't of been any more friendlier - yes, I'm  being very sarcastic. We ordered our food at the window and she was acting as if she had more important things to do than serve us. Apparently customers aren't very important here. I ordered the chicken, gravy and biscuits as well as side dishes of potatoes and bacon. Our side dishes came out first without warning and the food felt like it took forever to be served. The best thing on the menu was the bacon . Even getting silverware was a hassle! The only person who was decent to us was a smiling woman who was cleaning up after us and she promptly provided us a box. Honestly, I ate there an hour ago and I feel gross and sluggish. Is this SB restaurant trying too hard to be like LA? Nice try but even similar restaurants in LA have better service and items on their menu. Definitely not worth it!
Salmon Tugboat with the sauce on the side. Delish!!! Too much breakfast for me so had the second half for breakfast this morning and was still scrumptious.
