I was visiting Santa Barbara for the first time and my friend decided to take me here for breakfast. I was not disappointed. I decided to go with the classic fried chicken tugboat. It was both beautiful and delicious. We ended up going back several times during my trip as i enjoyed it that much. I would definitely recommend this brunch spot for both locals and visitors.

Definitely a cute spot to come enjoy a nice outdoor breakfast, the iced coffee is really delicious and I'm not a coffee person. Ordered the Chilaquiles and they were yummy. Would definitely recommend to friends and family visiting Santa Barbara

Breakfast is one of those meals that is hit or miss. There's less range than lunch or dinner, and people are less inclined to be spendy at 8 or 9 in the morning. Shop Cafe impresses with a small but mighty menu that varies the classics nicely. From smoked salmon on toast to eggs with tomatoes to a creative breakfast salad bowl to muffins and biscuits and oatmeal and yogurt and fruit, you'll get the sweetness, savoriness, and saltiness that your system is craving. If it happens to be raining, as it was on a winter weekend, the outdoor patio stays fairly empty while the indoor area fills up with hungry eaters in groups of 2, 4, or more. 

Individual meals under $10 each come plated on white circles or squares with nice presentation and sensible seasoning. Breakfast isn't one of those meals where you want to be confronted with new spices or fancy techniques, and it's probably easier to give people what they want in big portion sizes than to have the culinary courage to go small and simple. Personally, I prefer small and simple and don't want a big breakfast to weigh me down when I have a long day of sightseeing planned. Shop Cafe, with its walk-up sidewalk ordering, efficient and unobtrusive kitchen, and clean indoor seating, made things easy, breezy, and healthy without being lightweight or inconsistent. A good bet, a safe rendezvous, an ample but not overwhelming morning meal. This is subtle stuff, but pretty significant if you'd like to start the morning off right.

We were looking for an outdoor brunch spot with ample seating and this place fit the bill! Their patio has many tables and lots of umbrellas that make for a cute ambience. Dog friendly as well. 

Overall, I thought the food was okay. It wasn't bad but nothing to write home about. I ordered the Frenchie with fruit. It wasn't too sweet which I liked and came topped with fresh banana, apples, and blueberries. My family got The Melt which looks like French toast with ham and cheese in the middle. The Frenchie with fried chicken is actually boneless chicken which makes it easy to eat. The salmon toast comes with a generous topping of salmon which is nice. 

There's street parking available nearby. There was a bit of a line when placed our order but service was quick.
This is such a cute location right next to a tire shop. Such a cute breakfast spot.

Ordered the eggs Benedict, oatmeal, and Rolex burrito. Food is so flavorless. They don't add seasonings at all it's so bland. The food looks good in pictures but not worth it. I'm sad i thought this food was about to be so good. Highly disappointed

This is a good spot located off milpas on the East side. It can get busy on the weekends so be prepared! The food is good both to eat there and to take out. This place serves as a breakfast brunch lunch time. The chilaquiles are delicious the only upside is that there is a sub charge if you want to add protein to the dish and these are chilaquiles for those that prefer their spiciness level on more of the mild side. The rollex is basically a breakfast wrap and I suggest getting a side of salsa or if you want to be experimental hollandaise sauce. I add chicken to it and split it with a friend. Half of it is pretty filling. The shrimp and grits are very flavorful and left me with wanting more. It's a good comfort food to have on a foggy Sunday morning. If you get the banana toast you can never go wrong with adding honey if you want something more on the sweeter side. The prices are slightly higher than other places in similar category but still delicious.

Honestly not sure how this place has so many great reviews. It's an average brunch spot with average food.

Dropped in on a Sunday at around 9:30 AM. I ordered the "like-a-tiger", which is an egg white omelette and a single biscuit. My friend ordered the tugboat with smoked salmon.

THE GOOD
- The biscuit was definitely the highlight. Nice and fluffy. It comes with honey butter (which is a nice idea but executed poorly with cubes of butter and only a tiny bit of honey) and berry jam.

THE MEH
- My friend's tugboat was not warm. The avocado spread clashed in flavor with the hollandaise sauce and over-powered the smoked salmon. The poached egg was very, very runny and everything just seemed to meld together into a mush.
- The egg white omelette also felt like a mis-mash. The egg white was cooked separately from the filling and was rubbery. The filling of veggies meanwhile was undercooked and doused in olive oil.

It is nice that there's lots of patio seating, but the food was so sub-standard. Hopefully it was just an off day versus the norm.

Stopped by here on the way from SLO to Orange County. Maybe it was due to all the Yelp hype. Maybe being hungry makes one more irritable. But this is what disappointment tastes like.

Also the restroom is filthier than a college dorm's. Enter at your own risk.
We walked over from State Street and the walk was so worth it! Our group got a bit of everything chilaquiles, french toast, Mac and cheese and breakfast sandwiches. Everything was delicious!
Stopped in on our way to San Luis Obispo- delicious food, good vibes & excellent service!
Really good food at a reasonable price. Ordered the chilaques and the east side. Both yummy. I would recommend adding avocado. Only issue was there was a piece of plastic and an egg shell in our f
My eggs Benedict was prepared perfectly! Come here as you will love the service and they have a nice patio area!
Love this place! Chilaquiles are the best. Great coffee, love the outdoor dog friendly patio.
This is very Overrated. Strangest combo's of food I've seen.  Forgot half our order too... would stay away from meat dishes. Ordered 3 of them and no one liked or could finish.  People are nice

I've missed the brunch experience- but ordering pickup through DoorDash for now will have to do! Pick up was super quick and easy, I just walked up to the ordering window and they finished making the food about 10 minutes before estimated ready time!

Rollex: everything breakfasty/brunchy in a wrap! Eggs, bacon, avocado, and a tomato sauce. The flatbread it was on reminded me of a flour tortilla, and it had a light layer of grease on the outside (so wash your hands and be prepared to get your hands a little messy!) The Rollex was very enjoyable, my favorite out of the two things we ordered. I split it with my boyfriend, but would probably be quite content with the portion size if I ate it all by myself.

Like-a-tiger: a healthier approach to an omlette, filled with zucchini, mushroom, onions, and spinach! I was a bit disappointed with how small the actual omlette/egg portion was (about the size of my hand), but it tasted good. The potatoes were a bit soft instead of crisp even though we ate in the car right after picking up the food, but I liked how they sautéed onions with it as well. Saving the best portion of this entree for last- the tomatoes!!! They were sweet yet somehow savory at the same time, and gave little bursts of flavor whenever I ate one.

I decided to stop by The Shop Kitchen for brunch during a road trip up to NorCal, based on the good Yelp reviews as well as a Groupon deal that was available. 

I love brunch foods, and I tend to gravitate towards eggs benedicts. However, after browsing the menu here, the Mac on Crack immediately caught my eye and I knew that I had to try it. This dish was a flavor bomb so I'd recommend sharing it with someone if possible. It was delicious but the flavor was super strong and I'm not sure I would have been able to finish the whole thing by myself. The mac and cheese base is rich and cheesy, and topped with some chopped green apples for a tart flavor that cut through the cheesiness.

This was one of the more unique brunch meals that I've had, and I'm glad I got to try this place!

This is a very sweet and funny little cafe that is next door to (yet separated by hedge and a fence) a auto body shop,,, not sure if that's where it gets the name The Shop kitchen?!?!
But, it was a homemade and delicious breakfast while visiting Santa Barbara!!!
It seems to be a place where the locals go.

Neat little brunch place. Lines can be seemingly long but it goes by better than expected. The chefs are professional artisans who make the simplest foods so well. Try the biscuits, they're the best. There are lots of beverages to choose from too. 

While you wait for your food just look out for seating. It's mostly communal. Plenty of street parking available and nice shops nearby. Overall a pleasant experience and I would go back for brunch next time I'm in the area.
Great service, quality food. We got sides for the kids and had a great picnic. The tri tip was delicious!
Get the Chilaquiles w/ carnitas. Just do it! Incredibly delish. Great flavor, just the slightest kick of heat - and perfectly cooked over easy eggs. And I feel like the tortilla chips were homemade.

The sando sandwich was yummy  
The salmon tugboat was also  delicious. 
Strawberry banana basil shake was good but couldn't taste the basil much FYI 
Chai tea was on l
I would go back or recommend eating there.

The food was good but coming from someone who works daily in the kitchen for their career it would be appreciated if they could practice proper sanitation and health techniques during the pandemic especially if they have an open kitchen where customers can see the preparation of their food in front of them

Had Breakfast plans on a weekend away in Santa Barbara. The place had a two hour wait so we went on yelp and searched out this restaurant. It was cute, comfortable and had amazing food! Would Recommend it to anybody!

Not sure if they were just having a bad day, but I probably won't be coming back here anytime soon. We ordered the oatmeal, "just the tip" sandwich, and salmon eggs benedict through Doordash, along with a latte and hot tea. The oatmeal and sandwich tasted fine, although the price ($13 and $15) was a bit steep for what we got. The eggs benedict ($18), on the other hand, was practically inedible. There was not one, but two hairs in it, and the muffin was so dry it was inedible. Also, the tea bag had been added to the water before leaving the restaurant, meaning it was far oversteeped by the time we got to it.

Great food and great find. I stopped by Super Ricca Taqueria only to find it closed. Read a few reviews and decided to drive a little up the road and give THe Shop Kitchen a try...I'm happy I did. A transplanted NYC chef, I am always happy to see small local shops putting out ambitious food and hitting the mark.
Wow. What a really interesting menu and so well made by the team inside. Lots of patio seating with some good music playing. Just really a perfect spot.

An excellent stop for breakfast. I've been looking for a good go to place for breakfast in Santa Barbara and this is it. Lots of unique menu items plusfriendly staff. Given the current Covid craziness, the staff here handled it well and the food came out hot and delicious. I had the eggs Benedict with fried chicken and it did not disappoint. Crispy fried chicken, perfectly cooked, poached egg, scratch made hollandaise Piled on a crispy biscuit. Heaven on a plate. piled on a crispy biscuit. Heaven on a plate. The staff here was very attentive given the current situation with the Covid. They were doing everything they could to make customers comfortable and happy. Props to them! I will be coming back for more breakfasts.
This place used to be amazing. Now it's just ok. The food used to justify the cost. Not so much anymore
Delicious food and excellent service! Thank you all for being so accommodating and patient. I will definitely revisit...

I have been to almost all the brunch/ breakfast spots in Santa Barbara if you can imagine haha, but unfortunately this place didn't hit the spot:( 

The aesthetics for everything here is an A+ but the food was lackluster in flavor and overall pretty mediocre. However, we did enjoy the Groupon that saved us money! If we didn't have the Groupon I would not have thought the food was worth it, but it sure did look pretty! 

If you have a SWEET tooth, I would recommend the french toast! That was my favorite part of the meal, however it was overly sweet. That being said, get it with fruit (it helps balance it a little more). The chilaquiles was also okay, just not super traditional and honestly pretty bland and not authentic.

Bottom Line: A lot of effort has gone into making this place and it shows, however Im afraid that it unfortunately doesn't live up to the hype.

        The wife and I met up with some of her friends for lunch at this spot to give it a try for the first time.  The wife and I ordered a burger to split and our friends ordered the Tri Tip sandwich.
     The burger patty was thin and hard.  The only flavor afforded us by this sandwich came from the condiments and for the first time in my life the meat to condiment ratio went significantly the other direction in that the vegetables over powered the meat!  That's a first for sure - not necessarily a bad thing but that patty needs some serious work being that close to Sams to Go....

   Our friend didn't really like her Tri Tip sandwich either.  She said specifically she didn't like it in a "mayonnaisey saucey way"  Now Im not really sure what the hell that means because I regrettably didn't get a chance to try it but I can only assume it meant it had too much sauce, in a bad way.

     Everyone that we saw that worked here was super nice.  Super nice people came by to clear the trays, the guy that took our order was super nice and helped us navigate the menu, it was very warm that day and they made sure the readily accessible water containers were full of cold water (which was very nice BTW).
     I LOVE the toolbox inside with the cutting board on it - so much so that Im stealing that idea if I ever have a proper kitchen.

      With the reviews as strong as they are for this place I can only assume that we hit it on an off day and we are just going to have to go back and check it out another time.

This was my second time here and unfortunately I got the same thing both times. Its just too good , I had a fried chicken sandwich,  it came on a brioche bun with a tangy cole slaw. Very good, my friend got a hamburger,  sorry i can't remember names of items. But she had a double cheese burger basically it looked amazing.  Both came with homemade potatoe chips,  which were nice and crispy. We sat out on their cute little patio. They have plenty of seating and I love their  yellow umbrellas , we ate a late lunch it was around 1:30 so it was pretty quiet.  I've been there before earlier and they Get busy. They close at two by the way. We ordered at the counter and a friendly young man brought the food and drinks out  to us. The staff is polite and friendly. I can't wait to go back again,  and I promise to try something new. I say definitely go!! P.s. there is  a Groupon right now so its totally worth it.

A great brunch/lunch spot in Santa Barbara! We were on the way to pismo beach and stopped by here for lunch. Their ingredients were fresh and everything were delicious! I especially like their salads, they all looked amazing!! They have both indoor and outdoor dining options. Highly recommended

If your looking for a great outdoor seating and good sandwich to eat this place has good sandwich and burgers. Have not ventured outside of that but if the rest of the food is anything like the burgers you will not go wrong! Place is right on the corner and fairly priced.

Never thought I'd order (let alone love) a breakfast salad, but here we are. It had been a heavy beer-filled long weekend for us and my body was begging me to order something from the "Lite" menu section and so the Sunshine salad with greens, potatoes, poached egg (and more) called my name. As far as salads go, it was super flavorful with the perfect amount of dressing. Potatoes were delicious and I loved the crunch and sweet bursts of the pomegranates. I'm also a sucker for anything with an egg on top. 

My husband got the Rollex and loved it. It totally would've been my second choice. 

Very busy on a Sunday morning at 11am, but we were able to find a table for 2 outside. 

Counter service style and very friendly service.

Hopefully its better if you dine in but our to go food was super soggy. It would've made sense if I took forever to pick my order up but I got their early and they still were working on it. Food isn't cheap so I expected way better. Maybe we'll try again some other time

Holy Shit. We moved here back in March and I'm soooooo sad we waited so long to try this place! I've never been a "brunch to go" person but I'm not trying to get COVID and it's my birthday! So we ordered and picked up. 
I got the Eggs Benny with Ham and it was SO DELICIOUS! The Benny is on a biscuit........what part of that can be wrong!? My wife got the Sando. She's not normally a "breakfast food person" but she killed that Sando. Success all around! We will be back!!!!
Great food and service. I would recommend the eggs Benedict. Cappuccino was good too!

Synopsis:
Get the Eggs Benedict. It's an awesome dish. The drinks are great too. We had an horchata latte.

The good:
- Eggs Benedict dishes
- The place is cool, I really enjoyed eating here
- The drinks are great
- Consistency. They are always great and a stable food anytime I visit.

The bad:
- It gets crowded if you go on the weekends. 
  (We've always been lucky to find a seat, but we always have to squeeze into tables and stuff. If you don't find a place to sit, ask for it to go. It's worth eating the meal. Your nearby the beach and the mission so you can eat around those areas.)

I highly recommend this place.

After reading many good Yelp reviews, my husband and I were excited to try this place for our first brunch while on vacation in Santa Barbara. I can honestly say this was one of the most disappointing meals we've had (on vacation or back home) in a long time. We came for a very late brunch on a weekday and were the only customers there when we first arrived. Our food came out quickly. My husband ordered the "Tugboat" eggs benedict with salmon. It was fine, nothing spectacular, and we both noticed that not a single element of the dish was warm, much less hot. I ordered the "bananas toast". Maybe it's my fault for not reading the menu more closely, but I assumed this was French toast, because why would a restaurant put plain dry toast on their menu? Turns out this was literally just a single thick, dry piece of wheat bread topped with almond butter, cold sliced bananas, and what seemed like a small drizzle of butter or maple syrup. At $11, this seemed like a joke. I could spread nut butter and banana on bread at home for about $2. The portion was small, but not good enough to justify even finishing it. We would have shared our feedback with the waitstaff if they had ever bothered to check back in with us, but unfortunately they did not. We will not return.
Love this place - casual outdoor seating and great food!!  We never miss it when we're in Santa Barbara!
Come here on a sunny day and you can have breakfast / brunch outside on their patio.

Can't go wrong with brunch here! Don't be discouraged by the line to order at the window; how quick they bring your order to your table in the expanded dog-friendly patio makes up for it.

The Tugboat (eggs Benedict) seems to be one of their most popular dishes. I've tried one with smoked salmon, but I prefer the one with fried chicken because I think it pairs better with the biscuit, avocado, and smoked tomato hollandaise. I do wish the Benedict came with a side of hash browns, home fries, or fruit like at other places though. I love a good french toast, and The Frenchie did not disappoint! The sprinkles of fragrant basil added a refreshing savory element. The Yolo (fried egg and fried chicken on a biscuit) was yummy too! I was surprised that the side of sausage gravy wasn't as heavy as it looked. The Melt (ham and cheese sandwich) wasn't quite for me; cheese, ham, french toast, and syrup didn't go together as well as I thought it would, especially compared to chicken and waffles.

If you're looking to save some money, check out their deal on Groupon!

Small outdoor cafe along the street. 

Parking: street parking, wasn't hard to find. 

Hostess: none, this is an order window and find your own table. 

Service: they only bring the food to your table, so I wouldn't expect much in way of service. However the ordering process is fast and they brought the food in a timely manner. 

Food: I had the eggs Benedict and it was really good! My wife had the grilled cheese and tomatoe soup. The grilled cheese she really liked, but the soup she said tasted like a spaghetti sauce more than soup. I tried it, and it was decent. 

Pricing: very fair

Got takeout from this place after a long night of drinking and this definitely hit the spot. The outside of the restaurant is very simple. I couldn't even tell it was a restaurant because all I saw was a Tire Shop sign. Anyway, don't judge a book by its cover because the food here was damn delicious. Definitely recommend the Yolo and the Fried Chicken Benedict. Their outdoor seating is pretty casual too.

Looking for place to eat in Santa Barbara, on the way north. Looked on yelp
And found this place, looked ok So we decided to go. It has no sign out side so you will have hard time finding it. Place clean and organized with a good selection of food to eat. But very expensive for what you get and small portions. Food was ok, we had fish tacos and cheese burger. Staff was pleasant and friendly to us but places was slow, I guess it was because of Easter Sunday. But not grate but not bad if your willing to over pay.

Everything  that we ordered was DELICIOUS!!! Great service and fast friendly staff . We had a great breakfast an a great time. definitively these going to be our place for breakfast next time we visit Santa Barbara.
so good!! the food is amazing!! perfect place for brunch with the girls! very aesthetic!!! highly suggest the eggs benedict w/ the salmon!!

This spot was good. In enjoyed the set up. The salmon tug boat was good and the chilaquiles were great! The Mac and cheese was interesting. The service was A+ overall it was a good experience. Oh and the horchata latte was tasty

If I lived in Santa Barbara id be a regular!! the outdoor seating was perfect for this sunny winter day

Order at the window and food will either be delivered to your table which can be either indoors or in their umbrella'd outdoor picnic tables

--Tugboat benedict w/ ham: only available on the weekends! the biscuits & avocado make this benedict very enjoyable! it's pretty large so if two people are ordering this, i'd get a benedict & salad to share
---got an arnold palmer to go too!

NOTE: seems like they may share the building with a tire shop?

I am writing this because WE LOVE The Shop & it's food... we have been coming here since it opened... 
I am writing in the hopes that they will FIX these issues.

There is THING 1 & THING 2:

THING 1). For the last 3 times over 6 months our "hot" food has been almost cold (about room temp).  Today Friday July 10th around 1p, there were 3 tables with not more than 6 people total... & NO ONE in line.  I bought my fave --The Salmon Tugboat & it came out "cold".

I took it back & explained to the kitchen help & he GRACIOUSLY apologized & heated it.

I went to the girl who took my order & explained to her... she seemed to care less & made it like it was MY FAULT... & the 2nd girl I talked to blamed the PANDEMIC... I said that I studied physics & I asked if the Pandemic means that hot or at least warm food is now impossible?????  That 2nd girl later said "we are doing our best"... I responded "I think WE can do better!!!"  For $16 for an Eggs Benedict, I at least want it to be warm, when I am almost the only one there... or only serve COLD foods on the menu.

THING 2) I get my coldush Benedict & notice that the is ABSOLUTELY NOTHING ELES ON THE PLATE... for almost $16 !!!   Soooo I then order a side of potatoes... huge bowl, hot & AWESOME !!!!
I suggested that they LET U KNOW WHEN U ORDER... that nada comes with the eggs... to prevent having to wait an extra 12 minutes for great potatoes!!!!   She received that suggestion well.


PS. I hope that changes can be made, especially when the place is almost empty... we love(ed) The Shop & it's food!

-Namaste
Customer service on point!! Food delicious! And we got it pretty fast and the vanilla latte was delicious i love this place.

This place was great. Even though it's order at the counter, they seat you, so none of that waiting with food in your hands for someone to get up. Some of the best french toast I've ever had. I was concerned about the basil, but it was delish. Pass on the roll-ex, it wasn't that exciting. My mealmates loved the banana toast (almond/peanut butter made on site) and the salad with the shrimp. Also, the owner kept checking in to make sure we were satisfied. Great all around!

Yummy! I've loved this place since the first time I discovered it while down here for work. This time had my family with me and they really enjoyed the casual feeling and good food. 

Great for a nice quick bite with kids.

Good overall! A little pricey for what you get but ambiance is really cute.  BF got the East side which was better then my Eggs plate.  Ordered a Bloody Mary but they were out of the mix so settled for mimosa which was good

My Son & I both got the Benedict with the fried chicken (our bad). It was too much going on & the  flavors were not complementing of each other.It's served on a thick biscuit with avocado, cold hollandaise sauce, and a poached egg. It was a mix of a avocado toast, a Benedict, and the fried chicken that should've been served with waffles and syrup.
Love this spot! Oat milk matcha latte is delicious. I also got the French toast with fried chicken and the veggie Sando. Yummmmm.

This place is wildly overrated with its busy line and bland food. The chilaquiles is a joke. Clearly this is an Americanized version for people who can't handle spice. No salsa on chilaquiles? What is even happening. Just squirts of sour cream. I should have known better and looked deeper into the contents of the menu items. The fried chicken Benedict aka the tugboat had a very hard and weird texture on the bready part underneath. Overall very disappointed I bothered coming here, I had high expectations with all the hype. Guess Santa Barbara can't do food like LA.

Okay y'all- WOW. You MUST go here. The best brunch I've had in my life. The oatmeal, GF banana toast, breakfast potatoes... my GOSH. Found this lil gem thanks to Yelp and need to make sure to keep the trend going. Amazing atmosphere. Amazing staff.

Breakfast here was a unique but funky in a good way experience.  

You walk up and place your order at an outside window of what looks to be an old burger joint from the 1960's or 70's.  Then you find a seat inside a small dining area or on the outside patio dining area.   

The food is delivered to you and that's where you look down at your plate and say this looks friggen awesome.  I know its only breakfast but they really know how to make a variety of eggs benedict with homemade breads and muffins.  Do yourself a favor and order a side of bacon and potatoes.  The bacon is the best thick cut maple bacon I have had in quite sometime and the roasted cut red potatoes with rosemary is nicely done.  By the way the bacon and potatoes sides are good for sharing between 2 people.  

Parking on the street can be tough but well worth the search just to eat a good breakfast here.  I'll definitely be back when I visit Santa Barbara again.

Lots of outdoor seating! It's a unique place because you just order and pay at the counter and find a seat yourself. We got the tugboat which is eggs Benedict with fried chicken. It was good! Not much parking so we parked in a nearby neighborhood.

This is my favorite brunch spot! I am obsessed with the fried chicken benedict. It's forever my go to! Very big portions. Parking kind of sucks cause it's street parking, the matcha latte is just okay, and it's kind of pricey. BUT the food never disappoints and I love the outside patio

For the price, I would expect the meals to be accompanied by something. But everything is a la cart.  But we did enjoy our dishes.  The fried chicken that accompanied our dishes reminded me of Asian fried chicken.  I'm not a French toast person but I liked it.  It wasn't too thick and filling and went well with the chicken.   The gravy that came with the chicken and biscuit was on the thin side but it was tasty. We basically crumbled the biscuit into the gravy and it was yummy.  The veggie Benedict was as it sounds.  Lol.  

It's not an elegant setting.  The interior was sparse and a little depressing.  The patio was much better and you couldn't tell you were sitting next to a busy street.
We came to have a breakfast at the shop kitchen during our trip to Santa Barbara from LA. The food was very good. Tasted fresh and tasty. The location is also beautiful. Great place.

Came here early for lunch, it was completely dead when we got there, but within 10 minutes there was over 50 people outside ready to order, and now I see why.  The sandwich I ordered, was probably one of the best I've ever had. It was a a honey baked Ham and Brie sandwich.  All I can say is WOW, that was damn good.  I wanted to try several other sandwiches on the menu, but I can only eat so much, we'll have to come back the next time we're in Santa Barbara!
Delicious food!  My only complaint was that we almost missed the place because there wasn't a sign on the building.

Patio was great for brunch and also dog-friendly which is a plus. I ordered the fried chicken eggs benedict. The fried chicken was sooo crunchy and tasty. Definitely not the lightest breakfast of choice, but I sure enjoyed what I ordered. The sauce wasn't too overwhelming and by the end, I was so full.

Went to S.B for the first time and we decided to make a stop here for some breakfast before leaving. We both got the tugboat with maple bacon with a side of roasted potatoes; it was delicious & filling! Great customer service & welcoming atmosphere. Will be coming back!

Went to The Shop the other day for some brunch. Here's my thoughts:

I ordered the eastside and some OJ. Here's the deal. Was this avocado toast amazing? Yeah it was. But I got into an argument with my wife cause I didn't give it a 10 and couldn't name another avo toast id had that was better. Don't get me wrong, this toast was amazing. But I just felt like it could've been a bit more. They overcooked my poached egg which was a huge bummer, and I felt like the toast could've been a little bit toastier (a little too soft). The OJ was super tasty and sweet, def fresh squeezed. I've had other things here too, and they're all delicious but just were too heavy for what I was lookin for. Lighter fare this definitely hit the mark and honestly probably would order again. That said, I'd say 9/10.

Likelihood of an LA tourist showing up because it's on Milpas? 1/10 (major perk if you ask me)

Overall: 9/10

@santabarbarashane

Hands down my favorite spot for brunch in literally all of Santa Barbara. It's a new take on many classic breakfasts, using lots of fun ingredients that add yummy flavors to the plates. They also have a lovely outdoor patio. 

I've tried many things on the menu at this point, and I can say it's all been perfectly executed! My usual order is the "rollex" which is like a burrito, but the bread is way better than a tortilla. Inside are roasted tomatoes, crunchy bacon, avocado, and egg and rolled into sweet perfection. They also have a huge selection of craft beers, cocktails, and kombucha! :)
Such good brunch! The Rolex is my Saturday morning go too. It was inspired by Ugandan cuisine and the flavors are incredible. You can't go wrong!

Pretty standard brunch menu with affordable (for Santa Barbara) prices. I was excited to try this place only to be disappointed by the food and service. 

The good: There is a nice vibe with outdoor seating, shade coverings and music. 

The bad: I had the eggs Benedict (which itself was tasty) but the eggs were a little too undercooked for me (the white was runny). Also, it didn't come with anything else-no potatoes, fruit, meat-just the eggs Benedict. The point of brunch is all of the extras. Also, the service was not good. Not sure if they were in training, but they seemed disorganized and unsure of what to do (like what the guest ordered). I was sitting for about 5 minutes before I asked the server about my coffee. They brought it out shortly after that (which was not good at all). I went to the counter to put sugar and cream in my coffee and was out of cream; and had to wait a few more minutes before they refilled the cream carafe. I overheard a few more guest complaining about not getting their coffee and waiting for it to be brought out. As I'm finishing my food, the server tries to hand me a coffee cup saying I ordered one, meanwhile I have my cup in my hands. 

This place has potential, but I was dissatisfied with the overall experience. Can't say I wouldn't go back, but I'm not eager to eat there anytime soon.

Love their breakfast Sando with bacon! Amazing bun and holds up until the end. I typically sub potatoes for a salad and get their biscuit. Delicious michelada as well! The staff is kind and efficient. Highly recommend!

The food is fabulous as well as the service.  They are always more than happy to adjust menu items to accommodate vegetarian.  Use the axxess card every time for 10% off.  Love the sando, muffins, brown sugar cookie, the Rolex and absolutely am thrilled when the weekend rolls around for the eggs benedict.

This is a review based on the service. We clearly ordered two meals and the cashier left out one of our orders and failed to charge/put in the second one. He claims that we did not correct him when he repeated our order, but we had initially clearly ordered two items. We waited 45 minutes before the cashier came out to let us know and then he proceeded to ask us to have the second item charged. He did not offer anything to correct his mistake.

Just YUM!
There is a little wait to order in line before sitting, but because of this, plentiful outdoor seating and food all came out quite quickly after ordering at the counter.
Everything was delicious and so thoughtfully balanced with flavors, nicely but not fussily plated.
The mac-n-crack is awesome if you like blue cheese (which I definitely do).
The crystallized basil sprinkled on the Frenchie toast was a welcome and bright little herb note with their excellent sweet breakfast option.
The hollandaise on the tugboat is lemony/yolky perfection.
Def recommend!
Oh and super dog friendly! My pup loved his boiled egg that they nicely sliced up for him and presented in a takeaway box.

Atmosphere is great, food looks amazing excpet only for people who eat meat/dairy. No veggie patty available which is almost always an option anywhere else. I really reccoment adding this option. Tofu for your wraps would amazing too. Just adding a few vegan/vegitarian options would really make this place the best! Thank you!!
Must everytime we are in Santa Barbara. The salmon eggs benedict are so amazingly delicious!
Veggie Tugboat all the way. Honestly best breakfast/brunch in SB! Plus they started serving wings and other things for dinner under the name Wingman Rodeo!

The food is all from scratch. I am a foodie and a chef and I would say it's really fantastic! 

Super friendly people and great service!

During my trip in Santa Barbara, the shop kitchen is certainly one of the food highlights! It's a hidden spot outside the touristy zone and has incredible brunch options.

We got their famous tugboat, which is basically eggs Benedict but with biscuit and smashed avocado, one with salmon and another with fried chicken. Both are absolutely delicious but I do prefer the salmon one!

The salmon tugboat really packs a flavor! The gooey egg yolk, avocado and hollandaise sauce are so creamy that mix well with the texture of the salmon. I also love the flavor combination of the saltiness in cured salmon and the hints of sweetness in the hollandaise sauce. The biscuits are also toasted golden and adds some more crunch to the texture. Amazing!!

I also really enjoyed their iced americano (which I think it's from Handlebar?) and their service is super efficient & nice - we didn't have to wait for a table at peak hour on a Sunday! 

Overall the shop is such a great brunch spot! The only points off would be with the fried chicken - it's not the best fried chicken Benedict I've had b/c the skin is just not crispy enough. Otherwise I would strongly recommend this spot!

this place is the bomb!!! everything i've had here was five stars! fried chicken, the french toast, the avocado toast, the coffee, the kombucha! it's all amazing! they make fun, creative menu items with high quality ingredients and they feed you well. you don't get a tiny plate like some of the other sb restaurants. come here and you won't be disappointed! I always bring out of towners here and they love it too!
Overall pretty good service and restaurant. I gave it 4 stars cus the chilaquiles are more like nachos in almost every way
Best yogurt parfait I've ever had! The Rollex was amazing as well. This is definitely my new favorite brunch spot and happy to help support you guys during these challenging times. God bless!

First time at location. Found it in Yelp and was interested to try out because it had high rating.

First impression: 
Pricey meals. The restaurant did not appear to match their meal prices, nor did the appearances of the workers. The dining experience felt like i was ordering at a stationary food truck where you would walk up and order through a small window. The employees had casual clothes and one of them chose to wear his cap backwards, which is absolutely fine. I just expected more professional appearances considering the price they charge. It was next to a automotive business which is probably why it's named the Shop.

Dining:
Outdoor dining tables.

Food:
Fried chicken tug boat ($15.50), The Melt, and Vanilla Latte ($5 small)

Food came in white rectangular shaped  plates that looked nice.

But...Food was too mediocre for the price they charge, which have gone up from the menu in their web site.

The Melt had a lot of syrup doused on top. I'd recommend asking to have the syrup on the side.

The tug boat fried chicken looked nice. Fried chicken was crisp, but the whole dish lacked flavor and was bland. I don't normally use salt on my food, but this plate needed it.

Coffee wasn't as hot as I expected, and it was too sweet to finish.

Overall:
It was disappointing. I initially did not mind paying the price but not for a mediocre, drowned out, lack of flavor type meal, with the additional too sweet to finish coffee. I'm sure one could get a whole lot better experience, better tasting food for a lot less expensive nearby.

Been there, done that. Not worth returning for me.

We still love The Shop and love brunching here as often as possible. The Shop has quickly made itself a staple among the already delicious food among Milpas St. We're glad they're keeping up with the quality of excellent food in the area!

We stopped in today after a long Saturday morning walk around the neighborhood. My husband ordered the Mamma sammie and I got a Shop fav, The Yolo!! 

Mamma is a fried chicken sandwich with lots of marinara, mozzarella and basil with an fantastic side salad with pomegranate in it. The Yolo hit all my brunch spots! Fried chicken, sausage gravy and an enormous biscuit! 

We washed it all down with an iced tea and lemonade and a Shop made Michelada. I could've had at least three more Micheladas. The Michelada was definitely my favorite part of the meal!

Very very overpriced for the portion size. The biscuit was good but the gravy was absolutely flavorless. The banana almond butter toast was DELICIOUS. I'd assume there were some other tasty things on the menu as the menu definitely ranged we were just VERY disappointed by the biscuits and gravy and the price for the value. The staff was friendly and the patio was cute. With so many options in Santa Barbara / Goleta we unfortunately would not recommend nor return.

I moved to town recently and heard good things about this spot.
I was first to order out of all of my friends and got the Iced Horchata Latte with oat milk and the fried chicken benedict. The cashier should have informed me that it could not come with oat milk as there horchata was made with dairy as well. It took 10 minutes for an employee to come up to me and tell me that they could not do it with oat milk, and I said, "That is fine, I will still try it."  Another 10 minutes go by and I walk up to the counter to be greeted by a, "Oh I was just going to come tell you that we don't have horchata right now".  HELLO. Could you have figured that out when you asked me about the oat milk? Besides the fact that I paid extra for the horcahta latte and upcharge for oat milk and did not benefit from the now wasted money.

Next stop FOOD. My friends are all almost done with their meals and guests who have come in after us already have their food as well.  I still have not received mine.  No communication whatsover about a delay in my meal or what was going on.  We all ordered a dish with fried chicken but mine came out absolutely last.  It ended up tasting good but not worth all the hassle.

Ugh.

I had a craving for an egg sandwich and I'd heard such great things about The Shop Kitchen, I decided to pick one up to-go.

Served in a plastic container was possible the worst egg sandwich of my life. Instead of a cheesy sandwich with a nice runny egg, this dry-as-hell sandwich had a folded, well-done omelette inside... the type you would get at a Residence Inn breakfast buffet. Anyway, the sandwich consisted of a dry bun, this awful egg, a small smear of spicy mayo and some sort of guacamole. It came with potatoes which looked great but were raw when I bit into them.

What modern restaurant would make an egg sandwich like this? Don't they know what's happening in egg sandwiches these days? Food trucks, Eggslut, etc? Make the egg runny or don't cook it into oblivion!  I just can't trust anything else that would come out of this place.
The chilaquiles are to die for. That's it. That's the review. Everything else is great but if you have never been, don't you dare order anything else.

This is the worst restaurant I ever been to. I came with my family here because I read reviews of how good this place was . We tried the chilaquiles because it was recommended by the cashier. They are very dry and have no flavor they just come full of sour cream. The service is not great. If you really want to eat delicious with flavoring food and enjoy your meal this is not the place for you.

Very good food and service. The michelada was huge and delicious. The staff were all friendly and attentive, from cashier, to food runner, to bus boy. Props to them for great attitudes.

Also, it was nice being able to eat with my dog on the patio!

Highly recommend "The Frenchie" with fried chicken. What a combo! This sweet french toast topped with berries with slabs of fried chicken wedged between the toasts is a sweet & savory fanatic's dream. 

The outdoor dining area is no-frills and the view isn't anything to write home about, being situated next to an auto shop and all, but it has the feel of being in someone's nice roomy shaded patio with several picnic benches, and is quite clean-cut and cute. Speaking of the auto-shop, how genius is this location that allows you to get your car serviced while you get some brunch? Very. 

The price is steep however so grab the groupon while you can! And yes, it's true according to another yelper, that the cashier will select the tip percentage for you before turning around the tablet screen for you to sign. Luckily, she had selected it to 15% which is what I intended anyway so I left it that way. But yes, having that choice made for me was a little odd and off-putting. So check before you sign.

Overall a little disappointed in the food we got. We ordered the chilaquiles and honestly all the ingredients were good and food was delivered really fast however the chips were soooooo soggy. So I feel like even tho the food was brought out fast something was wrong because it was inedible due to how soggy everything was. Really wished the chips were crunchy in order to handle all the great flavors in the dish

Ate breakfast here this morning! Unique spot, walk up window order or sit inside, casual look but carefully organized meal. Quick service, the carnitas Eggs Benedict was exceptional!!! 

I would eat here multiple times a week if I could (I don't live in Santa Barbara), one of the best breakfasts I've ever had.

The very definition of a hole in wall. 10 minutes after ordering, your crew will be delighted at the sight of a lovely brunch-style meal. Highly recommend the like-a-tiger egg course, or the oatmeal for not only it's ravishing flavor but flawless execution and presentation. If you're ever passing through Santa Barbara or staying in the area, make sure to give this place a try!

Ordered the gluten free frenchie and it is NOT THE same as the pictures posted here from 3-4 years ago. That French toast they served before was ahhhh-mazing and thick and tasted like reg bread. Worth every penny. But the one they serve NOW is HORRIBLE! Weird nuts on the side, ruining the French toast texture as well as oats. It is thin and taste very much gluten free. With such a HUGE change in quality they should have adjusted the price or put up new pictures. I make better toast at home. We drove pretty far to come back and have the toast we have had many times and were completely disappointed and out of a lot of money becasue we ordered for the whole family. Buyer beware  that for gluten free folks you are better off making it at home vs being out of 15 bucks a plate and full of regret.

The most magical and revolutionary chilaquiles in town... like the original donkpad! El Bajio down street has 2nd best chilaquiles in town & best Agua Frescas. The Shop has a delicious salmon tugboat on a homemade biscuit as well and fresh OJ. Their salmon toast with fried capers is all worldly! Very friendly and cool staff always with a smile. Great lunch options too the tri tip sandwich with horseradish is delish. This is a real locals spot for Santa Barbarans. They also have coolest playlists/music in town here. The owner/manager must be hybrid DJ at night. #spotifyapproves

The Shop Kitchen is a hidden gem of Santa Barbara. It's located next to a tire shop so make sure to note that when looking for this place. There is street parking but no actual parking lot so keep them in mind as well. 

The menu has alot to offer! They have a ton of different breakfast and lunch options to choose from. The fried chicken eggs benedict, the tugboat, and the mamma are some of the things I've had. 

The fried chicken eggs benedict The chicken is crispy and juicy and not dry at all. The boiled egg has always been cooked perfectly with the best hollandaise sauce. 

The Mamma is a fried chicken sandwich with lots of marinara, that has mozzarella and basil on it. 

The Shop Kitchen is a great brunch, breakfast, and lunch spot! I'm looking forward to coming back to try more of their stuff on the menu.  Everything I have had was is delicious and I can't wait to try more things on their menu.

We tried this place for the first time because their menu sounded so delicious. I asked the kid at the window what their most popular tugboat option was and he replied the "fried chicken". My husband got the "Souper lunch" with Grilled cheese and tomato soup. The sand which as all bread and one slice of cheese. They up charged for the second half to make it a full sandwich. My tugboat was bland which was surprising seeing as they had sauce cheese fried chicken, still hardly any flavor at all. Sorry but all in all was very disappointed especially for their "most popular". Close to $35 for two items with no drinks... we can cross this off the buck list and happily try something else next time we're visiting the area.

Classic example of how poor ownership takes for granted their own kitchen talent and service  staff, when ego exceeds what it means to provide hospitality and a culinary experience. Food and staff, A+! Ownership, FAIL! I witnessed the owner throw a $20 bill at a guest and make her feel bad for waiting in excess of 40 minutes for her food. She was polite and just wanted a refund. I won't be supportive of a business that conducts guests relations in this manner.

This was a pleasant surprise, we ate here both mornings instead of at the hotel. The breakfast was outstanding! The Bananas, with almond butter and honey and Salmon on toast with a poached egg were great. Don't miss the hibiscus limeade. It's not sweet, but it's very good!

Our Brunch at The Shop was a huge disappointment.  We were anticipating an above average dining experience because of all the positive reviews.  There wasn't much of a line when we arrived and there was plenty of seating available on the outdoor patio.  I ordered the Tugboat aka: eggs benedict which I thought was their signature dish, and my husband ordered the Frencie aka: french toast.  The eggs benedict looked good on the plate, but tasted bland and mediocre at best.  The underlying biscuit was soggy and falling apart, the eggs were overcooked, there was no avocado, and the hollandaise sauce was tasteless.  My protein choice was the applewood bacon which was limp and soggy from the hollandaise sauce and also void of a distinct taste.  Each bite was a flavorless, uninteresting, gooey mess in my mouth.  My husband's Frenchie consisted of 4 small slices of extremely thin bread, borderline burned, and swimming in a pool of syrup which only made the bread soggy and soft.  There may have been powdered sugar sprinkled over the top of the French Toast, but it was conspicuously absent and most likely absorbed by the vast pool of syrup making it undetectable.  We both ordered coffee which arrived extremely hot in to-go coffee cups even though we were sitting on the outdoor patio.  Condiments for the coffee was self-serve with the only choices being 1/2 and 1/2, Spenda, and honey.  My husband asked for regular sugar and was told they had none.  All in all, it wasn't a very good cup of coffee.  This restaurant was unfulfilling and uninspiring.  There's absolutely nothing about The Shop that would make us ever want to go back.
Every time I have eaten here I loved it! Cool spot, off the beaten path, amazing food, outdoor patio, and Kombucha Sangria. I mean come on, what else do you need???

Love their food but my experience today was horrible. Yelp read due to COVID-19 to call then for hours.  Which I did they were open I gave my order over the phone since I had a Group-on deal to use. I told I would be there in a few minutes. I got there and had to park around the corner because they only have street parking. This was especially hard for me since I'm disabled.  
When I tried to pay they had Apple Pay only, I'm a droid user.  I only had cash in my pocket and left my wallet in my card. They weren't taking cash. I was angry because I had to walk back to my car to get my card. Why didn't the gal who answered gher phone tell me that? But they were accepting CASH tips. They had a tip jar on the counter. Very upsetting and disappointing experience.

Good was good. Safe and nice little outdoor seating area. I thought the food was good but nothing out of this world incredible. We got chilaquiles, with and without carnitas. The matcha latte was definitely not very good and tasted like it was made with water. ‍

Quick recap:

-          Food: Very Good
-          Portion size: Average
-          Service: Order at the counter; Nice Staff
-          Environment: Fast casual
-          $: Average
-          Perks: Outside Patio

More details:

Had a Cecilia salad ($11). It was really good. Also had the Sando with Bacon ($13). Quite tasty too.
Super fairly priced in my opinion.
The staff is nice and helpful.
Pick up is very easy.

Overall?

Great options. Fresh. Good.

Had a bit of a mixed experience here but overall it's a good place for brunch. They were out of frittatas which was the main dish I wanted and they didn't have the Arnold on the menu (even though it was on the online menu). Ended up with a sunshine salad (my boyfriend got the tugboat with carnitas) and a latte. It's pretty crowded so be prepared to wait a little for a table to open. Everything was pretty good, but I had an issue with the bill. I used a Groupon that I paid for in advance  ($12 for $20 worth of food), but I realized once I got back to the table the cashier had charged me for the Groupon in addition to everything else. I asked for a receipt after I ordered but the cashier didn't know how to print one out. Before we left I went to let them know and he ended up just giving me $20 back in cash (I guess it was too busy to take up too much time figuring it out). I'm glad that I was able to get something sorted out, but just make sure you double check your tab if you purchase a Groupon in advance!

I went here on a brunch emergency whim and it was the best spontaneous restaurant pick of my life. I can't wait to try more of their menu. In a world riddled with troubles lately, this was a much needed pleasant surprise.

THE BEST!  We have yet to order the same thing twice because EVERYTHING on the menu looks amazing. We have been blown away every time.  The avocado toasts are my usual go to but this beet salad was amazing.  Love the new indoor seating.

4 orders from here and they were all great. 
The salmon toast I ordered was based on a grilled sourdough slice, good quality salmon, poached egg, capers, onions etc. It was excellent! I tried the chilaquiles and those were very tasty too. I particularly liked the touch of cilantro. The Tijuana wrap was juicy, tasty deliciousness that was wrapped in buttery , crispy African bread. Lastly, I had a bite of my daughter's fried chicken sandwich. The crispy skin reminded me the of fish and chips batter. Oh and the chips were home made potato chips.

Decided to stop by to try breakfast after checking the reviews, oh boy I was not disappointed. Food was excellent, nice atmosphere. Highly recommend it, will definitely come back. A must go place for healthy breakfast, it's worth every penny.
Chilaquiles, bit enough for 2.  Great outdoor seating and the Frenche!  Wow.  Awesome breakfast spot.  Enjoyed our morning.

If you like fried chicken and French toast, this is a great choice! The standards are good bet and it's a great patio with a hip scene for the Milpas area. The espresso drink options make it a perfect place to come for breakfast/ brunch. It's well known and there can be quite a long line during the weekend. Be prepared to wait for a table during peak brunch hours. It's well worth it.

We were in Santa Barbara for the day and needed. A bit of sustenance to get us to the beach. We drove Down a quaint street with Mediterranean style buildings and parked around the corner on a residential street. The amount of noise from the construction going on directly in front of the restaurant gave us pause. However as soon as we sat down at a picnic table to sip on our mimosas the construction crew took a break. Yay!
     The food was exceptional, hot, fresh, and delivered with a smile. We especially Liked the Caesar salad and the french fries. We felt quite safe as the tables were spread apart nicely.
the best eggs benedict ever... the carnitas one is amazing and cute outdoor patio seating!

Got the yolo, the Sando and the Rolex. Definitely a big fan of the sando with ham. The flavor was on point! The Rolex has a delicious tortilla and the chicken was cooked to perfection on the yolo. I would definitely come back here

This place has good food! We had a variety of brunch dishes including eggs Benedict, almond butter toast, and chilaquiles. The toast was super yum because it was freshly ground almonds. The eggs were good too. Some of the portions, including the avocado toast, are a bit small but they hit the spot. The quality is high and the outdoor seating is ample. We had a large party and they had more than enough room. The owner and service people were super nice and attentive. Would definitely go back the next time in Santa Barbara!

Amazing food and service here! My partner and I got the salmon benedict, egg white omelette, and our favorite, the frenchie with fruit. Im usually not a brunch fan but this place is amazing. And the food didn't make me feel sluggish! Only thing I didn't like was being asked if we want to tip before our meal instead of after.
It's a flavorful trip to the Shop Kitchen.  Took my son for bfast and dropped $60 with tip for 2 people.  A little over-priced IMHO for breakfast.

Food at The Shop is always good but today was a big flop. I ordered a bacon breakfast sandwich for me and eggs Benedict for my bf ToGo while on our bikes. It took forever to come out but I wasn't too bothered by it until we rode all the way to the beach and saw there were no Togo utensils and No bacon in my breakfast sandwich :/ so it was only egg and avo and was cold and soggy by the time we rode back home! Big bummer!

My husband watches this golf blogger who recommended this place so we stopped by last Sunday!

Amaaaaazzzingly flavorful! Love love love
You get in line to order and they seat you after which I appreciate as people tend to save seats I. Other establishments

We ordered the tugboat and the Chilaquiles. My husbands didn't add the pulled pork but I recommend you should as it comes with the egg and sauce. Never the less it was delicious! Very flavorful and portions were large

My tugboat was perfect! Fried chicken with a poached egg and this yummy sauce! Can't wait to come back and highly highly recommend. If we had more time we would have got some bubbles and sat longer
This is a great spot for breakfast or lunch friendly staff great eats I like the super cheesy. The new dining room looks great.

If you look inside that kitchen, you will see that there is absolutely no seasoning in there. I'm shocked that this place has so many good reviews considering how much flavor it lacks. Yes it is pretty to look at, but not to consume. Like, salt cost 99 cents at target. The staff is super sweet tho! It's not their fault that the recipes are slacking.

You order at the order window, get a tumble & then find your own table. The food will get dropped off at your table! 

There's a small indoor area with several tables and a nice outdoor patio with wooden tables. It's like a picnic!  

I ordered the tugboat with salmon. It comes with a grilled buttermilk biscuit, avocado, smoked salmon, 2 poached eggs & smoked tomato hollandaise. The buttermilk biscuit was really hard, it was probably toasted too much? The smoked salmon was good! The poached eggs were perfectly cooked - with the yolk oozing out! Just how I like it. The sauce on top was a great addition to the overall dish. It definitely wouldn't be the same without it. I also got an americano - they serve handlebar coffee! 

A great spot for a quick breakfast/brunch! :)

We come here almost weekly to order brunch to-go and our experience has always been excellent. The chilaquiles are wonderful, and we've tried everything from the Tugboat to lemonade -- all A+. Very vegetarian friendly too!

The best avocado toast bar none! My 14 year old is very particular about her avocado toasts, and her eyes lit-up on the first bite. They have a combination with carne asada, jalapeño and poached egg that is addictive. The Tiger egg white dish with veggies and potatoes is my go-to - protein-veg-starch...great way to start the day. Coffee is delicious and the Matcha Latte is very fresh with a nice strong matcha flavor. I wish we lived closer, this would be our breakfast spot. Waitstaff was friendly and efficient.

The owner is incredibly rude and unprofessional- check out how he responded to some of the low rating reviews! The restaurant is filthy, did not follow COVID safety protocols at the height of the pandemic, and the food is extremely underwhelming.

While vacationing in Santa Barbara, it was my mission to find a brunch place that would blow my mind.. and I think I've found it. Here's my breakdown:

Ambience: The Shop Kitchen had a walk up to order window, with a nice enclosed outdoor seating area to the side. It gets pretty crowded so getting there early is a MUST. Has a nice picnic/garden vibe, and it's a really amazing place to sit with friends and just converse over amazing food. 

Food: I hardly even know where to begin with this part of my review. I initially chose this place because of their eggs Benedict w/ fried chicken (which was AMAZING), but it was another dish that stole the show! The Frenchie, in my opinion was the star of this meal. What essentially is just French toast with buttery syrup and BASIL infused sugar, blew my tastebuds out the water! The chilaquiles were the perfect contrast to the sweet and savory combo.

Overall, I highly recommend this place for anyone looking for an amazing brunch experience. Will definitely be making a return in the near future.

Literally the most disgusting food of my life. Ordered "The General" which is a fried chicken sandwich, with french fries. Both were still sizzling with grease to the point that I soaked up two napkins full of nothing but grease. The chicken was dark meat. The fries were soggy from all the grease. I could not imagine ever eating here again.

Finally a spot in SB with GREAT and affordable cafe style food!  I got the Rolex and the Burger and they were both unlike anything i've ever had.  This food is so good, you would be stupid not to try it!  Well done gentlemen
The food was bland, service was not great, and the line is way too long. Very difficult to give this place high ratings after trying authentic Mexican food in Los Ángeles.

After writing my review, the owners contacted me. They informed me that they took the feedback from my review and have since fixed the issue. They invited me back to the restaurant to give it another chance. They welcomed me and wanted to make sure everything was to my satisfaction. I yet again got the tug boat with the fried chicken. It was definitely cooked better than the previous time, so I'm inclined to say they have gotten the process down. Give this place a try, it's very welcoming.

This place is solid! What an amazing breakfast joint. Had the fried chicken Benedict which was perfect, with a nicely crisp fried chicken cutlet. Fried potatoes were good, could have used more seasoning and crisper. Had an amazing latte with Handlebar coffee. Fantastic and a must!

YOLO! Not just you only live once but this killer sausage gravy with fried chicken and a biscuit was amazing! Let's not forget the melt, which was sweet and savory! Heyyy, these two are definitely my favorites, I just have to eenie meenie mine mo!

The food looked great, but it was lacking flavor. I ordered the Egg Benedict with salmon and the bread was extremely dry. The total for our food was around 70 dollars for two breaks fast sandwiches and truly not great quality of food and expensive for what we ate. It's upsetting we paid so much when I couldn't even finish my breakfast because the bread was so dry (it would crumble in my mouth of how dry it was). My boyfriend tried helping eat it so it wouldn't go to waste and he didn't like it either. (I paid extra for the salmon and they got my order wrong (they gave me a bacon egg sandwich which I had to return to get the correct one). It was our last day in Santa Barbara and it was a bad choice on our part.  Definitely will not come back here.

This is our new favorite breakfast/brunch place to eat!
You're immediately greeted by a very friendly order-counter server; Megan was awesome. Once you order you're escorted to a nice covered patio area...very nice vibe!!
Everything we saw and everything we ordered was excellent!  Besides the delicious toast, we had the "Like-a-Tiger"...all very good.  The grits were a nice surprise.. fluffy, cheesy, and delicious!  Highly recommended!

Visited for brunch on a Saturday morning and  the place can get busy. If a line isn't there, you approach the hostess/clerk to order and they will assign you a table of your choice and upon availability (outdoor/indoor). There is limited indoor seating so it's mostly outdoor. A nice benefit is that it's a dog friendly outdoor patio so you can bring your furry pals if you wanted to. 

For service, the hostess was very kind and courtesy, but aside from that, it's minimalistic bring your food and take away the plates service. I did notice a few times that the servers bringing out the food having to take a pause to recall where the food was supposed to go. Perhaps just a new server on the job that day. 

For food, the meal came before the drinks. Because it was rather chilly, we opted to eat the food instead of waiting for the beverages, which came about halfway through out meal - to each their own, but I would have preferred if the beverage came first. In total, we had the Like-A-Tiger (vegetarian omelet), Eggs benedict over toast with added bacon, and Tugboat with fried chicken. To start, the beverages were pretty nicely done in my opinion. The chai latte was full of spice and the macchiato had a very nice roast to it. For the like-a-tiger, I liked how fresh the ingredients were and the omelet layer was nice pan-fried. The (purely preference) negative was whether the ingredients melded together nicely. Because each ingredient stood out by itself, it didn't mesh well together and was just a mix of fresh ingredients such as zucchini, hon mishi mushroom, spinach, etc. For the egg benedict toast with added bacon, the amount of bacon was surprising and the quality of the bacon was superb in my opinion. The bacon wasn't overcooked and had a nice crisp to it while retaining its moisture -  this was a definitely highlight. The eggs benedict were nicely done and not too heavily undercooked. They were still flowy, but I think a bit overdone was the amount of chives on top of it. I think less would have been better. For the tugboat, the fried chicken was delectable. Thin batter, moist chicken, and nice complement flavors with the egg benedicts. One thing that was a bit off was how tarty (lemon juice) the hollandaise sauce was. A better ratio could have been had to balance the sauce's flavors, but the texture and consistency of the sauce was on point.

All in all, we enjoyed the brunch and can see why quite a few people enjoy it there. Although the service is minimalistic, we enjoyed them more for the quality of their food. The ingredients tasted fresher and were better prepared than other brunch places we have been and that's a positive in our book. Definitely worth a try to formulate your opinion or if you are in the area.

Visiting from out of town and came across this place on Yelp. Unfortunately the stars were misleading. Ordered 2 OJ's (they were GREAT + FRESH SQUEEZED) we also ordered 2 coffee's, unfortunately the coffee was awful. It tasted as if it was Folgers instant coffee. Which is very disappointing because it's just coffee.  For food I ordered the Tugboat with veggies, I was quite excited for the veggies but when I was given my plate the veggies were not properly sautéed or seasoned. It had no flavor, it seemed as if they relied on the flavor of the Benedict sauce to give the veggies flavor. It also didn't see to be warm, the veggies were kind of cold making my eggs cold. Overall my plate 3/5. My partner ordered the Rolex, this was also disappointing in the fact that it barely had any avocado and bacon. The avocado seemed to be slightly there to non existent. Flavor 4/5 expectations 3/5.

Two Words: YOLO heaven

This place is super low key. It is perfect for brunch or a morning after date ;). Super chill staff and I love that they name their foods in an interesting way.

I ordered the YOLO. Fried chicken with biscuits and gravy. Most places in SB do not know how to make fried chicken, but The Shop does. It has a great crisp and crunch to it. Even the crunching sound sounds tasty...

My friend told me that sometimes the owner comes out to greet themselves. Next time, I hope to catch them!

This place was just "ok". Maybe I was expecting more from a brunch place with such high reviews. I had the Tugboat with salmon, and my friend had the Sweet Maria sandwich.
First of all, the food took a VERY long time to come out. The food itself was just "ok". I enjoyed the Tugboat, but it was just an embellished eggs benedict, which didnt taste like anything that special. The sandwich was very underwhelming. There was almost no seasoning on the chicken, and there wasnt enough sauce. She had to add hot sauce to add some flavor, which she never does. In addition, the chips that the sandwich came with were very bland and unseasoned. For the price that you have to pay (around $30) for two people without beverages for an uncomfortable seating area, I expected more from the food.

I think the only reason why this place is popular is because this place is dog friendly. The dogs take up a lot of extra space that could be used for human customers since the seating space is very limited.

The sign for the place is somewhat hidden so you gotta trust the map. The spot it's in has been one failed place after another so they're doing well for themselves.

You order at the stand and they bring your food to you.

Anyone who ordered a "toast" got an amazing dish. My "Eastside" was SO good.

Others ordered the Chiliquiles and they looked amazing. Beautiful plate. But nobody finished them and it wasn't cus it was too big.

There's one bathroom, fine. Everyone has gotta go when they gotta go. But when four of the guys working there follow each other into the bathroom over a period of 15 minutes, you kinda don't wanna follow them in for a long time.

We'd go back. Probably would make sure we didn't need to use the restroom ahead of time.

Most overrated overhyped spot in SB. This place used to rock but now is disgusting. Their kitchen must not have good cleanliness.. evident in the food. Biscuit was sour. Bloody Mary was watered and tasted like old wine. Disappointing way to spend my birthday.

I ordered The General, and it was awesome! The mix of apple slices and the spicy sauce was perfect in the fried chicken.. I would highly recommend this place. The vibe, outdoor seating, music, and people who run it was exactly what I was looking for.
The outdoor dinning was cool with some music on.. so beach vibe. Food was awesomely good but a little pricey. Will definitely come back.

$30 for 2 dishes and two drinks. Severely overpriced for what your get on your plate 

My portion size was fine, but my friend's was small for $13

Mostly outdoor seating.

Wouldn't recommend the place, but it is cheaper compared to most breakfast and brunch spots

This place was ok. You order at a window and they bring the food to you in their outdoor patio. Simple enough. The tables were close together so social distancing was a little hard.

Shrimp and grits (2/5) it was ok. I love shrimp and grits and have had better. My expectation may have been high. It wasnt flavorless but it was surely lacking. The grits textures were a bit grainy.

Salmon toast (4/5) topped with runny egg. This was pretty good. The capers and runny egg did not over power the smoked salmon


Overall a 3 in my book

I will start this with an apology if I rub some people wrong here, because I  have read a lot of great reviews about this place. 

I have friends that have been here and have raved about it. 

So naturally my wife and I decided to check it out. A little about me if you don't already know I am on breakfast like Marvel fans are on Iron Man. I love breakfast! It's a meal one could eat at any time in a 24-hour hour rotation.

So let's do this. 
The food is delicious. But 4 stars not 5.
The food is beautifully presented, this was 4.5 stars.  The price $12 to $14 which normally is not too bad for a decent breakfast...

.....except that the portions are suprisingly small.  What I ordered was suggested as one of the favs, the tug boat.  To be fair Tugboats are smaller than bigger boats,  but I know how big tug boats really are see.  So i was thrown abit to be served a piece of toast, with cheese, a perfectly soft poached egg with jalapenos and I had the avocado on the side.  Yummy to the tummy but left me wanting. Basically I got half a tugboat.

It felt more like a snack.  
Atmosphere (patio)  2 stars (generous)
When you read some the other reviews they will use words like quaint, that's not quaint in a good way.  The patio at In&Out has more going for it.  One review, like the unbreakable kimmy schmidt, seemed extra happy about ordering at the window taking your number where they bring you food.
 
Staff was friendly,  3.5 stars and they have a tip jar at the counter, I suggest a dollar.  You will feel good about not over tipping.
Portions-
The photos by my fellow Yelpers are beautiful, but deceptive.  Objects in mirror are closer than they appear. 
The plates are small.  Like large square saucers. This gives the illusion of wow, I don't know if I can finish that.  So when the dish comes be prepared to be impressed by the artful placement of food and simultaneously underwhelmed by it's size. 

Don't get me wrong, lovely concept, good food, but the ambiance is that of a fast food joint with fast food staff, and food ordering, but with the price of the full service eatery, minus the full service, portions and ambiance. 

Over all I give it a 3 star. 

Suggestions, clean up that patio, put up some bamboo, barrier that doesn't show the truck yard next door. Music that doesn't remind me of my age. Maybe a new patio deck look to spritz it up a bit.  It's like a gourmet taco stand without the tacos.

Okay I'm done. I feel a bit like the kid in the Emperor and his clothes.

Did I like the food?  100% yes.

Will I recommend this place to a friend? Yes, but only if they don't care about the money and they love In&Out.

Good food. Quick service. Order at the counter. Outside seating. Some indoor tables. The fish tacos were good but over seasoned in a vinegar dressing my first bite was juicy with vinegar flavors. The service was fast. My boyfriend ordered The Rollex- it had bacon, avocado and scrambled eggs but it didn't look very appealing and he said it was just ok. 

My family ordered fried chicken- it was crispy. The server came after the food was delivered to make sure everything was to or liking and immediately offered to alter anything if we wanted anything altered to our liking. Really fantastic service. The outdoor patio was very simple but welcoming. No frills. They offer espresso and cold brew. The indoor seating is not so nice- I've never seen the inside of a prison but I'd say it looks a lot like the inside of this place. But the food was good. The bathroom was clogged so a bunch of people were trying to go but I couldn't go so I can't speak to the state of the bathroom. Everyone in the kitchen was laughing and having a good time. It felt like a good spot. The food was just ok.

This is a "new American" style eatery in the lower Eastside, a rarity in the area that's known more for its taquerias. 
It's got a hipster vibe with a little Portland thrown in for good measure; most everything on the menu made in-house, like the bakery items and the salmon gravlax. 
There is seating both in and outside. This is Santa Barbara, so most people choose the "al fresco" dining option after they order at the outdoor counter, and laze about outside, twisting the big umbrellas on the tables for shade.

The menu items have clever names, like Salmon...IN YO FAAAACE, or YOLOOOOO. It's not actually spelled that way, but that's how I always feel like saying it, and I imagine I'm ironically wearing an Affliction t-shirt at the same time. 
The food itself, like I said New American, lies on the cusp of comfort food and slow-food. The mac and cheese will have some kind of twist to its sauce so it won't be like boxed stuff, and it won't be like every gastropub that has its cliche truffle mac and cheese. The cinnamon sticky bun will have a citrus zest in its frosting to give it that little extra...I don't know what. Je ne sais quoi?

Poached eggs on excellent, whether as eggs Benedict (called the Tugboat here), or the Justin...YO FAAAAAAACE (it's really gravlax on toast, plus poached eggs). 

They also serve a small selection of local beer and wine, and although they are mainly a breakfast/lunch spot, they are open late-ish during the concert season, because the Santa Barbara Bowl is about a block and a half away.

I've only eaten here once, so this may not be the most thorough review. My wife and I stopped by here on the way home from a visit to Santa Barbara. We sat outside on the patio to the left of the main building. It was a nice spot with bench seating and umbrellas if you need them. 

We were a little confused when we first walked up because there was no "Order Here" sign but we figured it out. I ordered the chilaquiles and she ordered the benedict with ham. My dish was pretty spicy, which I like, but could be a bit much for some. The green chili was on point and the cheese gave it a real creamy flavor. Her benedict was awesome. She even stabbed my fork away when I tried to get a bit. The ham was nice, thick, off-the-bone cut. Our coffees were very good as well. 

One minus was that the inside was kinda gross. We only went in to use the facilities before the car ride home. It could use a can of paint on the walls. It did smell like pee a little. If I had to sit inside, I probably would opt to eat elsewhere.

Sunday Brunch is something I look forward to every week - there's just something about brunch that hits different

The Shop Kitchen has outdoor seating and takeout available right now. You order and pay at the front and once you order, they'll seat you at a table. There was a bit of a line to order around 11:30/12 but it went by fast and we waited around 15 minutes. Once we were seated, we waited another 15 minutes or so for the food to come out. The staff was very attentive and had great customer service so kudos to them

When our food came out, I was staaarving. I ordered the tugboat with fried chicken and my table split the frenchie with fresh fruit between the four of us. The tugboat was just like your usual eggs benedict but it came with tons of avocado which I loved. One of my eggs was runny while the other was a bit overcooked sadly.
