I had the Figgin' toast. The ham was delicious, warm and not too salty. The fruit on the side was perfectly ripe (sadly so rare nowadays.) The French toast itself was awesome! The fig cream cheese and syrup were sweet but not overwhelmingly so and the whole thing was pretty well proportioned - it was a little too much food but I loved it so much I tried to finish it anyway.

Plus, the service was great. Our waitress was kind, attentive, didn't keep us waiting very long.

This spot is a little hidden since it's not right on State st, but seriously worth the 10 extra steps!

I had relatives visiting from out of the country and wanted to take them to lunch to a place with a charming atmosphere and good food. I was impressed by the reviews on here even though reading the menu left me nonplussed. But I gave it a shot anyway. DELICIOUS FOOD! So simple, yet just so, so good. I highly recommend the buttermilk fried chicken sandwich, and of course the burger with the fig jam in it. Both were fantastic. I also enjoyed the chocolate cake we ordered for dessert. The pieces were small and light, and the cake was fluffy and had a touch of cinnamon. Definitely coming back to try the brunch menu!

Wow, this place is a real gem. Amazing first spot to eat on our first trip to SB. It's in a cute area called La Arcada and we sat outside. Ordered a pomegranate mimosa and the fried chicken breakfast. The chicken was tender and delicious. It came with biscuits and this amazing jalapeño country gravy. I'd go back just for that gravy. My friend got the tomato avocado pesto panini that was also good. We're very happy to have tried this place and will be returning for sure.

This place is awesome!! Came here to eat brunch and I loved the atmosphere. Our waitress was really nice and attentive. I had the Presidio omelette and my husband had the Steak and Eggs...both were great. We will definitely be going back.

We stumbled on this place after a long drive to SB and no proper meal beforehand. After walking around for about an hour to loosen up our limbs, we decided to eat at the State & Fig. I had the Fig toasts - yummy!  My husband ordered the calamari, which came out hot crispy and with other little bits of fried veggies as a bonus (my fave!).  We then moved on to the soup.  Hearty portions were served and really nice tasting, if not a little on the salty side (Kale and Sausage, if I remember).  Last we split the Fig burger.  My mouth is watering just thinking about it all.  It was so much yummy food.  We left happy!

Worth going for just for a cool patio. Service was pretty good, they forgot the hard boiled egg on my wife's salad, but were nice about getting it once we reminded them.  I had a turkey club that was amazing.

This place was AMAZING. It is a bit hidden off the main streets but it is so quaint and dog friendly on the patio! The food was WONDERFUL - my hubby had their famous fig burger which he said was perfect (this man rarely says this :)
The server was friendly and on it! I never had an empty water cup and he made us feel at home. I had the caprese heirloom salad which was yummy and filling. The ambience was beautiful as I loved the restaurants decor, WE WILL BE BACK! Thank you!!

Welcome to another boring 3 star review.  Take a seat.


State and Fig is another one of those places where I've tasted a WAY better version of most items on the menu at OTHER places.   This spot is too mediocre for it's own damn good.  Upscale hospital food.

Look.  I understand that you're in Santa Barbara and everyone lives a rich healthy lifestyle, but with all due respect, if you're gonna have burgers and fries on the menu, you've already lost the battle on "healthy", so why don't you just go the fuck all out and flex your muscles!   Show us what you can do!

The meat was too dry and lean.  Needed a better ratio of lean meat/fat cause it was dry as hell.  I can respect the idea of grassfed beef, but sometimes it's just too lean and makes for a rather uninspired burger.  

And those boring ass fries, although fresh, were only sprinkled with sea salt.   Shit.  I was so disappointed.  I was looking forward to a juicy gourmet burger and gourmet truffle fries, garlic fries, something.   They played it too safe. 

And my friend's omelette...the only exciting thing was the goat cheese.  Nothing else.  No complex flavors.  No new spin on an omelette.  No truffle.  No rosemary.  No balsamic.  Nada.  And the rest was straightforward dry toast, fruit, etc.  


Ugh.  God.  Where's the inspiration?  Don't they teach you how to spice things up in culinary school?  And to those of you who frequent this place: Do you really come out to pay for bland, dry and boring?   If so, you should've just stayed at home.

State and Fig is my favorite lunch spot in downtown Santa Barbara. It's tucked away in a quaint part of a shopping structure next to other great restaurants and a bookstore. I like to bring out of town guest here because the area has old Spanish tile and buildings. 

The inside of the restaurant is very elegant with tall ceilings and chandeliers. It reminds me of cafes in Scotland. The staff are very nice and accommodating. 

For lunch: I love their fig and arugula salad. It's a big salad and I always leave full. I also like the fig burger with caramelized onions and a side salad. The clam chowder is truly the best chowder on State street. 

Desert: sometimes they have a Scottish putting that they serve with peanut butter biscotti. It is delicious! Ask them for the dessert of the day. 

The prices, ambiance and the food make State and Fig a winner. Try it!

There is nothing to complain about at state & fig. I've been here twice for their Sunday brunch, and both times have been great.

The food is awesome. Everything I've had bad tasted amazing, and their brunch specials are great. Truly unique combinations of breakfast food.

The food is great, but what makes stage and fig amazing it's the bottomless mimosas. Not only are the mimosas very heavy on the champaign, you never have a empty glass. Seriously, or waitress was amazing and was always there to fill up your drinks. But wasn't being intuitive. We were hanging out drinking for over 2 hours and we're never pressured to leave.

Hands down, state and fig us one of the best brunch places in Santa Barbara. I would definitely recommend it.

The great food and service made for a fantastic last night in Santa Barbara.  We truly enjoyed our experience at State & Fig.  This fantastic restaurant is in a great location just off state street.  The patio was a fantastic place for dinner and drinks.  The owner (and chef) came out and spoke with us towards the end of our meal.  He was very nice and we had a great conversation.  We will definitely come back here on our next trip.

My wife and 2 kids stopped by here for a quick visit to Santa Barbara. With my wife and I looking for a good place to eat and my son wanting pasta we came here. We say outside and had a wonderful meal. My wife and I had the tuna and my kids had a an amazing pasta dish. The desserts were excellent too. This place had a an excellent balance of food quality portion sizes and service. I will be back again!

This is a relatively new establishment on the Santa Barbara restaurant scene, and I couldn't be happier!  For Santa Barbara, the prices are relatively inexpensive, about $16/person for entree + soft drink.

The menu is simple and elegant, coordinating appropriately with the restaurant's "farmhouse chic" decor.  The service was quick and friendly, especially for a Sunday morning brunch.  My girlfriend and I arrived around 10:30 or 11AM and didn't have to wait at all.  This, I imagine, is due to its status as the new kid on the block.  (Jeannine's, on the other hand, had a massive line out the door.)

My girlfriend had the fig French toast and I had their rendition of biscuits and gravy.  The French toast was very good, not too sweet like one often finds French toast.  The biscuits and gravy were also delicious.  The biscuits, unlike the traditional Southern biscuit, were thin and crunchy and topped with a piece of fried chicken and drizzled in a jalapeno bacon gravy.  The gravy only had a hint of jalapeno, barely giving your taste buds a kick.   I really enjoyed it!  The dish also included two eggs and country potatoes.

We will definitely be taking our boyfriends back here for brunch again!  Kudos on the new establishment!

Friendly staff and creative food make this charming little hideaway a great spot for a working lunch or cozy dinner. I have eaten here more times than I can count since they opened a few years back. We now use them almost exclusively for all of our catered company lunches. Try the array of sandwiches (pork belly ftw)!

I joined my family late for lunch but ordered right before they got their food and got mine very quickly afterwards. I ordered the kids mac and cheese for little A and a clam chowder soup for myself. Little A refused to eat one bite of her mac and cheese but A and I liked it so much that we devoured it for her. I didn't try the sandwiches and salads everyone else got but everyone finished their food. This place is located in a super cute picturesque alleyway that was a bit hard to find at first but if you know it's in the alley, it's not hard to find near the end tucked next to another restaurant.
Great food!! Pomegranite mimosas are amazing!! Panini's are tasty!! Very well priced for great, quality food!
This is a great place for breakfast, brunch and lunch. The meals were prepared just right and it has a great atmosphere. Very good comfort food!

Staff was great, it seemed under attended on a weekend brunch, strange, but maybe its the holidays.

Food was good but nothing special, I will try again though if I am in town.

A friend of ours was in Goleta on a business trip, so we thought we'd meet him in Santa Barbara for dinner. This handy site directed me to State & Fig based on fellow Yelper's reviews. THANK YOU Yelp!!! This place was 'To Die For' absolutely a five star "Woohoo! As good as it gets!". We dined on a Wednesday evening with only two other tables occupied indoors, such a shame really. The inside is dimly lit , very open space, a very intimate atmosphere, open yet very cozy. I hope more people in SB discover this place, so it'll stick around a while. Come to think of it, the place next door was packed, people we waiting in line for a table. I couldn't imagine missing out on the meal I enjoyed at State & Fig. Lucky SB I suppose, so many incredible restaurants so close together. If you find yourself waiting for another restraunt in "The Arcade" on State Street, just know this little gem probably has tables open, and you will not be disappointed. 

Ok so great ambiance, so how's the FOOD?

Everything was cooked and prepared so darn well, I had wished I'd starved myself earlier so I could try more of the food, it was all so amazing. We started off with the Antipasti, do not pass it up, every little dish packed so much flavor perfection into every bite, requiring each bite to linger longer than the last, savoring each burst of flavor. Potato Arugula Salad with capers and lemon vinaigrette, roasted brussel sprouts with bacon, onions, and a mustard vinaigrette or roasted peppers, capers, basil and EVOO, crispy garbanzo beans with lemon and chilies, just to name a few of these miniature dishes of taste eruptions. By the end of the Antipasti I was in love. My son ordered the Burrata Caprese - Burrata cheese, market tomatoes, basil pesto, arugula, EVOO, cracked pepper, absolutely perfect,  in May! Who has heirloom tomatos already!?!?!  Apparently State & Fig does!

At this point I was wishing I had another stomach to fill because I ordered the Fig burger, and this may have very well been The Greatest Burger I've ever had. I even took a photo of it. Excellent 1/2 lb beef patty, thick and juicy topped with Fig jam, caramelized onions, smoked delicious bacon and blue cheese all sandwiched between the most light and fluffy, tasty bun. It was one of those meals you hurt yourself over, it all just tastes so totally wonderful. Even the french fries were the best I've ever had.
 
By now I'm passed the overly full point, to can't move lying back in my chair. So of course the kiddos had to have desert, this is another don't-pass-it-up moment. Flour-less chocolate cake for the boy served with vanilla ice cream drizzled with hot fudge, real chocolate hot fudge. And for the girl bread pudding also served with ice cream with bread pudding sauce pooling in the bottom of the dish, something for us gluten lovers and the non-gluten eaters alike, cause you know I needed to gain another 5 lbs last night, entirely my fault, I take all blame. Since i go both ways with gluten, I tried each, and washed it down with a cup of perfect espresso. 

Did I forget to mention the beer and wine selection? The choice local selections moved this place to top on my list of favorites, local breweries on tap. Wines form the Central Coast. Cannot wait to go back and bring the entire family.

As if this meal wasn't perfect enough, the icing on the cake after we'd finished the cake, at about 9:30 (all the other restaurants were closed), the chef came out from the kitchen to see if we enjoyed the meal (he knew we were all so happy and full, ha!), he  shared some of his inspiration (Antipasti the way Grandma served it) all the staff were just all around pleasant and attentive. I cannot rave about this place enough!

I am hesitant to review this restaurant because I would like to keep it as a secret and locals spot...But I just can't keep it in. When everyone is trying to get everyone else at their table to try their dish you know it's a 10 star chef. There was a line out the door when we got there... and for good reason.

My best brunch experiences! 
The food is super delicious! The place is nice! The service is great! I will definitely come back if I go visit the town again!

This restaurant is soon destined to be the best in the Santa Barbara area once others discover it as we did yesterday. The three dishes we tried were a small polenta dish, their remarkable salmon, and the ahi tuna. And, of course, the incomparable deserts (just 2!). The preparation of each was as done by a master chef (which Josh certainly is!) The service was excellent with fine suggestions for the accompanying wines. Since we've already booked a return meal this week with about a dozen friends, new kudos should be posted soon.
Delish food and great service. Will definitely come back again soon. Great sandwiches and soup. Love garlic fries.

Decided on State & Fig July 1 for brunch. The place was pretty busy with all tables full outside and a party going on inside. 

Service:  Took 25 minutes to get a table. Food came relatively fast. Waiter was nice. If there was more staff we would've only had a 10 min wait as no one could help bus the tables. 

Food:  I had the chorizo burrito and my husband had the fig burger cooked medium. The chorizo burrito was saturated with oil dripping everywhere with every bite. The fig burger was tasteless. No seasoning in the meat which was dry. The fig jam was very overwhelming.  For such good reviews of this place, it was a disappointment to us.  Never was asked if we wanted more water. Why so stingy? 

Definitely wouldn't choose to come here again based on this first time experience.

Visiting Santa Barbara, this is on a very quiet street just off of State.  The service was excellent and the food is amazing. A hidden gem of a place, and me and the wife loved our experience here. The food was very good and prices reasonable.

I really enjoyed my last brunch in Santa Barbara here. It was Sunday after Fiesta, so it was refreshing to find a place that was not too crowded in downtown. The architecture of the building is gorgeous! It used to be an old church so it has a very cool old world feel to it. The food was absolutely delicious and the ingredients are super fresh. I especially enjoyed their "small plates" and fresh squeezed orange juice. The only downside I found was that the food isn't as good of a value as other places in Santa Barbara, but overall we had a great experience.

I had the Fig Burger. It was really good, but I had an upset stomach the rest of the day for some reason which is unusual for me. Will definitely eat here again though. Great place for brunch and all of the staff were very friendly.

Wow, my new favorite brunch/lunch restaurant in Santa Barbara. The Mi Belly pork belly sandwich was cooked to perfection and the Fig burger had just the right blend of sweet and savory. Garlic fries were delish. Ambiance outside was also a nice plus. Nice job guys, we're from LA and this restaurant alone was worth the drive!
Food tasted okay but two issues. 1. They don't serve ranch? And 2. The burger I ordered I asked for medium rare and they served it almost like raw beef that was a little warm. Very strange

The brunch food was absolutely incredible. Get the grits for sure. Bottomless is the way to go and really reasonable! The patio is dog friendly and the server was super sweet. Highly recommended in DTSB

Amazing restaurant! We tried the steak frites and pork chop - both were excellent and the bacon Mac n cheese that comes with the pork chop is to die for! The crostini trio was very tasty too. We sat outside, the ambience was lovely and we had a wonderful dining experience! Would highly recommend this place.
La comida estubo fatal las amburguesa cruda, las tiras de pollo quemadas, la atención del mesero fue buena, pero la comida fatal

This charming cafe in a quiet spot right off State street was the perfect stop for lunch on our trip through Santa Barbara! Best gourmet burgers we've ever had and a remarkably good value served up quickly on the patio by the friendly staff. Thank you yelpers for leading us to a great place!

This is for State & Fig's Brunch menu. Highly recommended, although service was lackluster.

*House Pancakes ($11): Lemon/ricotta buttermilk pancakes, blueberry compote, powdered sugar, choice of bacon, ham or sausage. //// I am usually indifferent to pancakes, but these are super tasty. They are fluffy, moist, and slightly sweet. My friend ordered sausage to come with it, but it was really dry. McDonalds/Carls Jr. does better breakfast sausage than this. So just order bacon! Recommended. 

PBR (Lunch Plate) ($11): Crisp pork belly, caraway kraut, Swiss, Russian dressing, griddled rye ////  My friend said it wasn't bad, but it may be because she isn't used to eating pork belly. I think it tastes better the next day than when it is ordered. The caraway kraut was bright and needed. Overall, a good sandwich. 

Clam Chowder Bowl ($7.00): It's a good bowl of clam chowder with smoked bacon. Dip fries in if you have them. 

SPECIALS:
Pork Belly Hash ($14): Pork belly/peppers/onions/apples/butternut squash/thyme/gold potato //// A lot of potato in this, but it's not bad. I would choose the other dishes over this one if I had to, but it's still a good dish. Came with fruit, which was a refreshing contrast to the heavy hash. 

Salmon Hash ($15): Salmon/roasted peppers/onions/gold potato /// The salmon came through strongly on this one and the potatoes didn't dominate the dish so I think it was better than the Pork Belly Hash. My friend liked it. 

*Short Rib Benedict ($15): Short rib/ arugula/pesto hollandaise/ 2 poached eggs/ english muffin/ roasted potatoes/ fruit /// So good. The short ribs were fall-apart tender, and the portions were really big to me. The english muffins are a little dry/chewy, and may be hard to cut, but once you break open the poached eggs, it should lend them some moistness. Recommended!

Po Boy ($13.50): Poor Po Boy. Needs seasoning. Definitely do not recommend, although it comes with a side of delicious fries.

SERVICE
When we were able to get the waitress to check on us, she was super nice and friendly. Still, when there were only three other tables inside, you would think we wouldn't have to wave her down multiple times. She also forget things multiple times when we asked her (another order of clam chowder, mimosa plz, an order of arnold palmer)

Good food, good location. Beautiful day, everyone in our patty was happy with the food, the service & people watching. Feels like a European cafe. Garden sandwich, turkey sandwich & biscuit & chicken all big hits.

The food is what sets this place high on my list. It's a must while in Santa Barbara. The restaurant is situated in a quaint little part of downtown. The ambiance captures the essence of what I love about this city. The architecture, location and the food is phenomenal. 

Came on a girls trip with my girlfriends & we all loved this bistro. Wasn't too busy on Presidents' Day. Waitress was friendly and quickly took our orders. We ordered all ordered mimosas that were perfectly proportioned. The clam chowder was sooooo delicious. Garlic fries were on point and just the way I like them... with the right amount of garlic. The BLTA was fantastic.

Went here for brunch and really enjoyed the food and awesome service (Ashley was super friendly and accommodating with our large party.) I had the scramble with chorizo and it was AMAZING! Came with home style red potatoes and fruit.

There bottomless mimosas for $18 and you can get a bunch of different flavors! Pomegranate, classic orange or mango and they are HEAVY on the champagne. My friends were drunk by the end :) 

Super cute atmosphere, modern with a rustic charm. Would recommend as a brunch or lunch spot if you are looking for something nice but casual downtown!

Remodel has made ALL the difference. Warm interior, beautiful photography, a total makeover. Very happy for Marisa and her husband, they have worked hard and it shows. Great lunch crowd today and I hope it stays that way. Enjoyed their speciality Fig Burger - blue cheese, caramelized onions, arugula, bacon and fig jam..great shoestring friends. Friend had the bacon mac & cheese, great portions and tasty! Looking forward to trying other items on the menu - pork belly sandwich is next on my list. Their daily specials looked delicious as well. Go out and support local business!

Great spontaneous lunch in beautiful Santa Barbara! Relaxing, outdoor seating available. 
Staff was prompt and polite. Thumbs up for the sausage and kale soup. 

One down side is their garlic fries. Regular fries are great, but the garlic fries are soggy and bland. 

Overall, lovely dining experience!
We had brussel sprouts to start and split a burger. Everything was delicious. Service was a little slow but very nice.

State and Fig is a nice place to grab brunch or lunch in a casual yet charming atmosphere. The menu is pretty simple offering a few sandwiches, burgers, salads, and soups- all satisfying yet not particularly extraordinary. It's set in a beautiful boutique style outdoor shopping mall and is surrounded by many great Santa Barbara attractions. Leaving the restaurant just a few feet to the left is the breathtakingly beautiful courthouse that is definitely worth taking a walk around to admire. Also close is the ever popular State St. which provides walking access to great shopping, museums, culture and entertainment. The staff is pleasant helpful but like the food don't really leave a memorable impression. Conveniently there is a public parking lot just around the corner that is free for the first hour and a half for those of us who have personal cars. Overall I give State and Fig 3 stars and will most likely return at some point to catch up with a friend and grab a business-casual bite to eat.

We were in town for Thanksgiving weekend. Our hotel recommended this after several other tapas places were full. We were delighted - took great care of us and two daughters. Food was delicious: clams and bread were particularly AMAZING! Kind of quiet and simple decor - made for easy conversation and great attention from staff.

We used State & Fig for our rehearsal dinner in October. Marisa, the owner/manager, was extremely helpful when we were in a bind because our original location fell through a couple weeks before. We're so lucky S&F was even available for a party of our size because it's an amazing restaurant with delicious food located in a gorgeous courtyard near all of SB's action on State Street. They accommodated our group of 50 people and supplied us with a stellar menu. Beyond the amazing food, they provided great service and helped make the evening as perfect as we hoped. We're definitely looking forward to returning as regular diners next time to venture to the area from LA.

What a great find! With so many places to dine al fresco in Santa Barbara it is hard to know which are worth it but State & Fig hits it out of the park.  

This small restaurant in the art gallery alley ways off state has a fairly small inside dining area as well as a patio.  It gets crowded during lunch so be sure to head over before the rush hour.

The food was all delicious and I personally recommend the Kali Club.  The other people I dined with all got salads and just raved about each of them.
A cute little place with tasty, fresh food!  I would definitely stop here again!

Awesome place for brunch in Santa Barbara.  After checking the yelp reviews for restaurants near where we were (thanks yelpers!) we decided to try out State and Fig.  My husband went with the Mac and Cheese and I went with the french toast and both were delish!  I loved the whatever the fig middle thing was.  I had no issues with the service.  We were asking the waiter lots of touristy questions but he was nice enough to answer them for us.

They also have a great mimosa deal $15 gets you unlimited mimosas.
Love this spot.  It's in my regular rotation.  Lunch menu is one of the best deals in SB.

This is still the best restaurant in Santa Barbara!! During this past year we have brought over 80 guests here and EVERYONE has agreed with this description! Never had even a mediocre meal! We never take a chance... Always State&Fig

I really enjoyed my visit. First, my mom, sister, and I ordered 2 meals to split. When we got our order they split our plates for us. Even out panini was in 3rds! So thoughtful. We had Mac n cheese which was cheese, rich and delicious. Our panini was ham and fig. Good flavor. You could really taste the fig. I was so happy to sit outside and enjoy the day.
Went here for my birthday. The atmosphere is laid back. Everything we ordered was absolutely delicious, especially the gnocchi.

A couple friends and I decided to try out this place while vacationing in Santa Barbara. Definitely a great spot to eat brunch. It has a nice homey feel with two stories. We sat upstairs. I would recommend the salmon hash. Everyone enjoyed their meal. It might be on the pricey side, but so worth it!

The clam chowder was to die for-the best I had, in years.
Burgers are excellent as well.
Great place with great location.

We visited on a Friday night and although we were the only ones on the patio service was pretty slow. We were given two wines menus instead of actual food menus haha :) no biggie. Sat on the patio with our pooch enjoying the evening so the slow service wasn't a big deal. Food took quite some time. 

Had salmon which was delicious :) fiancé had chicken...superb :) 
The man that helps the server (wish I had gotten his name) is the heart of that place! He brought our dog a water bowl, he was so kind and constantly checked on us. He is such a gift to that place. Their food is fantastic but he was so real and genuine and we pay attention to that stuff. 

I'm sure well be back with family. :)

Loved the service and food. 

Got the Fig burger, the cheese, fig jam, caramelized onion, and burger patty was a perfect mix of flavors!! 

And if you get fries. You WILL upgrade to the garlic and rosemary fries. I NEVER finish my fries but I did here. Better than any typical truffle fries and Parmesan you'll ever eat.

This place is pretty low key and delicious!
Food: always good! Takes a little while to get food once ordered so don't come here if your about to kill your significant other because your "hangry." 
I would always recommend the pork chops!! They are so damn good and served with Mac & cheese that you can't miss up. 
Atmosphere: so quiet! We've brought our four year old brother here before and it was to quiet for him to be here. But perfect for first date or date night! 
Drinks: they have a huge wine selection and for beer they have several in bottle and only 3 on draft but that's okay! 
Service: pretty dang good! Since it is hardly ever packed, they are there for all of your questions and on top of refills, etc! 
Would totally recommend this place. 
Sorry I was starving so don't have any pictures but trust me it's good!

Such a cute, rustic little place. We are on the patio, and the whole atmosphere inside and out is great. They serve breakfast during lunch (til 2:30). I had the yummy portobello panini, and my friend had one of the breakfast scrambles. Both tasty, and nice presentation.

I love brunch! To me, breakfast foods and a little day drinking with friends is the epitome of a relaxing day off. State and fig is a good spot to do just that.

The outside has the more desirable seating but the interior is not bad either if you don't feel like waiting. 

I was perfectly happy with my Benedict. It was tasty and well prepared. I only wish I got more house potatoes as there were very few- about 1/3 of what other places usually serve. 

Our server was attentive and readily refilled the bottomless mimosas (which you too can have for $17 with purchase of a meal). Our server poured a stiff drink - about 90 champagne :) 

All the items were tasty and I'd gladly return here again.
The food was delicious, the clam chowder had bacon bits among other ingredients made it so flavorful it's  the best in town. The chicken pesto sandwich was incredible.

We chose this restaurant because of the good reviews on Yelp but it was disappointing. It is just your average sandwich and salad spot and the restaurant didn't seem clean. I would not go back as there are many other great restaurants in Santa Barbara.

Love this place. Good food, awesome prices and great service. The burgers are great, the flavors in everything are spot on and it's really affordable for lunch. Plus they have a nice patio seating for days you want to be outside - pretty much every day here.
Went for dinner and liked it so much, we went back for brunch the next day!  Highly recommend!  Make sure to get the Brussels sprouts appetizer and tomato salad.
Terrific service! I strongly recommend the triple toast sample and the polenta. Wonderful!

The service was great. This place has the best mac&cheese I've ever tasted! We had the Fig Burger. I was hoping this burger would change my opinion about bleu cheese but it didn't. lol Fiancé and I don't like bleu cheese but we're open minded. I think the burger itself was really good and if I had it without the bleu cheese, I would love it. Would definitely come back.

State & Fig is a great place for lunch, tucked in a small walkway of different shops/restaurants. I came for a late lunch on a Monday around 3pm and pretty much had the whole place to myself. I had a portebello mushroom panini and couple bites of the fig burger. 

The portebello mushroom panini included a generous amount of red bell peppers. The bread had a touch of pesto sauce and it all melted nicely together with provolone cheese. This also came with a side of arugula salad. I loved how they put the vinaigrette dressing on the side.

I had a few bites of the burger and it was just ok. I did enjoy the fries that came with, lightly crunchy and not overly salty. 

Service was ok, can't complain, prices were fair. I'd come back to State & Fig in the future.
I was somewhat disappointed when told I was too late for breakfast at 11am, but there was a brunch menu in the window. However, my chicken sandwich was really good.

This place had a great atmosphere and a great menu. We went for lunch. I had the fig burger with blue cheese. It was very flavorful. The fries were a little disappointing (small and over cooked). Fig Panini was recommended as well.

I love being able to have 'brunch' any day of the week - inspired idea!  Went here recently and my friends had eggs benedict and one of the special salads and a soup.  both extremely happy with their meals.  I ordered the 'fig burger' and it was amazing!  I asked for medium and that's how it came!!  Also had the rosemary garlic fries and I would go back just for those!

Service was nice and the place was packed.  Had to ask for extra water, but that's a minor thing.  We were offered extra iced tea and Arnold Palmers though, so all good!

Lovely place to go.  Shame they are only open Wed - Sat for dinner.  But that's better than nothing!!

This place is so quaint and cute! I came for bottomless mimosa brunch with a friend. SO GOOD. We shared the "Gaucho" breakfast burrito and the fish tacos. Decently sized portions and the salad that came with both plates was delicious. The fish tacos were kind of dry, but with the salsa (pretty spicy btw) they were good. The Gaucho was one of the best breakfast burritos I've had. The melted cheese and the hangar steak, WOW YUM. The girl who was serving us was so on top of it as well. Our glasses were never empty for more than 30 seconds! They're not stingy with their champagne either. That's the ideal kind of bottomless mimosa service I'm looking for. Love this place, & definitely going to come back to find out if there's a bottom to bottomless mimosas.

The mac&cheese was mainly cheese with some macaroni in it and the olive oil chicken was a pool of olive oil with chicken in it. 

Its opposite day,

Just read the menu backwards and you'll get what  you expect.

Caitlin was a beautiful star in the sky of our vacation. A shooting star who trailed delicious mimosas and primo service. I do not live in Santa Barbara but if I did, would come back every Saturday for the AMAZING food and EXCELLENT service. (So good caps are required, I promise.)

This isn't a review for their food since we didn't get to try it.

They open at 10:30AM and BFF & I were starving by the time we got there. Keep in mind we were up at 7AM and practically tried to kill time and actually waited for this restaurant to open to have our 1st meal.

However, at 10:30, they were still setting up. More time passes by and it doesn't seem like they're ready to be serving soon. 

Ended up next door at Jeannine's since we couldn't wait any longer for grub.

WOW! This place is a hidden gem....but not for long. The food is absolutely amazing. Best benedict I have ever had and the fried chicken and biscuits is unmatched. Excellent service and the owners are very friendly and engaging....Everything is great! cant wait for them to open for dinner!

My wife and I have been in Santa Barbara just under a year now and finally made it in to State & Fig and I'm so glad we did.  The food was amazing and the service was impeccable.  Big thanks to Doug for helping make our experience memorable!

We walked all the way from the Funk Zone to eat lunch here based on reviews and both dishes we ordered were pretty bad. I ordered a chicken panini which had cheese and olive salsa verde. The entire thing was dry, except the panini bread which was an oily, soggy mess. There was no flavor. It was the worst sandwich/panini I have ever tasted. We also ordered the candied burger and all the toppings were great, but the burger itself was cooked until there were no more juices left. Dry, dry, dry. Will not go back. I do not recommend to anyone. Fries are good. That's about it.
Great spot for lunch. Get the garlic fries and have the fig burger. You won't regret. Lovely place to sit outside and and people watch!
Terrific meal last night! Good service. Well priced. Inviting menu. Highly recommend this place.
The service was very friendly and the atmosphere was nice. We were very disappointed by the menu. We ordered a salad and hamburger. Both were bland.

We searched for this place after reading the great reviews.  It didn't disappoint!  I had the salmon salad (with 2 mimosa's) and my son had the children's cheeseburger. Yummy!  The atmosphere was perfect - awesome Santa Barbara vibe.

I have enjoyed the food, atmosphere, and staff here every time. Great place for brunch on the weekend! Awesome lunch too!

Definitely recommend it!

Today I enjoyed the buttermilk chicken and bacon jalapeno gravy on biscuits for brunch. It came with excellent home fries and eggs. Delicious!

Great food. I had fig burger, everything was fresh and hot. My friend had BLTA it was also good. The chips are excellent!!! The fries are ok order the chips. The service was good. The restaurant was clean.
BLTA was real good.  Not too greasy or rich as they sometimes can be.  Size was spot on with the fries for a good lunch portion.  Quick friendly service at a later lunch hour.

The pesto omelette was pretty good as was the toast and jam. The garlic fries were very very garlic-y. And the lamb sammy left much to be desired. Overall was a bit overpriced, but so are most things in santa barbara. 

The location and venue were really nice, tucked away on Figueroa Street. And the wait staff were very friendly and accommodating.

This place was not busy at all on a Saturday night around 830pm. We ordered the following - 

Tasting trio of toasts - 3/5 just ok, fig toast was good
Crispy Brussel sprouts - 3/5 just ok, a little spicy for me. The Brussel sprouts look like chips. 
Short ribs with polenta 4/5 - really good! 

This place is just ok for me. Nothing special but at least I enjoyed the short rib!
This place is pretty amazing! Great food and drinks! Patio is pretty awesome and it has a great breeze coming through that helps beat the hangover if applicable.

We've had two dinners here since our daughter started UCSB, and both meals were beautiful. If you like upscale burgers, they have wonderful choices. Several salads and I had a gnocchi with mushrooms which was good. 

The real treat was the latte after our meal and the beautiful decor, along with a professional and attentive staff. We'll be back.
Excellent ground beef in their burgers. The patio seating made for pleasant al fresco experience. Our waitress was kind and attentive. The entire experience was ideally Santa Barbara.

Yummy!!
All that State & Fig is comprised in that word. The hubby and I were looking for a place to eat when he stumbled across this place on yelp. 

It is located in a beautiful courtyard full of many restaurants. As soon as we walked in we were promptly greeted and advised to sit where we would like. We choose to sit outside. I ordered the Tuscan sausage and Kale soup and he got a turkey burger. My soup was cooked to perfection. It was full of veggies but not overly salty. I also got a side of fries. Note: the side could be shared by four people. 

Our server was great! He offered many suggestions and even told us our options for visiting the pier.  He felt more like a friend than someone just doing the job. A lot of servers could learn from him. 

Next time we are back in Santa Barbara we will return.

We arrived for our 8:30 reservation on a Saturday night and took an outside table as inside was pretty crowded and noisy. We ordered the Eggplant Parmesan to share as an appetizer and it was delicious. Very flavorful and nicely presented in a mini kettle pot. My boyfriend had the flatiron steak which came with an amazing side of mac & cheese and roasted vegetables. He really enjoyed his meal (as did I - just had to taste the M&C). I had the grilled halibut with a medley of chopped vegetables. The presentation was beautiful and the flavors rich and wonderful. We practically licked our plates! We weren't in the mood for wine, and quite honestly too full for dessert, but we were very tempted by the butterscotch pudding on the menu. Prices were fair for the meals and the atmosphere of eating in the arcada was romantic and made it feel like we were on vacation just a little. Staff was very friendly and attentive. I would recommend and will go there again.

The ambience was great. The portion sizes were good. The server was fantastic. The food was a tad on the bland side (I had the pappardelle, the wife had the salmon carbonara) but not bad by any means. We'll try it again for sure. Highly recommend.

This has become our new favorite restaurant in town.  The food is unique and really good.  The fig burger is excellent with a touch of sweet and savory at the same time.  And clam chowder is better than most that you would find back east!  Add to that the owners often come around to the tables and check on how you are enjoying the food, it is really a nice experience.

I highly recommend the seasonal arugula salad with the dates, green apple slices and raspberry vinaigrette this summer of 2016. We also shared the minestrone with tons of fresh veggies (zucchini, carrots, tomatoes). Soup was ok tasting; a bit bland for my taste. The fig burger was disappointing as the blue cheese over powered the fig jam. Meat patty was nothing special. I do not recommend the fig burger unless you're a fan of blue cheese. Go elsewhere for burgers.
Great food, service and atmosphere. Weekend brunches - especially the chicken and biscuits are epic!

Have been here twice now for dinner had great experiences both times!  This time we brought done friends for a birthday dinner.   We sat upstairs to get a little more intimate feel, even though the waitress had to go up and down the stairs we never felt neglected! 

All the food was on point from appetizers to steaks to pastas!  They have an a good wine list and some beers for those non wine drinkers like my friend.

I felt like the staff cared about the food and our experience!  We will definitely be back again, hopefully to try the brunch!

I honestly don't know why this place has such good reviews. I feel that this is a huge huge yelp fail. I am only giving two stars because the place itself is adorable and makes you feel like you're eating on the streets of Europe. Now, here are my complaints. The sandwiches my dad and I ordered were both disgustingly oozing with aioli (which was not even really aioli - more what I would call straight mayonnaise). My dad forced it down, but as I cannot stand mayonnaise, I wanted to order something else. Frustratingly enough, the waitress never came back to ask us how the food was. After a full 15 minutes of my dad waving his hands in the air to catch her attention, she finally came over and I ordered the Mediterranean salad with chicken. Guess what? The salad came with the chicken very obviously undercooked. How the chef missed this huge detail? I couldn't tell you. By this time, I had had enough with the restaurant and ate only the lettuce. When the waitress came back, my dad told her that the chicken was undercooked, only so that the chef could be aware of his very dangerous mistake. The waitress came back with the check with the price of the sandwich and the chicken I added to the salad removed, which we appreciated. Never never ever going back again. Next time I'll enjoy the street with just a walk by.

Had lunch here for my birthday recently. I really wanted to like this place. It is in a nice space, although it is out of the way and a little bit hard to find, it has reasonable prices for Santa Barbara, and it has a decently varied menu. The service was fine. I had the House Burger and it was only alright, not bad at all, but not really a "wow" either, and the fries were totally forgettable, I think they sat for awhile since they were barely warm. For me, if an upscale place can't produce a really good burger and fries at lunch, I question how good the rest of the menu is. I probably won't go back.
Super tasty food, nice setting, and great service. We had the Brunch Burger and Fig Salad and both were terrific. And don't miss the garlic fries. This place didn't disappoint!

The food and ambiance was great, but the service could have been a lot better. I got the breakfast burrito since you could never go wrong with that, but I do wish they had hot sauce floating around somewhere. We got there on a busy Sunday afternoon, and it took 20ish minutes to get a table, and it didn't seem like they had a very efficient system for it ( we just kept making eye contact with the waiters until they came up to us). It's located on a really cute alley way on state street, and they definitely weren't too happy about a younger crowd coming in. My friend asked about just getting the bottomless mimosas ($17) without food and we got a very rude "this is not a bar scene" instead of them just saying no. Some of us did end up getting the bottomless mimosas, and the champagne definitely did its duty. Overall, the visit was okay, but I am going to be looking for other brunch places in the area as well.

A great little gem right off the beaten path of bustling State Street. Tucked away in a off shoot walking only street- still plenty of people watching, just a little more laid back. The outdoor tables are lovely if the weather is nice.... Which it always is in Santa Barbara!

The service was horrible. It took over an hour to get our food. The place was not busy at all and there were several tables waiting for their food. What was so frustrating was that there was no communication. It would have helped if our waitress came outside and apologized for the wait. Instead, my husband had to go inside the restaurant to see what the problem was. One of the other tables that was out on the patio with us cancelled their order and left. This is really unfortaunate because their food was really good. Our experience in regards to the service was so bad that we will not be back.

My new fave lunch spot in SB is State & Fig.  The restaurant itself is charming, bright and airy (during the day... I'm sure the ambiance is great at night, too!) and the staff is friendly and helpful.  I had a seasonal salad with arugula, dates, apples, feta, pistachios and red onion.  It was absolutely delicious and bursting with flavor.  I had my eye on the antipasti and can't wait to return to try some small plates.  Great value and beautifully prepared seasonal food.  Yum!

I don't give too many 5's...but if any place should get a 5, this is the place!
A bit off the main drag but still great location; staff friendly and very knowledgeable;  menu small but still something for all. 
The chicken dish is great. The clam chowder is as good as any I've ever had, including great places in Boston and Philly. 
...a really great little place!

My wife and I were in Santa Barbara for a few days for my birthday and the first night there we ate at State and Fig. I had the special which was Sea Bass with gnocchi and shrimp in a pesto sauce and my wife had a hamburger. The sea bass dish was fantastic and my wife said that the burger was one of the best that she ever had.  Though Santa Barbara is a wine town, there was a great chocolate stout that they carried which we really enjoyed. The staff was really attentive and friendly. The ended up being our favorite dining experience of the whole trip.
I love the ambiance! One of my favorite little alleys in Santa Barbara...very romantic and European feeling. The food was really good, too!
Really great food. Went here once and will be back. Got the pork chop and the Mac n cheese was incredible! The service was excellent too.

This place is hands down my favorite brunch spot in SB. Everything I've ordered here has been absolutely delicious, but I would highly recommend the Fig'n Toast, which is a unique and flavorful spin on the average french toast. If you're in the mood for a little more variety of food I would recommend the Bello Benedict and the Fig Burger!

Not only is the food delicious, but the atmosphere is great since outside seating is offered as well which is perfect on a sunny day. The only complaint I have is that the service could definitely be better especially considering that the multiple times I have gone there has not been that many people.
Horrible service and after waiting an hour because the hostess never put our name on the list I asked for a simple egg white omelette and she said no substitutes. I will never ever come here again.
Chicken entree was deeeeeelicious and eggplant parm was very tasty too. Very reasonably priced. Nice service and quaint outdoor seating.
Amazing sausage and great servers. If you go here, get the sausage, it's the best you'll ever have. Get the sausage on the side of Figg'in toast for sure.

Had a late lunch here on 2/2/17. The service was excellent and friendly.  I got the portobello panini which was yummy.  I upgraded to the fries as a side and didn't regret it, they were fresh and delicious.

Only great things to say here. 

Staff as friendly, prompt, and very knowledgeable when it came to the food. 

Food was sooo good. Ordered the garlic Parmesan fries. A bit much on the rosemary they included in but besides that, quite tasty. And they give you plenty so you don't have to be greedy. 

For dinner my husband and I shared the porkchop with brussel sprouts and perhaps the best bacon Mac n cheese I've ever had. Quite a generous portion too! Walked away completely full and with a very happy belly! We I'll be back!

I thought the food was a bit over priced.  $12 for a simple sandwich was a bit much.  I was never asked for my preference with side order.  I don't eat potato chips so I was a bit sad about that.  I drink water and there was never an open opportunity to get a refill on my glass.  I guess I could have gone back up to the counter again. The food was very tasty though.  I'm wondering if I went on an off day.

My husband, baby, and I popped in on Saturday night for an early dinner, and the staff was very friendly, welcoming, and accommodating to us with the baby and stroller.

The service was excellent- very attentive but without being overdone.

My husband enjoyed a glass of Cab that was delicious, and we ordered two appetizers to try out.  The Tuscan kale and sausage soup was hot and bursting with flavor, and came with a nicely grilled piece of bread perfect for soaking up the broth.  The portion was generous- I could have ordered it as my entree and been satisfied.  We also ordered the Crispy Calamari and Shrimp with Romesco dipping sauce, and I was loving how light and crispy they were, and the garnish of kale chips and lemon slices were fun too!

For our entrees, my husband chose the Cider Brined Pork Chop with soft polenta, roasted brussel sprouts with a maple reduction.  Um, yum.  He's not usually a brussel sprouts fan, but he had no problem finishing  them up along with the rest of the meal.  everything was perfectly cooked, and the sweet/salty flavors were nicely done.

I ordered the Butternut Squash Gnocchi with kale and pecorino (I think?) and it was such a great choice!  I'm still thinking about it and craving it now.  The gnocchi was perfectly pillowy and the butternut squash puree was silky and sweet.  

The ambiance is really great too- dimly lit for dinner, beautiful artwork, and gorgeous hardwood flooring.  I even commented on the cool chairs!

I have now added State & Fig to my list of favorites in town.  We'll definitely be back, and we can't wait to try breakfast and lunch too!
Really good, no complaints. Pig and fig sandwich was amazing, rosemary fries a must. The chicken panini was also great. Outdoor and indoor seating available. Easy public parking

This is a nice spot to have a leisurely lunch. They have outdoor seating in a quiet alley space - it reminded me of the French District in San Francisco. So quaint, with simple but delicious sandwiches and salads. Fairly reasonable price for the food and atmosphere. I'd go again if I find myself back in Santa Barbara.

Our standard stop when we stop in SB, we usually split a Kali Club.
This time it was chilly and drizzly, aka perfect weather for shorts, so we split a bowl of the Bacon Clam Chowder.
Perhaps the waiter did not realize the gravitas when I said it was the best we've ever had.
My dad, from Maine, has sent more New England clam chowder along the East coast back to restaurant kitchens than he has eaten.. he would rant about most of it being 'budada' [potato] chowder.

So here we get plenty of clams, tender!, and properly cut, low on the potato, the right consistency - not too thick nor overly creamy. 
Yep, bacon nails it. Oyster crackers of course. Next time... a whole bowl for me.

Very cute location, very good service but the food was just OK for me. Too much salt and nothing to make me want to come back soon. I do recommend though for the fun and romantic atmosphere and friendly staff.

Unfortunately, we were not impressed with State & Fig. We were in Santa Barbara for a day trip and turned to yelp for a good place to eat. We had a late lunch on a Saturday and there were the patio area was probably 2/3 full. We opted to sit inside because remaining patio seats had some sun exposure. The inside only had one other party but it was a late lunch.

Anyhow, we ordered the fish taco and the kali club. And they were both okay. The kali club was probably better than the fish taco but it was a standard sandwich with nothing special about it. The fish taco was very average if that and definitely way pricey for what it was. $16 for two mediocre tacos? Yeah, we were disappointed...

The outdoor patio and the indoor seating area were nice. Our server was also nice but not very helpful. Well, I guess he answered our questions but I think he basically said everything was pretty good. I'm used to them giving a more persuasive yes or no. But really, no complaints there. It's just that I didn't think the food was worth the price. Usually at these prices, there should be more of a wow or unique factor and we didn't feel that at all.
Hands down, now it's my favorite lunch spot. It was raining when I went so the outdoor seating was non existent. Anyway i liked it. Good food and refreshing drinks, that's enough for make me happy.

Classier place for lunch. Think nice hotel restaurant. Great turkey melt (uniquely prepared -- not just turkey and cheese) for about $15 with choice of side. Not that crowded, and service was excellent.
Good location...great food....had the pork belly hash....wine list..large menu....bring friends...indoor outdoor seating

Very accommodating! I came with a party of 8 people during graduation weekend. With no reservations to any restaurants, our party decided to call every restaurant on State street. With the help of a fellow yelper and friend Sonia H., we were able to get a table at State & Fig. The hostess warned us beforehand the only available table was outside and they had no heatlamp. Not phased, we decided to take this table. The food was pretty good. I ordered the braised beef short ribs, and it was definitely tender as I did not have to use my knife at all!!!! However, because it was so cold outside, my dish got cold really fast, and it became less appealing as it got colder. So my advice to State & Fig is to set up a canopy area (like the restaurant next door) for the outdoor seating and add heat lamp. Until then, I am keeping 1 stars from you!

First things first, dear chef, for the love of tastebuds in Santa Barbara,  please stop serving the marmalade gruel with the duck. Thankfully, the duck was delicious. My sister ordered the seafood soup special and loved it. Last negative comment, a cleaner bathroom would have been appreciated.

Stopped for a quick snack and glass of wine, so glad we did!  The rose wine was fantastic and the fig and lemon ricotta toast as well as the warm Brie with grilled grapes were delicious!  Quaint ambience, a good mid point visit before our 2 mile walk to dinner.

Came here last year and it was great! Bottomless mimosas were $13 which was great! Service was awesome too. BUT I came back today and it was AWFUL. Worst service ever and they lagged with everything. Food was okay but definitely didn't match the price (better go to a Mexican deli or Panera). Mimosas were weak. Won't be coming back. Please don't waste your time coming here..
Sorry! Haha forgot to add that my friend found hair in her food

The fig burger was awesome and not quite what I was expecting. I've had Brie with fig but never bleu cheese. It was interesting and fun to try. It pairs well with the caramelized onions and bacon. I enjoyed the combination but it was very rich. 

They had awesome fries. Nice and crispy on the outside and soft on the inside. Served with ketchup and a mellow aioli. Overall delicious!

Nice patio seating with umbrellas and great customer service. One girl helping all tables. She was on it! Fast service with care!
Best  birthday lunch and the first place i ever had a BLT! Double points :)

Love the outdoor patio vibe... made for a fabulous brunch to celebrate my cousins graduation from college!  They had an awesome selection of bloody Mary's.  Try the lemon pepper one if you like your Mary hot.  I got lucky and they had an avocado toast special as a starter.  When I asked about it she told me they could top it with a poached egg for me and make it more of a meal.  All I can say is it was on point, It was just the perfect amount of food to not leave me feeling gross, if you aren't into eating a something too heavy early.  My aunt had the eggs Benedict and she literally licked her plate, so I didn't yet a bite, but I think it is safe to say it was delish.

This is a relatively new establishment in the ever-exploding Santa Barbara food scene (which, unfortunately, is really lacking in diversity). State & Fig, aptly named for its location, only started their dinner service a couple of months ago. They started out as a brunch/lunch place to test out the waters.

Dining on they outdoor courtyard is quite lovely on a really nice summer night. The inside is charming, dimly lit, and romantic. 

The staff is really nice and easy to talk to. They gave us recommendations for the starters. 

We ordered the antipasti and chose the crispy garbanzo beans, potatoes, and brussel sprouts. Each were so flavorful and really lived up to the term "appetizer." We were definitely excited to eat after that. 

The boyfriend ordered the short rib with soft polenta and I ordered the fig burger. The burger was really good. The sweet fig jam was a nice contrast to the blue cheese and the patty was juicy. The burger was large and filling. The boyfriend's short rib was so tender. However, my favorite part has got to be the soft polenta. It was SO GOOD. It was creamy, cheesy, salty without being inedible. So much OOMPH in that polenta. My second favorite was the budino for dessert. It was like eating little spoonfuls of heaven. 

I am big fan of this place, and I am eager to come back to try their brunch.

Very nice atmosphere. Most of our party had burgers, which were good but a bit messy. They were able to swap out the beef patty for chicken breast on one of them which was great. They are mostly beer and wine so no cocktails, which was a bit of a let down. Overall it was a good though and we would probably come back.
Great food. I am satisfied. I ordered the special food which was delicious. The server and other staff were very attentive. The place is located in downtown Santa Barbara.

Celebrated UCSB graduation dinner with group of 7 people.  Food, service and ambiance were all excellent.  Everybody in the group raved about the food - fig toast, fig burger, short ribs, salmon, & gnocchi were excellent.  Would definitely visit again!

I've been here twice for lunch and it's always clean and the service is very friendly. The inside is comfortable and breezy, and the outdoor patio is shady and quiet - either way you win.

Both times I ordered the pig & fig. It's amazing! Ham and fig on delicious bread. Definitely recommend. The chips seem homemade and are light and crispy. 

Check this place out! They also have a great brunch menu.

I have had lunch and dinner at S&F and it never disappoints. The burgers are so filling and tender. The flavors are perfect. And if you aren't afraid of garlic definitely order the garlic fries. Caprese salad with chicken is also great.

Came here around 12:00 pm and it certainly wasn't as crowded at Jeannine's next door. I wanted to try this place out despite the reviews about the poor service. Our waiter looked like he didn't want to be there--but who would? It's July 4th weekend! We don't blame him.

I got an item off the brunch menu. Chicken and gravy or something along those lines. It had a really nice presentation for something that's messy and pretty unphotogenic. There was a lot of variety on the plate. Two poached eggs atop fried chicken atop cornbread atop a bed of herb gravy. It was savory and pretty good, though nothing to really rave about. I'm a bit biased though since I am more of a salad and soup kind of person.

Husband got the breakfast burrito and complained that there was too much potato in it. It was very very filling. The greens in his salad were also browning and not fresh.
Every thing was surprisingly good here. If you have to get only one thing, my vote would be the short rib, it was amazing!

Loved this place! We came here for a bachelorette lunch with the girls! I ordered the fig burger and it was perfect! The interior of the cafe is very vintage and it has a nice ambiance. Patio seating is also available!

This is one of my favorite restaurants in Santa Barbara. I've had a few sandwiches, salads, and breakfast foods and they've all been great! Plus the prices are incredibly reasonable. Half the time I'm taking home half of my sandwich! Go here!

Went back here again and all I can say is Pork Chop, Pork Chop, Pork Chop....get it. That's all there is to it. My wife got the salmon and loved it also! We asked why didn't come back more often, it's that good. Get the Pork Chop!

We were sad hungry puppy parents who had just dropped off our 10-week-old lab with the breeder for puppy school in Monterey...for a month. 
On our way home to L.A., my husband and I stopped for lunch (1/20/17).  We were sad and hungry! We ordered from the lunch menu.  He had the BBQ Cheeseburger, and I the Shorty Melt. We also shared a cup of Clam Chowder. All were excellent choices! Food was great and service was warm and friendly too.  The restaurant has a romantic casual elegance to it.  I also had 2 cups of their good, hot, and strong coffee too! Neither of us took photos of our food or the inside of the restaurant.  : ( 
We will definitely be back when in Santa Barbara!
Great ambiance. I recommend the Presidio scramble.

My husband and I were in Town this weekend to celebrate our three years anniversary, so we were looking for places to eat and run into this place and I loved the patio so we ate lunch there on Friday. I had a chicken  and my hubby had fish tacos which were not that grate I would rate them at 3. Then the next day we went back for dinner which changed our expectation for this place! The food was amazing as well as our sever

I hate that it has taken me this long to write a review since I was so impressed with this place when I was there 2wks ago! 

I love everything about this place. It totally has the essence that I love about Santa Barbara from the architecture, a downtown location, close to shopping, great service and the food is spectacular! 

I ordered the french toast with the fig spread and it was amazing! 

I've found my favorite brunch spot in SB here ... At the corner of State & Figueroa. I hope to be back soon for another weekend trip.

I dont give out 5 stars ever...until now...AMAZING.   Had the salmon, which was unlike any I have had before.   The wife had the fig burger, which I had a taste of and it was incredible.  Wait staff was awesome.   I just wish I didn't live an hour and a half away, or I would be here all the time.

Ok the brunch is tasty! My poached eggs for the salmon Benny were cooked to perfection, the bottomless mimosas heck ya but our server :/ she wasn't 'on it' instead she was on her phone texting and whatever, sorry but service when I eat out is a must!!! Reason for service is I can eat just as tasty food at home with bottomless mimosas for a whole lot less $$$! Service service service!
Very yummy meal. Will definitely come back. Had the short ribs entree and the warm Brie appetizer.  Must save room for bread pudding!!!!
Good food, great service, nfe outdoor space, bathrooms were very lacking.....no return.....
Love this place! The food and service is awesome and you have to try their amazing chocolate cake!

Neat patio bistro with an interior that's bigger than it looks at first blush (because you don't immediately notice the upstairs dining area until you check the place out more carefully).

A great server who knew his stuff pointed us in the direction of their wonderful grilled asparagus salad, followed by their roasted organic chicken (a "whole half chicken" which was enough to feed me and my evil twin brother), and their mahi mahi special for the evening. Everything was excellent. As was the neat Tocai Friulano wine the server suggested, and which went perfectly with what we ordered.

Finished with one of the best plum tarts I can remember ever eating and walked away happy, food-satiated tourists.

Amazing salmon, sweet potato, goat cheese and farro salad!  (Great combination!) Salmon was seasoned and cooked perfectly!  Such a cute, cozy little place.  Perfect for lunch!  Wines by the glass are top notch and the service is warm, attentive and gracious!
The hours are wrong. They are not open at 2:30pm on a Tuesday even though yelp said it was. Thabk goodness there are plenty of other places to eat in the area.
Delicious unique comfort food (grilled scallop salad with fresh avocado) that will entice your crea8tive side and leave you wanting more.....
Great starters!!!  Brussel sprouts were yummy.  Great service, simple and enjoyable decor.

Wow, Super Impressed!  Wife and I dropped in for dinner tonight. We ordered three small plates to start, including the Calamari/Shrimp, Arugula Salad, and Pork Belly Appetizer. All three were excellent!!  For the main we split the Beef Short Rib w/ truffle cheese polenta entree which was OUT OF THIS WORLD amazing!  

The service was great...very attentive and friendly.  Wines were great. The owner Patrick came out and introduced himself. I really appreciate it when the owner of an establishment takes the time to talk with the customers. Super nice guy!  

We hear it's a very kid-friendly place so we're looking forward to bringing our son for breakfast this weekend!

I actually never tried the food here because after 15 minutes of waiting to get a menu, my friend and I left. The restaurant was fully staffed with 4 servers but only half-full at 2:30 yet everyone was sitting and waiting to be served.

On our way up to a concert at the Arlington we decided to stop by for a quick bite.  Appropriately named due to proximity, State & Fig is tucked away just off of the busy main road of State Street. It seemed a bit slow for a Friday night but maybe we were there early.

The beer selection was somewhat limited but the wine list seemed more extensive. However we were there for the food. I was pretty hungry so I went with the Fig Burger. This signature burger sure did deliver on flavor and taste. The bacon and bleu cheese complimented the fig jam to perfection. Although its not the cheapest burger I've had it was worth every penny and at least fries were included. The lady enjoyed a special meatball plate with a seasonal salad. Both dishes were a perfect satisfying meal that didn't weigh us down for the show.

Service for us was prompt and helpful. The meal was delicious. I'm sure we will be back.

We were there for their very first night of dinner service. People didn't know they were open for dinner so it was not crowded, but they had a full complement of staff.
Their staff is friendly and attentive and we swapped good hiking locations.
I had the Roasted Organic Chicken with harvest risoni, (like rissoto meets rice-a-roni in  a good way), and green olive salsa verde. The chicken was tender and delicious, but an enormous portion. Even with Chinese style sharing with my table mates I still took home a doggie box.
The menu looked delicious and I wanted to try lots of dishes, but alas my seat mates all ordered the braised short ribs, roasted carrots,soft polenta, arugula and truffled pecorino dish. The meat was packed with flavors and fall off the bone tender. I loved the polenta, carrots and all.
Nice desserts too. We were helpless to resist the flourless chocolate cake with whipped cream, not too sweet to counterpoint the sinful cake.
I liked the ambient lighting, the soft warm faux walls and high old world ceilings. I'll go again.

I love the food here. It's kind of a best kept secret. The arugula salad is to die for with figs and apples. Fantastic burgers. The clam chowder is over-the-top. Their polenta  is scrumptious. Service is excellent. Try this place!!
Food was so yummy. I ordered the open faced Chicken Biscuit with eggs and gravy. Service was good. Atmosphere was cool. The chef/owner came out and said hello. Will be back!
Amazing food, authentic service. Have the burger...have the biscuits...have the Benedict. All at once!!

Food and service were fantastic!!! I had the pig and fig sandwich and it had a ton of ham and the fig spread was delicious! There are signs to find it and it has a get patio area with tons of seating. Definitely recommend. The prices were reasonable too! $25 for two people for lunch!

The food is great, the service is terrible.

We called a few days ahead to let them know we would be coming with a big group, they said they did not take reservations. We tried calling again the day before to let them know we were for sure coming, with 16 people. We wanted to make sure they were ready for us.

When we got there, it took them 20 minutes to seat us. Not a big deal, since of course they don't take reservations (however they did know we were coming). They seated us in two separate tables (which again, isn't a big deal, but hey, we called ahead and let them know, should have been prepared). We all ordered bottomless mimosas, and an entrée. The food was delicious.  But with the bottomless mimosas, they stopped serving us because they said we were averaging a bottle per person and it was a liability. I asked how many bottles we had at that point, and the waitress told us we had 10. Well, I am no math genius, but that is only a little more half a bottle per person. Which comes out to maybe two-two and a half mimosas. When you are there for 2 hours, that isn't going overboard. So much for "bottomless". 

The service was bad, the staff was rude, but hey, at least the food was good.

We will not be returning.

I was looking for a new restaurant to try in downtown SB for a day trip and noticed great reviews for State and Fig on Yelp. I love their location, inside La Arcada courtyard and their menu looked good. 

We stopped by for lunch and we wanted to be seated outside, to enjoy a nice summer breezy afternoon. Great outdoor area, spacious. I liked their indoor space as well, , airy, with modern, chic- rustic furniture and cool art on the walls. Nothing pretentious, but cute, elegant and simple. But the courtyard was irresistible. 

We ordered 2 State Burgers and enjoyed them (with arugula, provolone, avocado and great, fresh tomatoes, sprinkled with pepper, just delicious). Loved their buns and the aioli basil sauce. Great fries to go with! Very nice, upscale gourmet, tasty burgers. 

Service was nice, we were trying to pick our beer (they have a great selection of local wines and local indie beers on tap) and the waitress (very knowledgeable) offered to bring us a few beers on tap that sounded good to us to sample. So we tried a Summer Ale Firestone (good, bit like a Sam Adams summer ale or Hefeweizen) and a Telegraph beer (local indie brewery) - which we chose, Amber, darker, what we wanted. It was nice to have that offered, it never happened to us before.  

I'm sure their breakfast food is great, we want to try it sometime. They close at 4pm in the weekends and open again after 5:30 for dinner.

Nice meal, great environment, charming place. See why my fellow Yelpers raved about this place!

This isn't my first time here, but sadly this review is being written after having my worst experience. 

We literally showed up at 5:33 pm, we were the only people there. Getting seated was a bit of an awkward experience because the host wasn't very assertive. 

Our server also didn't seem totally comfortable with what he was doing. He brought our salad out and one of the plates was dirty, so I had him take it back and put it on a fresh plate. 

Then, I ordered a burger, The Candy Apple. We ordered all of our food at the same time, but due to "some mixup in the kitchen" my burger arrived almost 30 minutes later than the rest of our food. (Remember when we arrived we were the only ones there and the first to place out order.) 

Now when we were done and our check was brought to us our server did thoroughly apologize which was greatly appreciated. I hope that this is not an experience that anyone else has. 

**The food was delicious though. I recommend the Brie toast and the crispy brussel sprouts.**

Couldn't be a better location.  It is located in a breeze way off State, so you have a lot going on, but not all the craziness of State St.  Parking was easy in the Figueroa parking garage and just a short walk.  There is a store across the walkway that was filled with beautiful Christmas decorations making it very festive.

Although they didn't have a children's menu, they fixed their "fried chicken" from the menu into a meal for the Punk.  Chicken and french fries, her staple.

We had a guest diner with us and she ordered the Tomato Panini and was more than pleased with it.  They come with green salads on the side, so lighter options are available.

We held our wedding reception lunch at State & Fig. Everything from getting a menu together to the service to the food went off without a hitch. The owners are also awesome people and were very nice and helpful. 

Our table had basically every option of our menu, including arugula salad, eggs benedict, salmon, butterscotch pudding, and apple crumble. Everything tasted delicious and was as good as we'd hoped after we had our tasting beforehand. The mimosas were also quite a hit.

The servers were very professional and it doesn't seem like it's staffed by a bunch of kids (which is refreshing). We couldn't have asked for more from the service. It made for a perfect day.
I had the steak special here last night. It was amazing, and it was one of the best meal i had for this price. Although they were very busy, the service was excellent too.

Sadly just another place that falls short of my expectatuons. We had a large group for dinner on a Saturday night and just wanted to eat after a long day of wine tasting. Our waiter was pretentious and just dampened our experience. We never was asked if we wanted water at our table, we had to wait 1 1/2 hours for our food AND when he finally served us, he never came back to find out how the food was. A few of our dishes we're terrible. Overcooked pork chops, extremely runny alfredo, and mediocre  short rib. 
Three stars just for location and atmosphere, had nothing to do with the quality of food and the snobby waiter.

OMG!  This restaurant is so wonderful!  My husband (omnivore) and I (vegan) were visiting Santa Barbara and just happened on this great restaurant.  Best meal we've had in a restaurant in a long time.  He had the special of the day: Ling cod with roasted tomatoes and potatoes in a great sauce and I had the arugula salad (without the manchego cheese) which even without the cheese was spectacular--it had red onions, dates, figs, pistachios in a great balsamic vinaigrette.  I also had the crispy brussel sprouts.  My husband is very hard to please and he was so happy.  The portions are perfect--not too small and not too large.  Always hate when portions are so big you can't finish and you feel like you're wasting food.  Anyway, if you're visiting Santa Barbara or lucky enough to live there, don't miss this place.  Service was great too!

3 stars okay let me start: after a treacherous long drive to Santa Barbara we decided to try State & Fig. Pictures looked good but boy it started off wrong from the awkward moment of being greeted. 

Richard our waiter was quiet and not quite attentive to us. Now let me say we were the ONLY 2 ppl besides staff in the restaurant @ 5:30pm when they opened. We sat, looked @ menu and put our orders in. We got: The Misto Salad, Brussel sprouts, apricot Brie toast and bff got the candy apple burger with garlic fries. 

We got served the misto salad on a filthy plate, told Richard about the plate in which was visible, he returned salad on a clean plate shortly after. We then got all our entrees shortly after except The candy apple burger. After telling both Richard and hostess of where the burger was which was approximately 30 minutes no burger done with ALL our food but missing burger. Both Richard and Hostess said it was a misunderstanding in the kitchen. Ok sure but how does that happen when we were the ONLY ones in that restaurant. Killed it all to be honest. Just wasn't happy or satisfied. Bff lost appetite shortly after. Food was good I'm not complaining about that. But the flow didn't flow it just was off completely.  
Richard did apologize but which was nice but mid dinner he left us flat, MIA on other tables. 

Food was about $33 bucks for 2. 

Worst place seems like management needs some attention. I won't be back. 

Food was good.

I love State and Fig!! Let me start with one of my biggest selling points: bottomless mimosas EVERYDAY until 3pm! That is incredibly hard to come by, even on a weekend. My fiancee and I have made State and Fig one of our regular spots on the weekends. Aside from their delicious flowing mimosas, they have great food. I love anything caprese, and State and Fig has every combination of caprese I could ever want: scramble, omelet, salad, panini. What will I try next?! My fiancee has gotten the breakfast burrito, which is delish and a few other dishes, and has never been let down. My former college roommate and still very, very close friend (and vegan) came into town to visit us, and of course we took her to State and Fig! She did not have any problems finding something on the menu that she could eat, and actually really enjoy.
The staff is extremely friendly and not once have we had to wait to be seated. They don't rush you through your meal so that you'll stop enjoying mimosas, in fact, they actually let you hangout longer! We went in one day for a leisurely brunch, finished eating, but were still enjoying our time and the waiter let us know that he'd keep refilling our drinks because bottomless did not end until 3pm.
I have always had a great experience at State and Fig, and it's definitely our favorite spot to go for weekend brunch.

Not much of a brunch gal but this place might have turned me into a "BRUNCH BELIEVER". 

I was able to visit this location during my SB Trip this weekend with a few of my local friends and this place was to die for! Of course, I partook in the bottomless mimosas and loved every combo they had to offer (OJ, Mango, Pom). Also I was able to try three different dishes since all my friends ordered something different.
