If you are a cook or the chef you should see that this situation gets corrected because no fault to you this place is going to go outta business. To all the locals living in SB send'em packing back to LA.

I have dined at State and Fig twice...really good.  Third try was beyond a BUST
From  start to kind of finish, staff was rude and indifferent.  I waited 30mins for a table and 15 mins was waiting for the table to be cleared.  I finally gave up and went to Anderson's and had great experience

Had high hopes for this restaurant from the reviews. Came for dinner to find out they were closed without updating their storefront signs, Yelp, voicemail, or hours on google. So came back again the next day for brunch. 

Got the state burger with fries.

State burger- the inner edges of the bun and meat patty were burnt black. Would've tasted good if the burnt taste wasn't so BITTER (had to spit out my chewed up ood from the bitterness) and distracting from the dish. 

Fries- good and crispy. Also some fries were burnt at the ends (understandable since most restaurants have it). The burnt parts were easier to remove than the saucy burger patty and buns. 

Told the waiter who didn't do anything about it.

Came here on an early Thursday afternoon for my birthday lunch. The area this is situated in is so cute - definitely sit outside! We ordered the Fig Burger and Fried Chicken Sandwich - both were absolutely amazing. So much flavor and every bite was delicious. Our server was great and she even had the cook cut both sandwiches in half since we were sharing, as well as split up the fries and salad portions on our own plates. This place is a gem, I would definitely come back again if we are ever in Santa Barbara.

As recent transplants we've been on a vigorous and calorically enhanced mission to sample every restaurant in Santa Barbara. We now can declare definitively that STATE & FIG is the best burger. Boom. Start with a lovely brioche bun from a local bakery on De La Vina, the half pound burger is steak quality beef, cooked perfectly (my wife a well done; me a medium), with options that are complex but not silly as is often the case. I chose 'The Fig' with fig jam, grilled onions, arugula and blue cheese, just enough blend of tastes to enhance but not overwhelm the meat. The garlic fries are a revelation -- and if someone could figure a way to deliver them to me when I'm in my jammies watching Colbert eviscerate our clown in the White House, I'd call it heaven. Also noteworthy is a very genial and gregarious staff: in particular, Tracey, a fellow transplant from Pennsylvania who helped my wife figure out where to yoga, to massage, to pedicure and other verbs I'm making up. It's in that cozy courtyard at 1114 State and a great hang out. I don't eat much red meat so when I do, I do not want to waste my sinfulness on stinkiness! This is a better burger than any I've had in L.A. (maybe Pono Burger in Santa Monica is close). On we go exploring -- but this will become a regular stop!

Perfect place to go for bottomless mimosas on a Saturday afternoon. The brunch is amazing. Only complaint, which really isn't even a complain.... is they only had one server. Javier was incredible but they had no one to help him out...

Javier gave the ultimate service to our party! The food is beyond delicious however the service speaks volumes of the atmosphere and Javier surpasses all expectations! Our drinks were always filled and the food was exceptional! Thank you so much! Would definitely recommend this fabulous establishment!

On the weekend it's often difficult to find a high quality brunch or lunch place without waiting a half hour for a table, so I was pleased to find the charming State & Fig. The Fig burger was all it was cracked up to be so I'll definitely be back to try what looked to be some fabulous other dishes. Service was really excellent as well.

I had a wonderful lunch here in the summer. My friend and I ordered the Fig Salad and split the truffle fries with various dipping sauces. It's the perfect place for a long lunch, right in the heart of downtown Santa Barbara.

This place is located just off of W. Figueroa and just east off of State St. Fastest way to get to them is to enter the back pathway from Figueroa and it will be in the right side; near the turtle pond.

I came here with my family and the food was delicious and our server was friendly. You can either eat outside or inside. We chose to eat outside because the weather was perfect. We didn't have to worry about direct sunlight in our faces due to high buildings surrounding the area offering plenty of shade. 

My family and I ate their short ribs Benedict, BLTA (bacon, lettuce, tomato, and avocado) sandwich with chips, and a chorizo omelette. All of their food was quite delicious and fresh. The avocados were fresh and not old. The short rib meat was tender and fell apart easily. 

Prices can vary from $12-$22 depending on what you get. Beer, wine, and mimosas are available as well.

"Tracy is literately the best server I've ever had in my entire life. She definitely deserves a solid raise. Every time my mimosa needed a refill, she was there before I even asked. I love it." -miles hogan

What an adorable spot for brunch! Right in the middle of State St. this is in the La Arcada plaza which also has super cute stores to explore while you're here. We came on a Saturday at about 1pm and it was not crowded at all. We were seated right away at a table in the outside seating area which was exactly what I had hoped for so that we could enjoy the beautiful Santa Barbara weather. 

-Fig burger - Holy smokes, this was totally delicious!! 5 stars for this! I really wanted to try something with fig given the name of the restaurant so I opted for the burger. There was the perfect amount of fig jam spread on the bun such that I tasted the hint of sweetness in every bite but that it didn't overpower the burger. The bacon and caramelized onions also added a lot to the burger! Of note, I opted to get the burger without the bleu cheese as it's not really my favorite cheese. 

-Short rib benedict - Exactly what I imagined. Short rib was tasty, soft, and tender. I thought that there was too much hollandaise for me drenched over the benedict and that it was quite oily but all in all, still enjoyed it. The poached eggs were perfect. Home fries on the side was not crispy enough on the outside nor seasoned enough which I was sad about. 3.5 stars for this dish and not sure if it's worth the $18.5. 

I will most definitely want to return here and try some other dishes if I get a chance to come back to Santa Barbara!

Solid 4.5 stars. If your in search of a great cheese burger you have to add this place to your list!

The bun soft and on point- the burger was about as juicy as you can get- the avocado and arugula and tomato all fresh and bringing it all together. The only thing I would change is the cheese/ the cheese game was def on point however I would have preferred a sharp chedder or something that packs a punch vs the subtlety that mozzarella has.  

The Garlic/Rosemary fries that came with this 5 stars! Not too many places that say it's garlic fries really deliver- this place did not hold back on the garlic- just the way I like it. 

All in the total was $10.00 awesome value right off State street...

(Pic posted as well)

food was tasty but service was bad. I think they were under staffed that day on account if a local parade. they ended up blinking my friends food 30 min after mine arrived, which is poor etiquette. the place has both indoor and outdoor seating. the food was creative and flavorful. maybe best to try on off peak hours. the food we ended up getting was the short rib Benedict and the brunch burger which was spicy.

Hubby and I were in town for a wedding and arrived a day early...strolled through this gorgeous downtown of Santa Barbara.  State and Fig was on our list of places to eat.  Came for "linner" around 3 pm.  I ordered the Fig burger, substituted the cheese for provolone.  I loved the sweetness of the fig jam!! It's a must try.  Paired my burger with garlic fries.  It didn't disappoint.

Service was wonderful.  They were attentive, giving us suggestions and were very nice throughout our meal.  I love the quaint and the restaurant building is stunning.  Love the long steps that go up to the 2nd floor.

Very nice little spot located in a small corridor off State St. We got there close to when it was time for them to close and they were very cool and didn't rush us in anyway. We definitely closed it down and we were very comfortable until we finished our food. I think we showed up at 2:30 and they closed at 3:00. We didn't leave until 3:30. 

I'm not suggesting anyone push it and do what we did but we are grateful they didn't rush us.
Worst service I have experienced. Will not be returning. Food tasted like it came from the bottom of a pond.
Fast service with nice servers! The food was great, I had the presidio burrito and it was a good size. The mimosa proportions are also perfect!

After 4 years I was able to find my way back to this amazing restaurant. The fam decided we needed a quick weekend getaway, so off to Santa Barbara we went! My one must stop place to eat was State and Fig. I'm am sooooo glad this place has been able to stay in business during covid!!! We were kindly greeted by a young gentleman who gave us a menu and told us to go inside to the counter when we were ready to order and then we would be seated outside afterwards. I ordered the French Toast stuffed fig cream cheese. OMG it was so good. The toast had a nice crunch to it, and then when you hit the cream cheese filling...IT'S HEAVEN. With big smiles and full bellies we went off on our day. As long as State and Fig is open, they can count me in as a loyal customer! thanks so much for always making great food and providing a great dining experience!

Amazing burger and amazing service! I ordered the State Burger with Rosemary Fries and it was the best thing that I ate all day. The burger is topped with basil aioli, baby arugula, tomato, avocado, and provolone cheese. It was just what I needed!

First off, two words: BOTTOMLESS MIMOSAS!! They have the traditional ones, but for an extra two bucks you can do bottomless mimosas of other kinds (pomegranate and mango, and others depending the season). The service was great! All the staff was friendly, helpful, and fast. I came with a girl friend for brunch and we both loved our server. I went ahead and ordered the pesto mushroom omelet and my friend the breakfast burrito and we both sounded like bees buzzing, it was THAT GOOD! The restaurant has a nice view outside and the inside has two floors. Perfect place to have a girl's brunch or family breakfast!

This was my first time eating at state & fig, and it is honestly a hidden gem in uptown state street. If you are looking for a new brunch place to try out and catch up with some friends, then this place is perfect. It has a spacious, open floor plan and comfortable seating. I went with two of my friends and experienced a zero wait time on a Sunday right before lunch time. 

For the food, I ordered the mushroom pesto omelette. The portion size was generous and there were many sides included with it. My friend ordered the figgin' toast, and it was very rich, creamy and flavorful. If I go back again, I will lean towards ordering the fig oriented dishes next time! The figgin' toast was fairly decadent, so I suggest sharing this with another person if you want to try a couple things on the menu.

Visited SB yesterday and our party of 5 was trying to get brunch. Been going to SB for 30 years, know the town intimately. How is the food you ask? Well sadly I would have no clue. It's not a huge place but adequate. Their outside 4-5 tables were full as were their inside 5-6 tables. They have an upstairs seating area which they chose not to use. 

Why the 1 star? Because we were completely snubbed. We were awkwardly standing by the door (we were the only party patiently waiting, chill Sunday for us) and the 3 employees literally walked by us 20 times in total and not one of them ever made eye contact with us, made a gesture or uttered a word, it was brutal. Finally on pass 21 I asked "Is anyone ever going to talk to us?" She replied hastily "well we will, we are understaffed" and walked off. 

I mean I expect a 20-30 minute wait in SB at any restaurant at any time, but I also expect to be acknowledged and greeted, they left us for dead. 

We walked out, literally went next door to Jeanine's which I'd never been to. We were warmly greeted immediately (yes) and ordered and were eating within 10 minutes. Jeanine's wasn't amazing however solid 4 stars and a killer good looking and tasting Bloody Mary was ordered by one of us, they def have some passion for what they do. 

I'll never try to come back to this restaurant, they chose to be in customer service, they have to do much much better.
When you let someone book a table for 25 people and then just straight up don't have a table when we arrive - that's next level.

We had a wedding rehearsal dinner at State & Fig and could not have been happier.  The food was delicious and the ambiance was perfect.  The owner and staff were extremely helpful, professional, and courteous.

Restaurant has been here for many years. First time coming in and actually eating. Food was good I had the Fig Burger, very tasty. The pork belly sandwich was a little lacking. Service was friendly and attentive. Medium priced for good food right off of State Street in the Arcadia mall

One of my new favorite restaurants in Santa Barbara!!
I just finished lunch with a friend.  He had a grilled salmon on arugula salad and I had a burger and fries. There is very little that they could have done to make what we had better! It was perfectly cooked. Looked and tasted great! The service was friendly and fast. The price was fair. 

Just a few blocks from my office... I will be back!

Good Food, Cute Location, 80% Hit/ 20% Miss Service. Been here a couple times now because they have one of the best Bottomless Mimosas in SB for under $20. The food is always good and the menu has a good variety so everyone can find something they like. Two biggest issues are the consistency of the drink, and the Consistency of the service. Drinks if not ordered as bottomless will vary depending on who makes them, some can be more heavy handed than other on the proportions of things. Service is contingent on, well I'm not, maybe people just being human and making mistakes who knows. But the last time I was there I was asked to give them my name and they would call it out so I stayed on a bench nearby and double the time they told us it would be went by and no name was called. Then we saw a larger party walk up and immediately get seated. Upon further inspection we saw several open tables so we took initiate and went back up to ask for a spot again. Maybe it was a fluke and they forgot about us, but this tends to happen when you go with just 2 people, anytime it's 3+ the service seems better.

People say I wouldn't make a good mother. And they are correct. I don't like children. But if my child was as wonderful as State & Fig, I might reconsider giving motherhood a shot if I wasn't already past my prime.

Like a newborn in its crib, this place is tucked away so neatly in the charming La Arcada shopping center. And also like a newborn, you could easily walk right past it and not even notice it. Partly because Cielito next door behaves like an obnoxious older brother craving all the attention with its sparkly decor and loud patrons. But trust me, don't make eye contact with Cielito, unless you like throwing your money away on tiny plates of overpriced tapas.

March right past it to my little DARLING of a restaurant, State & Fig. While I usually like to try different dishes, I find myself ordering the same thing every time. The Fig Burger. TO DIE FOR. This bundle of joy is everything you want in a burger with its fig jam, bacon, carmelized onion, arugula and bleu cheese. It's sweet, savory, melty and crunchy all at the same time. Can you even? I haven't had something that good in my mouth since I accidentally swallowed a tablet of ecstasy back in the late 90s (in my defense, I thought it was aspirin...I had a raging hangover).

And now to the staff. They are absolutely charming and just plain adorable! They are the only humans I've ever felt motherly towards. I feel as though they could spit in my food (not that they ever would)  and I'd still love them unconditionally. Like the youngest child in a large family, they can do no wrong in my eyes.

Go to State & Fig. And tell them Olive sent you. That'll really confuse them.

Honestly don't understand why this place is 4 stars because it is the worst brunch place I've ever been to. I'm from San Francisco so I'm used to trying various brunch places, and this was just not it. 

I ordered the fig burger with garlic fries and it was a pretty decent burger. Didn't like the blue cheese but that's my fault for ordering it. The fries had a strange aftertaste and didn't taste like garlic. The herbs they seasoned it with gave off a bad taste too. 

I also tried the short ribs Benedict from my friend and it was horrible. Extremely salty and tasted like corned beef. The whites in one of her eggs weren't cooked and was inedible. Not worth it for $23 which is extremely overpriced for something of such poor quality. 

My other friend got a mango iced tea and it tasted like dirty water. I don't really understand how you could mess up iced tea but she couldn't even drink it and had to request another drink. 

Also they refused to seat us when 2/5 members of our party were running late when the restaurant was half empty. Just overall nothing good about this place.

What terrible service. We had a party of four and there was an open four top. We stood there for a long time and we're ignored. The menu looked decent, but we were invisible. We ended up going to the place next door near the fountain. Great food. Great service. Never going back to State and Fig
Bottomless mimosas are the moveeee! It gets very busy sometimes but the outdoor patio, shade, and good vibes are worth it! Come happy. Leave happy.
Ordered an Easter Dinner package - both the quality and quantity exceeded expectations! It was the highlight of my quarantine! Will order from them again.

Stopped in for Breakfast and it was a great experience!  Love the food, location and the lovely owner.  We both had the breakfast burrito which was flavorful and filling!  Don't miss out on this great restaurant and check out the awesome tile on the back wall (the owner even told us where we could buy some).  Thanks for a great morning!

Definitely have to try the brunch options here. The pork belly was crispy and savory. Always enjoy having the aioli to go along with the fries. The side of fruit and home fries is filling. Top it off with a mimosa ( or make it bottomless) and you've got a complete and gorgeous area to enjoy a meal with good company!

Jocelyn was the most amazing server! She was very attentive to our needs and a very down to earth girl. She gave us the opportunity to not have to think of our experience and to just have a great experience. This company is so blessed to have such a wonderful server. She made my best friends visit very very amazing. We will always come back here :)

In our opinion, State & Fig has to be the best rehearsal dinner venue in Santa Barbara. Patrick and his team are incredible. Patrick worked with us to craft a perfect, personalized menu. After two long meetings with Patrick in which he gave us his absolute attention and truly seemed to want to know more about us, the outcome of the rehearsal dinner was absolutely wonderful. The rehearsal dinner can easily fall down the list of wedding to-dos, and Patrick and his team knew that. They worked extra hard to ensure that the night was a success without us having to go back-and-forth with them the way we did with other vendors. Patrick asked us questions about flavors that remind us of childhood, foods we cook together, memorable date night dinners... We left both meetings with Patrick feeling like we'd somehow fallen in love all over again. I don't know how but there it is.

After our first meeting with Patrick, we knew we could trust him, and because of that, we had no worries about the rehearsal dinner. The pricing was transparent and friendly to our budget, the food choices were incredible (people still talk about the dessert), and the venue layout and decor were great. The staff was incredible the night of the event, and so many of our guests raved about them. We have never experienced service at the level demonstrated by the State & Fig wait staff. State & Fig is a truly professional operation when it comes to rehearsal dinners (or similar events I am sure), and we could not have been happier with our experience. It was an intimate, memorable night filled with all the people we love and truly exceptional food. Thank you, Patrick and State & Fig staff!

I love how this restaurant is tucked away up an alley way, such cute decor inside too. Very roomy with stairs that go up to more dining.  There is also an outdoor patio area.  I ordered the Salmon Club Sandwich and it was very tasty, it had arugula, crisp thick tomato slices, avocado, bacon and salmon pieces with mayo and dill pickle on the side.   Half of that sandwich and huge plate of crisp potato chips was filling enough, I finished the entire thing and needed my hike afterwards.  This can easily be shared.   They have a nice Sunday Brunch menu- worth stopping by to checkout.  They also have beer on tap from local brewery Figueroa.   The service is quick and friendly and they have kids menu's with cute sticky sticks to keep the kids busy- I love them for this. :)) Prices range from 12-15 on most items in here and kids menu prices around 7-8.   This place is located right next door to a pastry/coffee/restaurant- so save room for a nice hot espresso afterwards...:))

Bad food and horrible spotty service. Upon arrival we could already see that the servers seemed to be running round like crazy. We were then warned that because of a few big parties the kitchen was backed up a bit. We thought that it couldn't be that bad and sat down. Then it took forever to get menus and we almost left...I really wish we had. 

Very cute place with indoor and outdoor seating. Potentially good food that wasn't done well. My husband and I wanted to get away from the LA for half a day and decided to come to SB on a Saturday. After driving here we were hungry and were looking forward to some good food. Instead we got spotty horrible service. The busboy was much more responsive than the servers. We could barely even get their attention. The kitchen was slow but we were warned about that. The food not good at all.

Fig toast
This seemed to be something that everyone liked when they ordered it and I had to get it. When it can out it was pretty underwhelming. Very small portion of thickly sliced bread that had been fried up then the fig cream cheese mix just slathered in between. The French toast part wasn't fried up until crispy at all and was just mooshy. Made even mushier by the fig filling. Worse they had decided to pour syrup directly on the plate before putting the French toast on top. A big mushy mess. Overly sweet already but too too sweet with the syrup it was soaking in.

PBR
Pork belly and sauerkraut on toasted rye with house chips. This had potential also...but didn't come out well. The house chips were extremely greasy and not very good. The sandwich was slathered in sauerkraut and drowned the entire sandwich. The pork belly was cooked nicely and was tasty on its own but entirely overwhelmed by the equal amount of sauerkraut. They also decided to plate this loosely held sandwich at a tilted angle. The whole thing was falling apart before it even got to our table,

I really wanted to like state and fig. Didn't happen. Bad food and service. We did eat everything because we were so hungry by the time we got our food. The kitchen was slow but it was made worse by the slow service. The fig toast was $12 also! For such a small portion it wasn't worth it unless it was extremely good.

Went in today for brunch and was sort of confused? Staff seemed unprofessional both in their casual dress and behavior. We stood around awkwardly by the entrance for a bit until someone approached to seat us. It took a while, but not terribly long, to get the food which looked better than it tasted. I was so hungry I ate half of my Chicken Panini before realizing that the off taste was from the chicken having a weird rubbery texture. Mixed greens were starting to brown on the edges, rest of the food wasn't very remarkable, but maybe was just an off day?
Burgers are overpriced same with Mesa burger, by the time it's delivered it's over 20 dollars  pricey for a burger when you can eat a A grass fed steak  for less:-)

After getting off the train, we were determined to find a solid spot for breakfast/brunch. State & Fig is about a 10-15 minute walk from the station and it is located in a quiet and quaint alley in the hustle and bustle of SB's main promenade. 

Service was fast and we were seated immediately. Their patio seating gets filled up rather quickly so we had to opt for indoor seating. 

They had many options for mimosas/bellinis, and the food menu was very inviting.

I split the eggs benny and french toast with my mother. Heads up - the french toast is extremely sweet. I consider myself to have a sweet tooth and this was just too much for me as well.

The savory options, however, are probably your best bet and will leave you feeling full!

Beautiful outdoor cafe seating like Italy, variety on menu w 
Most items $14.50-$17. Tasty food, be sure to sit under umbrella as it gets warm

State & Fig is a hidden gem with the cutest little outdoor patio. I came here with some girlfriends for big birthday brunch. There was a big group of 11 of us. They were accommodating and put tables together so that we could sit in the outdoor patio area. We were a little bummed that we did not get to order everything from the original menu, as they let us know that our menu would be different because we were such a big party. A few things were not available to order. I ended up opting for lunch and got the burger which was a great choice. 
A big reason why we came here is we wanted endless mimosas. The champagne was alright, not the best, but we stayed and enjoyed many anyway. The service was great and the food was amazing. I would come here again and skip the mimosas next time.

I found this cute hidden spot through Yelp and am so glad I did! We sat outside and enjoyed the beautiful Santa Barbara sunshine. We ordered their fig cream cheese french toast, the pesto mushroom omelette, fried chicken and biscuits, and the chilaquiles. Every food item that we ordered was delicious and huge portions! The fig cream cheese french toast was amazing. I would recommend sharing it because it is so sweet and rich in flavor and a few bites is plenty. All of the food came out hot and fresh. Everything was well prepared and flavorful. They also have a great mimosa/bottom less brunch. Our experience here was excellent and we recommend it!

Loved that they were able to accommodate a group with 3 dogs, so we all got seated outside for brunch.  The staff was really attentive, kept the drinks coming, and brought out lots of small requests from our group including many sides of ketchup.  The portions were pretty large and could probably be split by two moderately hungry people.  I got an omelet which also came with sides of potatoes and toast, and it was all delicious!  Really enjoyed the brunch menu at this spot outdoors tucked away in a quaint little alley.

Been coming here for years and always enjoy the pleasant wait staff.

I love the BBQ burger;  the meat is very good and I particularly like the fixins':  instead of the standard lettuce and tomato, it comes with spicy slaw and crispy onion strings. Also bacon and topped off with the BBQ sauce.  Choice of in-house made potato chips or generous salad.  Altogether excellent!

Lovely little patio restaurant tucked in the La Arcada Plaza between STATE Street and FIGUEROA Street.  We went for brunch, got to sit outside on a nicely overcast day (so, not too hot) and both enjoyed their Kali Club sandwich, although we got it fixed differently.  I don't eat bacon, so mine came without it.  My husband eats bacon, but he hates avocado, so his didn't have the avocado.  The sandwich also had arugula lettuce, tomatoes, and basil aioli all on toasted sourdough bread.  It was tasty, but it wasn't anything phenomenal.  We also ordered mac and cheese, which was made with fontina, provolone, and Parmesan cheeses, and cavatappi pasta with toasted breadcrumbs on the top.  That was very tasty and rich, but again, it wasn't a standout recipe, either.  I think if we ever return here, we'd get something different.  I'd give this 3.5 stars, but as we all know, they don't award by 1/2 stars on Yelp.

Do yourself a favor --DO order the fig jam and the House Benedict. The sweet and savory combination with the hollandaise sauce will set your taste buds on fire, wanting more, even after putting yourself into food coma, honestly. Also, the accompanying fruit and potatoes were fresh and delicious!! Would certainly come back and frequent this gem in La Arcada in my next Santa Barbara excursion!

Had to write a review before even leaving the restaurant because this place is DELICIOUS. Tucked back in such a beautiful alley courtyard that was quiet and actually socially distanced. Rave reviews on the burgers (my boyfriend called it one of the best burgers he has ever had) and excellent service! If you have not tried this place it is a must!!

I love that their place is pet friendly, but make sure your ready to wait about 45-1 hr. I ordered capresse salad and my husband get the eggs Benedict, the food was superbly delicious. We enjoy our brunch in their patio, stayed for about 2 hrs coz Im enjoying  my bottomless Mimosa. Took 1 star coz of the wait.

On the way from SLO to LA, we stopped in Santa Barbara to eat lunch here on a Sunday afternoon.  It was so fun to sit outside in their great alley location!  Service was great!  The food--I had the Buttermilk Fried Chicken/Jalapeno & Bacon "Country Gravy" and my wife had the Fig Burger.  Both were absolutely amazing!

My first time here but won't be my last! This place was really cool I stopped here for brunch and I never really been to any kind of brunch before lol but my girl insisted we do it..so they're 5 dollar mimosas were great the ratio of champagne to juice was perfect, the areas really nice I liked the old building feel even though we sat outside...I got the breakfast burrito with side salad n everything tasted bomb  asf.  One thing I also have noticed about food in SB is the portions are huge no matter where you go and this spot delivers on that too. I literally had a whole half of a burrito and my girl had half a burger. Over all i would definitely give it a easy 10/10

We had a wonderful experience at State and Fig and was so happy we chose this restaurant to have a birthday celebration! We came for BOTTOMLESS MIMOSAS on a Sunday and were able to find a table. You will need your whole party there to be seated. 

Our server Tracy was so absolutely attentive to our table, even when the restaurant was busy. She was always around to fill our waters, our mimosas and made sure we had everything we needed. The mimosas were great and did the trick to keep our party going. They are decently priced at $17 for the specialty flavored bottomless mimosas (mango, pomegranate). I ordered the short rib benedict and it was delicious. The prime rib was so tender and the pesto hollandaise was delectable. 

This is such a great spot as it's located in La Arcada and such cute decor inside. We chose to sit outside and it was like a movie with sunshine, food, mimosas, and laughter.

Definitely stop by if you love brunch!

SYOY,
Jess H.

Wow what a total bust, there are such high ratings but this place definitely fell below my expectations. We were on State St and my Husband was craving a burger. I found this place through Yelp and was excited to try it because of the high ratings. First off the service was horrible, the girl didn't even provide us refills on the drinks, she was actually headed out and was too busy counting her money than to pay attention to us. It was so hot too a refill on water would have been nice. I ordered the chicken panini with a side salad and he ordered their fig burger with fries. When the order came out, our sides were mismatched, he got my salad and I got his fries, how annoying is that. In addition, I specifically said no tomatoes on the salad and what did I get? Tomatoes!! The fries were awful too, very soggy and not fresh. The chicken panini was not that great, there was a big piece of mozarella cheese which I love however it wasn't melted, aren't panini's supposed to be hot and melted, that wasn't the case with mine. My husband hated his burger he barely ate half.  All in all we had a horrible dining experience and the service could have been better. I definitely wouldn't come back and wouldn't recommend it.

I've been here twice and liked it both times!

I got the BLTA sandwich, which was really good. Definitely hit the stop if you're craving a BLT. I also have had the Bello Benedict, which was pretty good. I've been meaning to go back and try their Fig Burger!

stopped for lunch on the way up the coast. was a little after two by the time we sat down and the dining area was about a third full. parked conveniently next door in the public parking structure.

I had the PBR -- STATE & FIG shorthand for PORK BELLY REUBEN (slow roasted pork belly, caraway kraut, gruyere, russian dressing on grilled rye). lots of flavors (juicy pig, nutty gruyere, tart and tangy kraut, sweet russian -- helps if you like caraway). tender, succulent pork belly was seared before going in the very, very rich sandwich. rye was nicely grilled (one of my pet peeves) and not nearly as beige as it looks in the photo.  

fries were crispy and fresh though a little stubby -- garlic and rosemary were nice additions but JULIANA and JODI managed to eat most of mine.

WYATT had the kid's BURGER with GARLIC FRIES. burger looked overcooked but he devoured every bite and pronounced it amazing so i'm going with that.

daughter and wife (JULIANA and JODI) split a TURKEY PANINI (turkey, avocado, basil aïoli, arugula and provolone) with a warm OLIVE ANTIPASTI (upgrade). sandwich was good. really liked the warm olives which were flavored with rosemary and citrus.

the kids had a DR WHO moment in the phone booth right outside the door.

The set up is kind of funky.

The entrance is hidden behind some outdoor tables. You walk in, it's a small place, the registers are "there". The employees were nice.

I ordered a Fig Burger to go. It was $12ish. It was on a super yummy bun, with a fig spead. The burger itself was tasty, (good quality ground beef).  The burger had blue cheese (a bit much for me), bacon (cooked well, crispy enough), the onions were good (but too many... messy). I chose a salad as my side (or fries). It came with a dill pickle spear (yay). 

It was very satisfactory. I was very happy with it. I'd definitely recommend this place.

The restaurant is located more in a corner location that is hidden away from the street. The decor is relatively modern, giving a nice feel when you sit down. Optionally, you can sit outside, where there is a nice open decor but lacking in shade. 


Now, on to the food: The food is what really
penalized itself causing it to earn only three stars. I really wanted to love the food, the colors and food was off to a good start. For starters, the soup was great. I had their clam chowder, the only wish I had would be for a thicker chowder, but not everybody shares the same opinion. The other soup that I sampled was a kale soup, which was a unique offering that many restaurants don't traditionally serve. Overall, the soup was off to a fantastic start and got me excited. 

However, things took a turn when I had their entrée. I had ordered their State Burger which has glazed onions and bacon. The taste wasn't awful, but the taste was definitely odd. But, the kicker that forced me to give it two stars was the plastic that I found in my burger! There was an entire piece of plastic that was stuck in the center of the party. That was a horrible turnoff for the restaurant. 

After informing the manager, their response was not the best. They offered no apology and quickly tried to run away with the dish. Unfortunately, I was in a hurry and had no time to wait for another one to arrive. But, their overall attitude regarding their mistake was summarily unapologetic. 

Overall, the restaurant may be a good one. But for me, their service and food caused me to give them a two star review. Maybe if I am in the area again, I can try again and see how they do. But for now, two stars is all it gets for it's food and service.

Went to State & Fig for brunch and bottomless mimosas. Let me start with how great the breakfast burrito is. I order breakfast burritos usually at every restaurant I go to and this one tops them all. I highly suggest the chorizo which was amazing. My girlfriend had a burger, which I tried, and was also unbelievable. Highly recommended! Will be back.

A group of 5 with a dog walks up to an empty restaurant for brunch. We tried making a reservation, but they do not take them. Waited for the host to come up to us, only to say there are "no available tables that can hold 5 of us outside". There were many tables outside open, one of which had 8 seats. Very unfortunate for them. We found a better restaurant not far, called Scarlett Begonia! Yum! Quality service!
Love the location, nestled in amongst several shops and other restaurants. Arugula salad with dates and pistachios was delicious.

The fig jam is so delicious with my portobello panini and side salad. The lunch special which was cheese burger with fig jam was so amazing and the portion was very large. Mimosas were $6 a cup and $17 for endless round. Also, the nice server just made everything perfect. He was so attentive and patient. It was a great time for brunch around 12pm. It was not to busy and there is nice outdoor seating.
Really yummy combinations. I liked the fig jam on my cheeseburger!

My boyfriend and I came here for our anniversary and we were just blown away at how amazing the food was. He got the steak with smoked bacon mac and cheese and grilled veggies...freaking amazing! I got the braised short ribs with roasted carrots, soft polenta, arugula, pecorino, and truffle essence....I ate the whole damn thing because of how delicious it was. Our server was so nice and attentive. This is just really good food and we will definitely be visiting this place again soon!
Amazing food. Super friendly staff and very helpful. Patrick who is the owner/chef takes great pride in serving amazing food. EVERYTHING was on point. Such a great way to spend Father's Day!

I've made a lot of terrible decisions in my life, but choosing State and Fig for my wedding reception totally cancels them all out.  And I made some BAD decisions.

From the very beginning, Patrick was a dream to work with.  He's kind and warm, he's also responsive and efficient and above all he knows how to cook, run a restaurant, and throw a great event!  He took care of everything, food-wise obviously, but also event-wise because he's thrown so many events at his restaurant and in his previous job.  

He was super patient with all our many changes.  Originally we were supposed to get married April 2020 but had to cancel due to COVID, then we had to keep canceling or next dates due to some personal tragedies (our first baby was stillborn in June 2020 then 2 weeks later my mom was diagnosed with terminal lung cancer, then 7 months after that our second baby was lost at 11 weeks, all this happened during the pandemic that decimated my husband's small business in the hospitality industry).  

Patrick was very accommodating of my brother, his wife, and their daughter who did not want to sit inside with the rest of us.  He was more than happy to set up a table on the patio and make them as comfortable as possible.  We ended up renting 4 heat lamps to keep them warm and it was super nice on the patio, they were not miserable at all and they didn't look like "pariahs" as they claimed they would.  It was a great setup out there, and Patrick even did the cocktail hour with passed appetizers out there so they felt more included.  It was perfect.

Not only was Patrick patient with all the switch-ups, but he was also incredibly warm and kind and empathetic about all our trauma and grief.  He worked extra hard to make sure we had the most perfect wedding possible because he felt we deserved one happy day.  And he pulled it off!  The food and ambience at our wedding reception was PERFECT.

It was hard to make our menu selections because all the options he sent us looked delicious!  He curated a menu based upon our many conversations and he really took the time to get to know our likes/dislikes and childhood memories.  All the options he created looked amazing so it was hard, but we finally narrowed it down to 3 tray passed appetizers (which people are STILL raving about, especially the salmon poke spoon and the battered halibut with tater tot and malt vinegar aioli).  

My husband is allergic to fish, but we still chose 2 fish appetizers because we felt our guests would really enjoy them.  I felt bad for my husband that he would only be able to eat one of them.  However, when we arrived at the restaurant (we missed cocktail hour because we were off taking photos), as soon as we sat down after our first dance, the server brought us each a little plate of the passed appetizers!  Mine contained 2 of each of the 3 passed apps and they were SO GOOD.  My husband's plate contained 2 of the vegetarian appetizer (it was a warm brie and mushroom crostini, to die for) and they even made him some special little sliders too!  Not only did they remember he can't eat fish but they went out of their way to make him something different that he could eat.

The salad and the entrees and even the dessert were impeccable.  They tasted delicious, were plated beautifully, and everything was served at the exact temperature it was supposed to be.  I will post a photo of the custom menus our florist (Brooke with Burlap and Bordeaux) printed so you can see how drool-worthy our menu selections were!  It was legitimately the best meal of my life, and I'm kind of a foodie and have pretty high standards when it comes to food.  I've had a lot of really good meals, but this one beat them all!

The service was wonderful too!  The staff were super attentive and professional, and they all really went above and beyond to give us a special day.  It was perfect.  We are so glad we chose State and Fig for our wedding reception and highly recommend it for anyone who wants to host a nice meal and really wow their guests.  We're still hearing compliments from our guests about the food and service and ambience of the restaurant!  It looked so beautiful too!  I will post some photos so everyone can see how gorgeous it was.

Came here for brunch with two of my friends. We didn't wait too long for a table and the seating was nice. The staff there were friendly and were patient with us. We didn't realize that they were trying to close up and waited for us to finish talking and having our drinks (probably about 30-45 mins after closing time). I got the kali Klub sandwich with a side salad and a pomegranate mango mimosa. Super delicious! I was full for the rest of the day.

Went for brunch.
Atmosphere - mad cute
Food - got an omelette that was probably ~6 total bites. Pretty damn small for $12. Highly doubt 3 eggs were used producing my omelette
Mimosas - $17 bottomless, solid. Dude was pouring 99% pagne / 1% juice just the way I like it.
5 stars for Atmosphere and dude pouring the mimosas. 
Pricing - meh, everything in downtown SB pricey. 
1 star for that weak omelette.   

3/5

Let me start off by saying that the customer service was extremely lacking the day we decided to eat here. As an advocate of great customer service and how that makes or breaks your dining experience, I was disappointed. Stopped by here on a Sunday, while we were driving back down to OC from Pismo Beach. Looked up on Yelp for a nice brunch like spot to eat and based off reviews, we decided to go with this place. What a mistake....

The food was lack luster for the price. Tried to order 2 mussels dishes to share among our party of 8 but was told that we couldn't because they had ran out and could only give us 1...it was in the middle of brunch time, so I couldn't understand how you could be running out; also seeing as how the restaurant was not crowded or anything. No worries, we worked with it and just got other dishes to try together. 

A party of 4 that was seated after us, got their food, finished their food and ours was still nowhere in sight. At this point we had been waiting close to an hr since placing the order. I was getting a serious case of the hangries. 

When the food finally came out, it wasn't anything close to amazing to my dismay. Not only that but, a friend had ordered the fish tacos and they skimped on the fish so much that he might as well had been eating a flour tortilla with coleslaw. The Brussels sprouts dish I got was not only miniature sized, it was drenched so much in Dijon mustard that I felt like I was just eating spoons of mustard.  

All the other reviews on this place have been decent so I'm wondering why my experience was so far off... I'm giving it 2 stars cause I'm willing to try it again (only cause my fellow yelpers like this place) and because though we only got 1 of the mussels dish, it was actually very delish.

We had such a great experience with this place. I got the house Benedict with bacon instead of ham and that was pretty good. My husband got the fig burger with goat cheese and wow the flavors were absolutely delightful. The service was good as well! Well worth the five stars.

Get there early for Saturday brunch and you'll have a fabulous time! 

A few gal pals and I flew into Santa Barbara airport and beelined it for State & Fig for some bonding and brekkie. It was a delightful way to get our vacay going, with bottomless mimosas and countless egg dishes. For $15 you can have the standard OJ mimosas, or for $19 you can get more exotic flavored juices like pomegranate. 

Even though it gets crowded, especially on the patio, our server never looked frazzled nor did he rush us out of our prime patio seat. That's so appreciated, kind sir.

With a slight buzz and a full belly, we departed State & Fig and traveled to Ojai. Not a bad way to start the day. Not bad at all!

Made a reservation here for my friend's birthday dinner since we were spending the weekend in town. Very cute spot with a very cute view outside too! Felt very holiday-like! :) 

Food:
- Warm brie: came with grilled grapes & bread - never had grilled grapes so it was interesting and I liked it. The bread was a little too burnt, but the warm brie definitely made everything better
- (Antipasti) Tomatoes, feta, olives, cucumber - very refreshing dish to start off with before our heavy entrees
- Brussel Sprouts (small plates): sea salt & garlic aioli? SOLD! Loved the crispiness of each leaf and the flavor wasn't very heavy so I liked its lightness
- Fritto Misto aka calamari: this was my least favorite - nothing special but it wasn't bad either
- Gnocchi: my entree was delicious! The butternut squash and kale in squash bisque?! I loved it so much! Will definitely order again!
- Papperdelle: my friend had this lamb bolognese dish - though I'm not a lamb fan - she killed her dish fast and really enjoyed it as well. I recommend for you lamb lovers!
- Pork Chop: grilled porkchop with brussels sprouts and mac & cheese! I will definitely order this dish if I return as well! The porkchop was melt-in-your-mouth juicy and soft! The sides that came with it also topped this dish off!
- Short ribs: anything with a hint of truffle wins my tastebuds! The short ribs were super soft and flavorful! Another must-order dish!
- Special: Seabass with gnocchi and pesto sauce! - super delish and definitely another item to try!

They came out with a complimentary dessert for my friend's birthday and sang with us as well. This place had such tasty dishes, I definitely want to return!

Great lunch menu, especially salads, if you can sit outside.  Inside, the environment is dull, and they need to bring bright colors and a good designer.  On the other hand, outside is lovely.  Therefore, wait for a table outside and you won't regret it.

While a little hard to find, it was delicious! Loved sitting outside! The short rib benedict was off the hook! so flavorful, im still thinking about it! I forgot my servers name, but they were very nice we will definitely be back

Excellent clam chowder. Very sophisticated and complex flavor base yet the delicate taste of the clams still shines through. Recommended. Panini was good as well, though the ham looked like it was processed (maybe it wasn't, but it had that grocery lunch meat look). Nevertheless it was good. Great service and nice atmosphere and location.

This review is for lunch.

On a nice day, State and Fig is quite an enjoyable place to eat - shady and pleasant patio seating in a shopping alleyway.  But there are only eight such tables, so it may be hard to get one.  The service was competent but a bit slow.

We had the chorizo omelet and turkey panini and both were well above average in both taste and size, but not truly exceptional.

Stage and Fig works well as a place to relax and enjoy the moment, and I would return if I ever happen to be walking that alleyway again.

I really wanted to love this place so am sad to give it only 3 stars. It was hard to find in the alley off of State Street, and the ordering was open tab concept - order at counter, seat yourself, pay at end of meal. My party of 2 ordered the Mediterranean salad with fried chicken and the French toast platter, with lemonade and guava mimosa. The mimosa was typically okay, and the salad had a little too much dressing mixed in for my liking. The fried chicken pieces were good and a lot of them throughout the salad. The French toast had a watery element to it but once you got over the texture they did taste good. Eggs were good and bacon was, too. So overall nothing to write home about. Other than the patio seating is quite lovely.

My wife and I hosted our rehearsal dinner with Patrick at State & Fig and he was an absolute pleasure to work with! As SB locals we've eaten here many times and always enjoyed the food and service. Our private event was no different and all our guests raved about the food. Through multiple delays and schedule changes due to COVID, Patrick was always accommodating and helped us put together a special evening that we will always remember. At the event, all his staff were friendly and on top of everything. Thank you Patrick and the whole State & Fig team!

Brunch here is so cute and so yummy. They also offer bottomless mimosas!! $15 (also have pomegranate for an extra charge). 

My friend ordered the fried chicken and biscuits which were delicious. It wasn't as doused in the white sauce as I've seen in other places and the chicken didn't taste so greasy as I've had before as well. The biscuit is delicious, too. I ordered the pork belly hash with poached eggs, butternut squash, potatoes, fruit, and rye bread (came with jam, butter, and ketchup). Everything was so good and fairly well priced for a brunch place on State.

Another thing I like about this cafe is how it's not directly on state street, it's in La Arcada and sort of in this alleyway away from the business of the street. Thus, I feel like this offers a quaint, intimate, and peaceful brunch experience yet it's very inviting and something I definitely want to bring my girlfriends to for bottomless mimosas!

Indoor and outdoor seating is both cute. We chose to sit outdoors because the weather was so nice. My only complaint was our waitress... She was very pushy into having us get alcoholic drinks and doing bottomless mimosas. And after we decided to order one drink (my friend the pomegranate mimosa and the blueberry mojito for me), she kept trying to convince us to order another. I doubt the other people who work there are like her, she said she hadn't been working there for more than 6 weeks and it seemed like everyone else was very friendly. The blueberry mojito was extremely sweet in my opinion, wouldn't order it again. Combining the sweetness of the blueberry mojito with the sweet jam and the fattening pork belly was too much for me. I regret ordering the drink; would have rather ordered the dish with a coffee instead. 

I'm very looking forward to trying everything else on the menu, the burger looked delicious and so did all the other items on their brunch special!
Amazing food. Super friendly staff and very helpful. Patrick who is the owner/chef takes great pride in serving amazing food. EVERYTHING was on point. Such a great way to spend Father's Day!

I read about this place in Los Angeles magazine so I decided to try it.

We headed to SB on a Saturday and stopped here first.

There were 3 other patrons at State & Fig.

We ordered the Fig Burger and split it. We asked for it medium rare and it was brought out medium. We ran out of water and waited and waited and finally asked for some.

We were pretty unimpressed. When your restaurant is filled with people, then there is room for error, but when the number of waiters is equal the number of patrons, there is no excuse for my water glass to not be filled once it reaches half way, nor for our burger to come out wrong. 

The ambience is nice and the inside is just as charming as the outside, but it wasn't worth the $14 we paid. I would have happily tried some where else.

If I could give this POOR excuse of a restaurant a negative 5 star review, I would.

The service is horrible, the wait staff is inattentive and rude and the owner is repulsive.
After waiting  for 45 minutes for our order to arrive, during which none of the wait staff bothered to check in with us, I told the other waitress that I was leaving because of the long wait and the poor service. Who waits for their food for 45 minutes?

Not only did she stare at me with a deer in the headlights look on her face, she didn't even bother to apologize or at the very least offer an explanation for the long wait. Instead, she asked if I wanted one of the orders to go. Why in the world would I want to do that???!! 
I should have trusted my instincts and skipped this place the moment I saw the entire restaurant empty. Only one other table was occupied there, yet they managed to take their sweet time to prepare my burger. Really? I thought they went fishing to fetch some salmon from my friend's dish.

I don't see this place lasting very long. They even had the nerve to charge me for my can of Sprite. To top it off, they held my shopping bag hostage(which I left behind because I was so upset) until I paid for the drink. I refused and the owner told me never to come  back to his restaurant again. GLADLY !!!!  I will not only avoid going to his restaurant, but I will tell EVERYONE I know not to go specifically to that restaurant. Its a shame to even call it a restaurant. Its a dump.

In this economy you are refusing customers? Good luck Chuck. That is not the way you treat customers. I have never been so insulted in my life and have never had such a negative experience at a restaurant, ever.

I will never step foot in this establishment again. I waited an hour and a half for this stupid, mediocre, disgusting excuse of a restaurant to open because of the positive  Yelp reviews.
Avoid this place unless you don't mind being insulted and served substandard, overpriced food by horrendous wait staff and an unappreciative, ungrateful piece of trash owner. 

Sidenote: I happily took my business elsewhere ( Los Agaves) and I was extremely satisfied with their amazing food and service.
Fig and State, State and Fig..  or whatever their name is..   sucks. Worst experience Ever. 
DO NOT EAT HERE !!! Spend your hard earned dollars at an establishment that appreciates your business.

Shame on you.

Best brunch spot in SB!!! The fried chicken sandwich is always my go to. The staff is always so friendly and helpful and the owner puts so much passion into his food. Definitely one of my favorite restaurants here.

This is a very cute restaurant located in La Arcada. I found it thanks to yelp and had a delicious portabelo pesto panini that came with a salad $9.50 and a great cappuccino with almond milk! Everything was really flavorful and not greasy. Tracy was very friendly and got my food out quickly. A very neat little area to walk around and see all the shops before or after.

Sometimes I like the food, sometimes I like the service. The problem for me is the inconsistency, hence the middle of the road, 3 star rating. The Tuscan Sausage & Kale Soup is tasty. I prefer it when I am dining in as I ordered a bowl to go once when I was under the weather and the portion was smaller than a cup of soup. I also enjoy their hash on the brunch special menu. They could improve their breakfast menu by offering some a la carte options such as biscuits & jam, a side of bacon, etc. for foodies like me who love to add on to my entree (and increase the restaurants revenue). Once, I tried to order a biscuit in addition to my entree and the waitress told me that Chef said he only makes enough biscuits for the chicken and biscuits entree. It seemed silly to me to order two entrees just to be able to have a biscuit with my meal, so I chose not to order anything and went to Jeanine's next door for my breakfast after my husband finished his meal at State & Fig. Little things like that make the world of difference in how often a customer repeats business at a restaurant. They could have easily increased their sales by three times what we spent by having a few more accommodations on the menu. There is a lovely dog friendly patio in front of the restaurant. Depending on which server you have they will actually bring them a bowl of water too, which is a nice touch when it is offered. This establishment has lots of potential and the food is generally good, however, service is a large component of the dining experience and can bring down the rating when it is not up to par with common industry standards. If you're a tourist, it's worth checking out because it is tucked away in a cute courtyard in the La Arcada plaza and has a nice ambiance outside as do the several neighboring restaurants.

I was craving a eggs Benedict so I searched and it brought me to State & Fig. My girlfriend ordered a burger and we both shared each. The service was top notch! Everyone in the entire place did such a great job that I felt very welcomed and comfortable. 

The food used good ingredients and tasted fresh. They gave us the wrong burger though because it came with bacon and we ordered a basic one. Interesting combo to use a sweet fig sauce on the burger which wasn't the one we ordered. I doubt they make mistakes like this often though because they really do seem to care.

I am glad I came here and am also glad they stayed open until 3pm. For whatever reason so many similar restaurants in that area closed at 2pm.

Had lunch here with three teenagers. The place is located is a quaint little plaza and there were beautiful sculptures and fountains nearby. The wait was 45 minutes, which we didn't mind because of the good Yelp reviews.  We waited a little longer because we wanted to eat inside. This was a waste of time because they had the doors open the whole time so it was just as hot inside as it was outside. There was also at least one fly buzzing around.  By noon they had already run out of a couple of the brunch special items.  They don't have busboys so the wait was longer that it had to be.  The menu is limited and the "gluten free" option is basically a salad, no GF buns or sandwich bread.  I asked for medium rare burger and got a rare burger with some char outside. When I asked for it to be cooked more, they basically just threw it back on the grill so my cheese and avocado got extra melted (yuk).  The kids enjoyed their burgers, which were on nice brioche buns, and they loved the aoli that came with it.  Thsts the only reason they are getting a 3.  The fries were mediocre as was the service. 

Overall, I don't recommend it, at least not for lunch and not in a hot day.

So. Fucking. Good. I got the short rib eggs Benedict and it was one of the best things I've ever had. My partner got a breakfast sandwich and said it was the best brunch he's ever had. The place was very cute and the staff was all very nice and helpful. Would totally come back!

Nothing very special. It was very bland and the shrimp was battered and fried for my wife's taco and it was not mentioned. The corn tortilla tasted like flour. Nothing really special I would recommend other places in Santa Barbara.
One of the greatest Benedicts I've ever had! If their seasonal menu offers a short rib Benedict, don't hesitate to order it.
Waited 20 minutes to be attended at my table and 15 minutes more for a cup of coffee. Poor service spoiled the food.

I placed an order over the phone. 
The "manager" took my order then immediately said "just a sec"
I waited a sec, actually several secs as that sec turned into 28 minutes and you my friend may be wondering why I would wait. 
The staff is usually with me 100% but on this day my order was taken and I was told to wait. 
When I arrived the manager was doing nothing absolutely nothing and I said I'm here to pick up my order 
She said there's no order for you
Odd very odd because you took it 27 minutes ago
She said I'm sorry I got busy doing something else there was a large I was helping seat and that took precedent over your mobile order and we typically don't take mobile orders 
Also odd as I order from her most weekends
I reordered and waited you might ask why, well because the food unlike the service is amazing 
I can't get mad at the chef it's not his fault his front of house staff is so unprofessional and careless!

I think this restaurant has AMAZING food. The lemon ricotta pancakes are TO DIE FOR, but every single time I've been, the service has been horrible. I understand slower service when a restaurant is busy, I work in a restaurant as well, but on one of my visits to Santa Barbara my table of 3 were the only customers in the restaurants and we were all but ignored the entire time. I've given the restaurant a few times because I visit Santa Barbara often, but I've seen no improvement in their service. Bummer... great potential.

Went for Sunday breakfast at 10 a.m. WE thought we'd beat the crowd and were immediately seated and had an excellent meal. The Hash with eggs is the best hash I've ever had. While we were there parties of 8, 10 and 6 came in right in a row and I was so impressed by the service they received. Highly recommend going here!

My boyfriend and I have been here a few times and it's always a great experience! COVID is tough on businesses these days and changes aren't always the best. We were skeptical paying at the counter since service typically suffers that way, but not here. Our server Riley was so hospitable and anticipated our needs before we could even ask. We had a few mimosas and had ZERO trouble getting another round thanks to Riley's impeccable service. He made the end of our trip a pleasant one! 

Onto the food: my boyfriend ordered the Presidio Burrito (he's tried it twice) which was delicious. It was generously filled with chorizo, home fries, cheddar and jack cheese, avocado, and salsa. It's paired with a side salad that's pretty tasty as well. For myself, I tried the Salmon Benny that was paired with a side of home fries. The entree was good, but the burritos here are definitely better. 

Drinks: this establishment has pretty good coffee whatever brand they use. Flavored creamer isn't necessary. We also had a few rounds of mimosas which are pretty darn good for $6 apiece. They have a variety of flavors to choose from too - peach, guava, pomegranate, pineapple and mango (my favorite). 

If you're in SB, definitely give this place a try. Your tummy will thank you.

If I could give 0 stars I would. We approached an EMPTY restaurant with ample outdoor seating, and were rudely told by the host that she could not accommodate our party of 5. She stated "I do not have any tables together that can fit that amount." Meanwhile we are staring at several tables that would fit our party. I was previously told they do not take reservations, so I am confused why we were denied service. Very unprofessional. Will NOT be returning.
Very average service. Annoyingly slow. Waiters seem confused about wats available on the menu.

Came here on a date for brunch with my boyfriend. What a lovely morning. We got bottomless mimosas for $18. I ordered a cup of clam chowder which came quickly and was very good. This was followed by a Caprese Salad and my boyfriend ordered a chicken Panini. We both very much enjoyed our plates and I just might have enjoyed my mimosas too much. The $18 option came with choice of Original, Mango or Pomegranate mimosas. Have to try one of each but be warned, they're STRONG.

Ps:They have a patio area where they allow dogs.

Food was delicious, enjoyed their tasty fish tacos while my lady enjoyed the turkey panini. Both of us enjoyed very much! Staff was very friendly, outdoor patio was lovely. We were seated just before a rush, got lucky and didn't have to wait very long at all! Even if there is a wait, it's worth it! Will be back! Thank you Yelp for the recommendation! 5 stars.

Located near State Street, this cute little place was perfect for Sunday brunch. They offer outdoor dining, but that seemed to full up quickly for larger parties so my party of 5 was offered indoor dining. Seating inside was socially distanced.

Short Benedict: They do not skimp at all on the short ribs. I only finished one of my benedicts because it was just that much.  Eggs were poached well. The home fries could have been a bit more crispy and slightly seasoned for an elevated taste. Again, the amount was more than enough. This also comes with some fresh assorted fruit too.

A variety of mimosas are also offered and available by the glass.

Upon entering the restaurant, we were immediately sat and our drink order was taken. We ordered two iced teas, two Short Rib Bennys, and a side of fries. The Benedict came with 2 english muffins, arugula, poached eggs, and their pesto hollandaise. This was so delicious!! The service was excellent and the food is outstanding. We will be coming back here for sure!

The service here was GREAT! the bus boy was super friendly and very attentive. You go inside to order and then they give you a number. It's odd that you don't pay until after you're done eating. They have a big selection of mimosas. 
The food was okay. I would give the food like a 3 maybe. I actually didn't feel good right after brunch. 
The place was cute but I don't think i would be back, not because it was terrible but because there's so many other restaurants.

We went here for Sunday brunch and I just want to say that the braised short rib benedict is absolutely delicious! We also got the Mac n cheese & the pork belly Benedict but they did not compare to the short rib one. The service was a bit off but nothing too bad! 100% would go here for brunch (next time with their bottomless mimosas)

We were driving back through after visiting Solvang and needed a place for a late lunch.  We also needed a place that would do decent take away.  So, we chose this location based off previous reviews.

There were 4 of us in our group and we were all starving.  Server was helpful when taking our order and gave us a pick up time.  We chose a burger and fries, chicken sandwich, and a huge main course salad (we also chose sodas and sparkling waters to go.)

While we waited we were able to walk around the area and take in a few local sights and do some people watching.

Picked up the food from another fabulous sever when promised and headed over to a nearby park to eat.  Everything was packaged up so neatly, even the drinks!  

Burger was fantastic - one of my all time favorites with the fig and cheese combo.  All our choices really were very good and were easy to eat and enjoy on the go.  We didn't even miss the table service that we normally would have enjoyed.

We really wanted to like this place, but it fell sorta flat.  While the server was very nice, the food not so much.  For the price, the chicken panini was small and basic.  Flavor was something I could have made at home.  Same for the salad.  It was a very small portion of salad greens.  I also ordered the Sausage Kale soup.  It smelled great, but since we eat with our eyes first, I could not get past the layer of thick floating grease/oil on the top. I could not eat it.  That layer of fat needs to be removed.  I understand fat is flavor, but this was too much.

After walking along stare for an hour we came across State & Fig. Tucked away in a Cute alley way it's hard to find this hidden gem. But so worth it once you do. I wish they had a sign pointing to the restaurant. But maybe that's why it was so easy to get a table! This was such a delicious meal we had. The food was fast and delicious! 

Parking: we parking at the mall and we're walking all around, but from what it seemed there wasn't a parking lot or anything?

Service: amazing service! Friendly service and amazing recommendations. The waiter was constantly refilling our water and checking to see how we liked the food.

Pricing: Considering you are in Santa Barbra it's was very decently priced. 
- 1 mimosa 
- 1 burger & salad 
- 1 chorizo omelet and fruit 
- 1 cup of chowder 
= $51.00 
Not bad for AMAZING / healthy(ish) food 

Trend level: girls ... come cute because you're going to want to be having your significant other take allllll the pics of you at this cute aesthetically desirable restaurant!

An eggs Benedict is my go-to brunch item to order, and this restaurant did not disappoint! The ham was crispy on the edges, the egg was perfectly poached, and the Hollandaise sauce was to die for. The side of potatoes were well seasoned too, and the side of fruit was a refreshing finale to my meal. 

My partner got the BBQ burger and he said it was one of the better burgers he's had. It was mountainous in size and came with deliciously seasoned fries. 

The iced vanilla latte was just alright--nothing extraordinary. The coffee tasted a bit watery for my liking. 

The employees inside the store serving us and making food/drinks were not wearing masks even though there's still a mandate in SB County. Something to keep in mind when you're stopping by, especially if you are covid conscious!

Our last night in Santa Barbara, we were looking for a nice dinner in SB and we used Yelp to help us find a place.  Boy, were we disappointed in this place.  Upon arrival, the hostess said it would be about 10-15 minutes.  When we went back 15 minutes later, she said it would probably be another 10-15 minutes.  My instincts should have told me to get  out of there, but we waited.  I wish we had left and gone to another restaurant.

We placed our orders but the waitress didn't even tell us the specials.  We overhead the waiter next to us tell the table seated next to us. Our waitress seemed to lack any personality.  Our waitress at one point said our food would be out soon.  20 minutes later it arrived. It was such a long wait for food.  And then we had ordered rosemary fries but we got regular ones. When we brought it to her attention, she didn't apologize just said she would talk to the kitchen.  When the "rosemary" fries came out we were disappointed.  They barely tasted like rosemary.  

I had the chicken which was quite good, but with the spotty service, it just wasn't enjoyable. 

Another thing I didn't like about this restaurant were the dirty floors in the back of the restaurant near the restrooms.  Near the women's restroom, there was a door open with a bag of either trash or linens.  Patrons shouldn't see that.  The floors should be washed more frequently.

Interesting place with potential. 

You wait in a line and look at the menu, a host will tell you when to walk inside to order and then you sit with a number. But they waited to bring our drinks out until the food came which I just found strange. I wouldn't have minded carrying them back to the table if it would have helped speed it up. 

I had the house Benny which was cold. The fig burger with garlic fries were great. Just mainly the service was what kinda killed it for us. 

Everyone seems a little confused, even dropping the food was somewhat painful to watch lol. It just seems like no one really knew what was going on the entire experience. I would see servers come out with two plates and then look confused as if they forgot where they were going and went back inside. Just a really weird experience

The doughnuts are pretty good. Nice consistancy but I'm not so much for fancy doughnuts but after Ellers this is the only other doughnut I will eat in SB. I think if they had hot hole to taste would bring more customers to try this place out.
An amazing place to go, there donuts are so fresh soft, and the perfect texture, best donuts in town. And the staff is so friendly & inviting i Highly recommend!!

Small selection of donuts that look amazing on their website and on social media! Very simplistic donut with a wonderful hint of delicious dough underneath the layer of brown sugar and Carmel! Great place and festive environment! Definetly will go again!! Follow their instagram page if you want delicious mouth watering donut photos!
No question this place is decadently yummy. Healthy is questionable, but yummy is not. Like all guilty pleasures, I love and hate it. And will probably be back :)

Wow... fancy donuts for the WIN! I have never had a fancy donut before and my office started buying these donuts for special meetings and I hope we have more special meetings in the near future. The Mexican hot chocolate is my current favorite but the hibiscus is also up there. Delicious treats for a little extra magic in your breakfast eats.

I don't normally help but I thought this place really deserved a good one. Visited Santa Barbara with a friend for a few days and stumbled upon this place looking up good restaurants on Yelp. Was not disappointed. Craft donuts made fresh daily with flavors changing seasonally. No preservatives. Tried the burnt honey & rosemary, brown butter and samoa the first day, they were so good we went back a second day to try the blueberry crisp and strawberry habanero. All of them were soooo delicious, no joke. The blueberry was probably my favorite though. If you're ever in the area do yourself a favor and go here. Get anything, you won't be disappointed.

When visiting Santa Barbara for only 2 days, you have to be selective about where to go and eat.  Hook and Press was worthy and delivered unique donuts that we cannot find at home.  Usually donuts don't get me very excited bc they satisfy just one taste: sweet.  Though these circular treats were sweet, each had another elementthat balanced out the sweet - lemon or butter or coconut.  Yum.  Our favorite was the browned butter.

I think this place is overrated. Based on numerous reviews and recommendations we went here. Donut was a bit better than average but it was quite expensive. I definitely had way better donuts in my life and the money wasn't worth it. I agree with some other comments the texture was very dense which didn't make it feel like a fresh donut.
Cool donuts. I recommend trying them all but I loved the Mexican one because it had a little kick to it.

Yo! On my quest for the perfect donut across the US has just been challenged by this place right here. I have been doing this for about 10 years now and this place is now one of my favorites and have visited twice on our trip, good grief point me to gym right, nah F it, I'M ON VACATION! .
.
What seals it was the approval of E who doesn't prefer a donut and she was all excited like me. As you all know it is hard for a trained palate(the baker she is) to like certain things, but she loves them like me.
.
What makes it so good? A donut is a donut right? Oh on the contrary. The donut has to be light, the dough just right with the touch of sweetness. Not greasy as most places leave the donuts in the oil too long. Then you have the flavors and toppings. The combination this guy Banker turned Baker does it just right. The true test is if you can make a simple glazed right, then the rest will follow. Here his base was a browned butter glazed donut and OMG! 
.
Done! Enough said! Carry on with your day!
.
If you are ever in Santa Barbara and you're a Donut Freak(and I wear that label proudly) please give this place a try. Incredible. Look em up on Yelp peeps!
Wow! Surely the best donut of my life. Visiting SB and saw this place. Who thought of all these flavors?  And a well made cappuccino made my morning.
The pecan pie donut tasted like the real thing! Also ordered an oat milk matcha latte which didn't disappoint. Try and come early because they have a small selection of doughnuts.
Amazing best donuts...love that we got this in SB. Love that its seasonal. Check out The brown Butter donut and the Lemon Curd.
Best donut I've ever had!.. I had the POG (Passionfruit, Orange, and Guava). Reminded me of being in Hawaii. Unfortunately they will stop making it tomorrow but I am ready to try others.

I went again to get a box to bring to a party, we all shared one bite of all of the flavors because I didn't want myself to eat all of them. People at the party were like "Oh my god" with a full mouth of donut. Super flavorful, super fluffy and just perfect. Don't know what you guys are doin but we love it!

Came here to kick off a day in SB and the donuts were delicious! We got a cinnamon horchata and a double chocolate and split both.  Both donuts were soft and super flavorful with great toppings.  Definitely will be back the next time I am in the area!

So many fun and creative flavors and all of the donuts are beautiful! They said they should be getting some gluten free options too as well! Pumpkin cheesecake, apple crisp, and the P.O.G were big hits among the group I went with! Love this cute new spot.
Tucked into a small shared space with some other vendors, this place is easy to miss. But so glad we stumbled across it. I had the nutella filled donut and the horchata one. Both were amazing.
Got one of each, couldn't decide my favorite. All delicious! Support great local businesses like this one!

I am a huge donut fan, so when I found out an artisanal donut place is opening in town I was so excited. However, after trying hook and press twice I have to say I am not impressed.
