Today we went again and 10 minutes into the hour we paid for my daughter was scratched and her hand was bleeding. The woman there offered a wipe and bandage but no apology or concern whatsoever. The claw went far into her hand and she had nerve pain and numbness in her fingers. Went went to leave right then and the gal just said "thank you so much for coming in!"Meanwhile another guest had simultaneously gotten bitten and was also bleeding and asking for first aid. 

I think this is a near business and I know we signed a waiver etc etc, but the owner probably needs to screen cats a little better especially if they are letting young kids in. The thing that will take them down is an injury that isn't so minor and if this is how they run things, it's only s matter of time.

I love what Cat Therapy is doing! I'm a cat person for sure, but seeing how much fun these cats have and knowing how many adoptions have happened thanks to this business warms my heart. Make a reservation online, it's the best way to secure your spot. My husband and I had a super fun afternoon and feeding these cats and giving them love.
Just a few skinny cats and coffee from a tiny little coffee machine--yeah it's indeed a cat "cafe"!

Such an amazing place... get to meet and feed adorable cats, each with a different personality. If you connect you can adopt! Owners are very friendly & love their work & cats you can tell by talking to them. I already told two cat friends in town to visit. Really the coolest new spot in SB if you love furry fluffy felines, unique concept that will make you feel fulfilled after meeting these adorable kitties. Meow!

I don't usually leave reviews but I feel like I need to for this place. I really enjoyed my time and the employees were great but I have a concern about the cats. The majority of the cats seem to be sick. Their heads felt feverish, they were all sneezing, and they had watery eyes. There were a lot of cats in a small area so it makes sense if one gets sick they all will, but I am worried they are not getting proper veterinary care. In addition a lot of the cats were itching like they had fleas and I just hope they are getting flea medication. The cats were all very sweet and I hope the colds were just a one time occurrence and this is not an ongoing problem.

The place was super clean which is great if your sensitive to cats or have allergies to cats. The cats are so friendly and mellow. They looked healthy and well taken care of. I got to love on all of them and didn't feel like any missed out on love. The place was so cozy and comfy. It was like a chic cafe with cats and yummy drinks to order. The people there love the cats and made sure the cats are being well taken care of which made me relax. I was just able to enjoy myself.
Purrrrrfect place.Went there couple times and both times it made my day. Also it really warms my heart that they have cats from shelters

Oh my goodness! We had a private event here yesterday for my eight-year-old daughter's birthday party. What a blast! The kids were in heaven, and I think the adults might have even had more fun than the kids! There were so many cats of all ages with different personalities (playful, mellow, etc.). There was a cat for everyone (cuddly cats, silly cats, etc.). We will definitely be back!

Definitely an amazing place to relax and pay it forward. 

Just read the photo attached to learn More

So nicely decorated and very intimate setting to get the perfect interactions with each cat!! Would definitely love to go back, only complaint was that I wish there were thousands of cats there... I'm not even a cat person and I had a great time

My husband and I just visited for the first time. Overall, it was nice and we were impressed with the cleanliness of the space. We were interested in adopting but didn't get a chance to meet many of the cats - they were either sleeping or just not out in the main room. We plan on coming back for another try. One recommendation I would make is to find out ahead of time if people are there looking to adopt versus just getting some cat time. There was a group of people there who basically took over the kittens so nobody else could meet them. If someone was interested in adopting, they should have priority when meeting the cats and kittens.

You can rest assured that if there is a cat cafe in any city I visit, I will find it. And from the several that I have visited, I can say that this place has the friendliest, most sociable cats in their shop. We went when they opened at 11am and So many of them were active! Several were napping the entire time, but the ones that were awake were all so curious about all their visitors, and would run around sniffing everything and climb into your lap to demand pets. They actively played with all the toys and some of the newer ones that were initially keep in a cage kept escaping to come out to play that the staff had to just give in and let them roam around as they please. They also have free coffee and tea here, and
I also saw someone buy lunch to bring here to eat and I guess that was allowed too? Overall it's a very relaxed atmosphere here and the cats' personalities make it super fun and cheerful. It was much more of a "let's all play together" vibe versus a "aww how cute all the kitties are" that most other cat cafes have. It made it so all the humans visiting the cafe were a lot more friendlier with each other too, which was nice. I really enjoyed my visit!

What a great time I just had at Cat Therapy!  Watching adorable kittens romp & wrestle & play,  jump on your lap for a snuggle & play with the feather wand you dangle. Giving the order cats a pet & chin scratch & love they've been missing.  The hour flew by and I gave not one thought to troubles, responsibilities, politics, aches, or anything negative.  Just pure joy.  The facility was clean, pleasant and perfectly suited to cat interaction but also allows cats to have privacy if they choose. These are lucky kitties and we're lucky to have this place. If you're thinking of adopting it's perfect to get to know the individual personalities of the cats.  And if you're not planning to adopt, it's a great way to escape the world & enjoy these wonderful creatures.

One of the most relaxed "cat Cafe"places I have been to. I was able to check in on Yelp and get 20% off of the entrance fee. I'm from Austin, TX, and have two cats waiting for me back at home. It was nice to visit this place and hang out with some of the most friendliest and cutest kitties I have seen. I drank some coffee and stayed for about an hour before heading back to my hotel room. I recommend this Cafe to anyone who needs to escape from the humans for an hour or so :)

Such a great place to visit for "therapy"! However, I highly suggest adopting. You can play with many kittens and cats to find your best match. These are the friendliest and healthiest kittens and cats around! My family adopted two!

A room full of kitty cats who need a furrever home. The small admission price keeps the place open. It's nice these at risk kittens and cats have a chance to win your heart, and it's nice to play with cats when away from home.

This place is amazing! We walked past and knew we had to go in! We were last minute able to book an hour and ended up having the whole hour to ourselves! All the cats were so sweet, and I wish I could adopt them all! We would definitely go back again and have already recommended Cat Therapy to so many people!

Such an awesome morning!! So glad to have had a full hour with these little fur babies!! Seriously, this made my morning! I can see why it's called Cat Therapy! I have a smile on my face from ear to ear!! Such playful little energetic and also sleepy babies.

Cat yoga is an excellent way to spend a Sunday morning! The class was relaxing and light-hearted, with adorable kitties doing their kitty things all aliens the room. Our instructor was great and guided us through a nice hour-long practice with a few catlike poses :)
Afterwards we were allowed to play with the cats for about 30 minutes.
Very kind staff, very easy check-in process. The cats are adorable and fun to play with. You will pay $10 for an hour. It will fly by because of how much fun you're having with the felines.

i love this place so much. Fair price because even though it's "only an hour" they don't mind how long you're there if there's no reservations coming up. Free therapy and the cutest merchandise! You can tell the workers definitely care so much about the little cuties here, and they even give you some free stickers at the end. Always gonna come back here for some real good kitty playtime and snuggles! Thanks cat therapy!!

Cat Therapy is one of the happiest places for me to visit. I am so impressed by how many cat adoptions they have had and how comfortable the kitties are in the space. It is such a great place to go on for a date or just to destress. I highly recommend checking out Cat Therapy if you're in the area!

Awesome way to spend an hour. I absolutely adored this place and it was great to feel like you are helping out while enjoying yourself around the cats. It's only 20.00 and is so worthwhile. If you are in town come help the cause and meet some cuties.

I've been here for cat yoga and had a wonderful time. We also recently adopted two beautiful babies and are so in love. It's obvious that the people at Cat Therapy love and care for the animals very much. Highly recommend for playtime with cats or for adopters

This was my first cat cafe visit and I will be back for more soon! I had such a fun and unique experience here! I loved being able to play and cuddle the cats here. There was even kittens here when we came which was amazing! All of the cats were different ages and breeds. Some of them were more friendly then others and but they were all so cute!
They even have food to feed the cats here, so make sure you ask for it!

They have free coffee and tea for you to enjoy while you are playing with the cats. They even have wine nights here where you can enjoy a glass of wine while playing with the cats. 

I enjoyed this place very much and love that they rescue animals that are in desperate need of help. They adopt so many cats out of this place it's incredible and amazing! I can't wait to come back here the next time I need some therapy.

This place is amazing. I went here on a date with my girlfriend a few months back. 

I would have never considered adopting a cat until I came here. I held this cat and fell in love with it. So I obviously adopted it which has been great. I strongly support their cause and their methods clearly work as a non cat person (Me), now has a cat.... Now I love cats so nice work!

My first cat cafe visit! Highly recommended. $12/hour. Free tea and coffee. A dozen cats of different ages and breeds. Ask for food to give them and the cats to nuts. The kittens are adorable. Definitely a unique experience to take your friends or family to. Would return for sure.

This place is incredible.  The place is crawling with adorable , well mannered and friendly kitties waiting to be adopted! Catalina the owner is super sweet and makes sure you are comfortable and have everything you need during your session.  You can order coffee , smoothies , and other delicious snacks from brazil arts cafe while you are there and they will bring it to you during your session.  If you are looking to adopt a cat , be prepared to be swooning over these kitties.  If not , be prepared to have fun! They even give you some cat nip treats so that the cats will come up to you more often :)

For the session I went to, The room was occupied with 12-15 people with 4 or 5 cats on the floor. As a cat owner I can tell some cats were exhausted and just tried to hide somewhere. It's good that you can adopt the cat from this place, but you can also visit animal shelter for free, and they have more cats available.

It was so relaxing to just chill around with cats for an hour. The price is $12 for an hour it's totally worth it for just hanging out with cats. The location isn't very secretive but isn't very busy. I got a-little lost trying to find it but eventually did. There are various different types of cats to play with all which are adoptable. They provide you with toys, seating, and food to feed them. I personally fell in love with a little orange kitten who fell asleep in my lap it was the cutest I was so sad to leave him
Come here. Pet kitties and adopt one or two. It's good therapy for you and it's good for the cats too

This place is more of an indoor cat petting zoo than a cat cafe. When I think of a cat cafe, I think of more chairs & tables with food & drinks being served & cats lounging around & walking about. But the focus here is the cats, which is fine. My husband & I were fine with paying for the entrance fee to support the cats. Fortunately, I found this place through Yelp, so we got 20% off the entrance fee, which came out to $8 per person. The entrance fee includes coffee, tea or wine, which is placed at a self-serve station in the front door area. There were a few some stools & tables in the room. Guests can place their belongings away from the cats in the side cubicles. There were over 10 cats here to interact with. Many of them were sleeping on the big pillows on the floor when we arrived. One orange cat was particularly hissy & scratched my husband when we visited. It wasn't too bad of a scratch though. The lady who greeted us at the door was polite & cordial. The cats here are available for adoption through the Stray Cat Alliance. I think more pet rescue groups should consider trying this model out to raise money for their pet adoption efforts.

I took a friend here from out of town. We made a reservation but the amount of people who were in the play area with the cats seemed excessive.I like the concept and enjoyed the few cats that I got to interact with. I was concerned about how rough the smaller children were handling the cats. I'm not sure if I will go back or not.

I'm a big cat person and can make friends with any cat. I've even tamed a few ferrel cats and got homes for them. I found this place by accident and was excited to come in and play with the kitties. I used the Yelp check in, signed the waiver and entered. All the cats were so loving even the spunky ones with purple collars. I even got a head butt from one of them. A cat person knows what a head butt from a cat is. I could only stay a short time since I had a train to catch. I wanted to stay all day. If I was a local I'd offer to volunteer time. The cats with purple collars wouldn't have them for long.  This is such a fun place to bring your kids and hopefully adopt a kitty. I hope this place stays around for a long time since they rescue cats from high kill shelters and find them homes.
The kitties are well take care of. Volunteers know a lot about them. They're so cute and some are adorably sassy.
I love this place! The cats are so well taken care of and I was really impressed by the staff. I wish I could give it more stars. Go here if you like cats or knead;) to destress.

(visited before covid19 situation)
I've visited a few cat cafes before, in Manhattan and other countries like Thailand and South Korea, but this cafe is the only one that allows visitors to wear their shoes in to the main area where we are allowed to mingle with the cats. There was also no requirements for us to wash our hands prior. Now that with the covid19 situation, they did do the necessary to increase safety for visitors, which therefore is better for the cats as well. However they should have better cleanliness standards for the safety and wellbeing of the cats right from the start.

The employee was so knowledgeable and friendly and helpful. He was attentive and kind. It was a great experience dealing with the humans. And of course, THE CATS! It was so fun! Some cats were frisky and some were napping but it was just so nice to be in a calm and warm environment that was brimming with love and acceptance. The cats are clearly very well cared for and loved. 10/10

Best place ever!!!! You get to hang out with cute cats and cool people all while enjoying a nice cup of coffee! Great atmosphere. It's nice knowing your money helps animals in needs and the animals are all up for adoption!

What an amazing place!  We were missing our cats back home and this gave us th fix that we needed.  The cats were so friendly and we quickly bonded with many of them.  Staff was extremely nice and was happy to answer any questions we had.  Would come back again!

My boyfriend and I were visiting for the weekend and we missed our kitties at home. We saw a card for cat therapy in our hotel's littler card menagerie and decided to check them out! We got there when they opened at 11 AM on a Saturday and were luckily able to fill the last 2 slots for that hour. We paid $14 each because it was a Saturday, but prices vary by day. I recommend booking ahead to guarantee a spot, because we saw multiple groups turned away after. It was quiet and clean with kitties galore, lounging, playing, snoozing, hiding. They were all well behaved and so precious. I love that they adopt all these cats out, but I also think it's a great concept for people who can't have pets to go snuggle for an hour. I think it's a great way to socialize these kitties before they find their forever home! Thanks, Cat Therapy!

Nice place! I was able to show up, get my cat fix and help out a good cause.


You might even be able take one home!

If you love cats as much as I do, you'll LOVE this place. We were greeted by a nice staff member who told us information about all the cats! There were many cats and they all had there own personality. 

They give you treats for the cats so you can get yo know each one. If you are looking to adopt a cat, this would be the perfect place to do it. 5 stars!
We absolutely loved our visit. My kids had so much fun with all the cats and will be back again. The staff was amazing and super helpful.
They were super friendly and the cats were adorable. A great way to spend an afternoon. The coffee was also really good. Definitely worth stopping by

Such a amazing find down a little walk way off of state street by McDonald's. If you can make reservations. You get a hour to play with lots of cats and kittens with all unique personalities. They adopt. It's really great therapy. Made my happy and helped with fibro.

I will never go back to this cat cafe- 
1.) it seems as though the cats there aren't the best to have in a place that advertises to people to pet and hangout with them- I reached out to lightly pet a cat on the head, and without notice, it attacked me and made me bleed. I've had cats my entire life and I was never in a situation like that before. There was also another cat that I suppose was new there and it was determined to start a fight with another cat by growling at it in the corner. I don't believe it is safe to come to this place, especially if you have a young child. 
2.) There is also a hefty price to get in that is questionable as to how much of it is actually donated to the animals.

Congratulations Santa Barbara, we finally have something that you usually only find in a metropolis, a cat cafe.  I have been here 2 times before, but yesterday was special.  For some reason, almost all the cats there were kittens.  Kittens!  A pair of black and white kittens by the name of Thor and Loki were the most active kittens.  As their names imply, they horsed around with each other nonstop.  I was partial to the 6 week old tabbies because my cat is a tabby too.  Too small to run around the room and confined to a cage with their litter maids.  They meowed in a high pitch voice that make your heart melt.  I wish the cat cafe many years of success in helping cats and people.

As a cat lover, I was STOKED to learn about a cat cafe coming to Santa Barbara since I'd always heard of them but never been. I followed on Instagram and always had severe FOMO when scrolling through my feed of adorable kittens. My boyfriend (who has a severe cat allergy) popped some Zyrtec took me here for my birthday. He's not a cat person but even he had fun. The space is really modern and cozy and you can order drinks which the staff will deliver to you from a nearby cafe. They offer tons of special events like cat yoga, studying with cats, cat wine  nights, kitten shower parties, and more. We met the owner, Catalina, who was photographing some kitties for IG and she was super sweet and shared her amazing story of how Cat Therapy came to be. Her creative vision has been executed so well and really come to life. We got to play with the kitties for 75 minutes which was plenty of time to feed them and take pictures and just hang out. A lot of cats were sleeping which is to be expected since they are nocturnal animals, but there were still many eager to play.

A few months later, I ended up winning free cat yoga passes for two from an IG contest and got to return for yoga with cats! This was so relaxing and fun and we got some kitty play time after. I love supporting this business because of the mission and work they do for cats. If you're a cat person, visit. If you're not a cat person, visit. You just might fall in love.
Lots of kitties!  Great work that they're doing here, come play with adorable cats and maybe take one home.

There is an entrance fee of $12 to pet the cats for 75 minutes and there is also a student discount available. However, I was not told that there is also an option to pay half price for half the time. I heard the employees tell another customer about the option, so I asked for a $5 refund since I was only staying for 20 minutes. They would not give me a refund even though they didn't give me the option in the first place. Also, they don't actually make coffee in the shop, they order it from a different place and pick it up for you.

I came here because I'm a huge cat lover. They advertise that they have over 15 cats- however they did not. They had about 8 though (or so it seemed). It is not very clean or sanitary in there. There are lots of water bowls out but no food- and it made me cringe a little b/c cats appear very frail, thin and malnourished. I felt sad in there. They should give away silver dollar size of dry cat food to every one that goes in - the cats are very active and they need fuel to keep up with their guests!

Just like the Cat Cafe in LA, Cat Therapy is a place where hoomans can come to relax, have some coffee, smoothies, or juice. The funds they make go towards taking care, and helping the cats find their Furever homes, it's on upper State St behind McDonald's, it's a very relaxing place, the staff is really great and friendly. If your ever need a place to relax and play with cats, come here and chill and adopt a cat!

Each week my work team does a 'Feed Your Feelings Friday', and this week we spent it at the Cat Therapy Cafe. It was the best group session we've ever had: so peaceful and fun, loving and nourishing for the spirit. The cats are amazing and wonderful, and the staff takes great care of them. It was reflective, calming, and thoroughly enjoyable. We will be back!

I loved this place!!!!
It really is therapy. I am not really a cat person but I love all animals the same. I saw a lot of reviews about cats attacking/scratching people, unfortunately that's something that comes with being around cats they scratch. They have colored collars on the cats to warn you of those behaviors/traits of some of the cats. 
I enjoyed this place very much and really love that they rescue animals that are in desperate need of help. They adopt so many cats out of this place its amazing. Definitely recommend this place to anyone cat lover or not you will have a great time and get to be around such cute little ones.

We lost our own cat to a sudden tragic accident a few weeks ago.  Although we are not feeling ready to adopt yet, being around kitties was incredibly therapeutic.  Unlike local shelters, these kitties are out in the open and able to roam, sit on our laps, get brushings, and try to sneak treats from everyone.  The employees and owners are really personable and their altruism is evident in their obvious concern for the 12-15 cats they always have up for adoption.  They don't pack the room with people in order to allow the cats to feel THEY are in control :)  It is worth the nominal fee to sit with these animals and leave feeling more balanced.  It's easy to chat with others in there if you are up for that as well, or just sit and have a cat on your lap and be quiet.

An added bonus is that they support another local business, Brasil Arts Cafe, across the street by allowing customers to order light items for delivery.  I hope this locally-owned business thrives and people take a cat home.

I came here last week and while the concept of a cat cafe is cool, the cafe itself was not. The staff is super welcoming and friendly but I think there was something wrong with many of the cats. A lot of them were sneezing and some had snot coming out of their noses. This makes me believe they were sick and that's pretty gross. I left half and hour early.

We absolutely loved our visit here! My girlfriend has always wanted to go to a cat cafe, so I found this spot to take her to. We called ahead of time and made a reservation to visit after we finished having some coffee down the street. We had an hour to sit and play with the cats. A lot of them were taking naps, but we still got the chance to interact with plenty of cats, all ages and sizes! 
I have a cat allergy and thankfully it didn't act up. I attribute that to the staff keeping the room and the cats clean, which I really appreciate! 
Thank you for a great experience!
Great idea and for a great cause.   Came by to pet a few furry friends.  Did not disappoint:)

The best place to visit if you are in need of good vibes and energetic. Thanks for great time with lovely kitties. Love such places! ))) Wish lots of people visit your place and adopt those sweet kitties)))
The cats are cute and it has good vibes. If I come back to Santa Barbara I would go again.

This was absolutely amazing. Came here during dead week for their Study with Cats offer, $15 for three hours!! OF COURSE, MINIMAL STUDY WAS DONE THAT DAY LOL. The cats are all so cute and friendly and my friend and I really wanted to leave with some of them ))': they kept sitting on our books and laps and laptops and in boxes cuz IF THEY FITS THEY SITS~ 

I would really really recommend everyone who isn't allergic to cats to visit this amazing place and adopt those sweet and playful cats. You can spend some time and see what lovely cat chooses you to be their hooman I really wish I could adopt one but my status as a "dorming" college student doesn't allow it. They have a lot of toys that you can utilize to play with the cats, and also give you treats to feed them. There's also a keurig for your coffee and tea needs. Looking forward to my next visit here!!

10/10 would recommend :')

they promised they would do a refund for us but forgot about it for 2 weeks until we reached out and still didn't ask our card info and blaming it on one of our friends for not telling the info but they didn't even bother to reach out to get it themselves because card info isn't something we can tell each other (privacy issues). 

Also got aggressive towards my friend for writing a bad review and called her a liar and made her delete the post on yelp..

when I was interested in adopting one of the staff showed an assumption that I was a college student, asking for my parents signature as well as making up stories I never even mentioned inlcuding saying: "didn't you say you're moving in your parent's place after graduation? That's why we need your parent's signature." When I am legally an adult (21) I didn't understand why she was showing such bias.

right after the adopting agency refused to let me adopt a cat, the cat therapy posted a picture of the exact cat on their social media. It felt bittersweet because I got rejected after being called an 'irresponsible college student' as well as being told to 'find another kitty in a shelter because they don't care who it goes to' and then being hung up on..   cat therapy posting the picture was no good.

A room full of kitties looking for a furrever home.  It was fun to hang out with them while we were away from our kitty at home. This is not a  "Cat Cafe" where you are served food and beverages...state laws prohibit that. It's a fun place to chill with cats of all ages, sizes, and personalities.

I hate to say anything negative about a place trying to get homeless cats adopted BUT their new policy of pretty much only allowing the 1 year and younger cats to go as "bonded pairs" is a misplaced understanding of cats in general. Most if not all adapt to being a single cat once adopted. In addition it was pretty clear when I went to adopt one cat that the "bonded" cat I would also need to take home was nothing more than a cat my desired cat had taken a liking to a few days prior. There was another family there at the same time and they left without a cat for the same reason, they only wanted to adopt one cat. This mentality will preclude a lot of cats from being adopted at a younger age when they are more likely to find homes. Whether it is the owner of Cat Therapy or the organization they are affiliated with making this policy, they are precluding lots of adoptions.

I actually already left my positive review but I was surprised at Kirby B's concerns that the cats were sick. I was there around the same time and I didn't notice this. I had also been there a few weeks before and it was the same cats who seemed fine then also.

Kittens are adorable and the folks who work there love their jobs. Who wouldn't? Only downside is when some people selfishly monopolize the cats and it's sometimes frustrating. Nevertheless even just watching them is a treat and it's for a good cause benefiting the rescue agency giving them a safe place to be until they can get their forever homes.

Five purr-fect stars for this organization. Doing their best for our feline friends. Comfortable, and clean without that cat aroma! Problem is you want to take all of the Kitties home. If you want to relax your mind, put this on your itinerary.

The cats are awesome. 5 stars would pet again.

The business model is not -- it is super-expensive just to get in, and by no means is this a "cat cafe". There is no cafe here. You are shown a menu of drinks & things upon entry and invited to purchase up front, but you are not told that someone then has to go out onto neighboring State St. and actually go to a real cafe and buy then bring these things to you. 20 minutes later. Want more sugar? more cream? got the wrong drink? Too bad!

I felt this was really deceptive and had I known I'd have just BYOC.

Amazing time here!! My gf surprised me with a visit for my birthday and we had such a great time. Sarah was so informative and knowledgeable on all the cats! I love the concept of saving them from high kill shelters and giving them such a cute and comfortable place to live until theyre adopted! 10 star!

If your SB Date game is getting dry and your partners tired of the same cycle of going to the pier, Mission, museum, retail therapy, every local taco spot, here's a new option for you! There was a holiday promotion for discounted admission if you bought $10 worth of cat merchandise so we got cat treats and a small toy. Otherwise I believe it was around $24 for two adults. I've been to a few animal cafes and this is kind of the average price, actually cheaper than some. There are birthday, student discounts, etc. if you're not here for the holidays so take advantage and keep your IDs on you. If there aren't a lot of people in the cafe, you can do a walk-in visit, otherwise you can book an appointment online for a 75 min. session. They have drinks from an external cafe but they're really expensive. 

I'm not much of a cat person, but my boyfriend is, so I popped an Allegra and made my way over here! This place is clean, bright, open and probably decked out in casual decor I see at Ross, but never manage to get besides this rug I recognized and had to get rid of because it shed so much. But it's ok here, because it blends in with the cat fur. There's cubbies for your bags and you can bring cameras as long as it's not flash. My SLR shutter kinda startled some cats in the moment, but it wasn't a big deal.

They give you a small bag of kibble upon arrival, and that's how you maintain your short relationship until the cats ditch you for someone else's kibble so don't become attached. That's not the cafe's fault, that's just cats being themselves. Some are nice, some are just straight up asleep, 1-2 might be kinda.. territorial. (Theyll eat food off your hand, but if you think that means friendship, that's your fault.) All the cats are pretty cute and they're from the local rescue so they are adoptable. It's a good cause. I had a good time pretending to like cats.
Awesome place. You get to hang out with and play with cats as long as your heart desires. Can't beat that!

Sad... What happened to this place? My daughter was so excited to go to Cat Therapy with me yesterday.  When we arrived, there were way too many people in the small space and too few cats.  It smelled very bad.  The receptionist was not friendly.  We decided to do something else instead. Too bad!

This is a wonderful environment for the cats to interact with humans and be adopted. It's much better than a traditional shelter where the cats are in cages. I would definitely go again. And the staff was really nice. Cats not always cooperative, but whatever they're cats.
Loved my time with these cats. I came here for my 30th birthday and loved every minute of it!
It was so relaxing being here. The staff are extremely friendly and all of the cats are calm and social. I had a great time!
Cat heaven! Happy to support such a great mission right here in downtown Santa Barbara.

I'm SO glad my friend and I wandered in here a few weeks back! We were exploring downtown and I had such a great experience overall.

Typically, you're supposed to book an appointment slot (for the sake of COVID and avoiding overwhelming the cats) but when we went, there was nobody there for the coming hour or so. The staff was just one girl working, but she was so sweet and helped us out with payment and showing us around! You're supposed to sanitize and then take shoes off before going in to the play area with the cats, which I appreciated a lot. 

I recently adopted a cat myself and now I understand that cats really do spend most of their time sleeping. A lot of the cats were dozing off, but there were a few playful ones who were active and interacting with us. There are a TON of toys available for us to use with the cats there and it was such a fun and unique experience on State Street! 

I can't remember the exact pricing, but it wasn't too expensive - it was definitely worth spending the hour with these adorable cats :)

My first cat cafe visit! Highly recommended. $12/hour. Free tea and coffee. A dozen cats of different ages and breeds. Ask for food to give them and the cats to nuts. The kittens are adorable. Definitely a unique experience to take your friends or family to. Would return for sure.

Logistics: Cat Therapy is clean, cute and chic. Cat Therapy is located off State St near Scarlett Begonia and offers tea & coffee from Brasil Arts Cafe. The cost is $12 for 75 minutes. You have the option of sitting on big pillows with the cats or enjoying your coffee at a table. In the middle, they have a big basket of toys for you to entice the playful cats. Each cat has a collar indicating boy, girl, shy and adopted. 

Impression: All the cats are rescued and available for adoption. Something that struck me is many of the cats are disorientated when they arrive to Cat Therapy but with time show more of their personality, which is great for perspective adopters to know the true personality of the cat. If you are looking to adopt a cat, I would 100% recommend you come here and interact with the cats to find your kitten match. 

I would also recommend this spot for locals who are in need of some pet therapy and a good cup of coffee. I could easily see myself picking up some cupcakes from SB Public Market and pairing it with coffee at Cat Therapy for a relaxing and delicious night.
